# NovaTrail decision log

> Why the platform is built the way it is. Each entry says what was decided, why, what was rejected and where it is described.
>
> **Rule:** do not re-propose what was rejected without new facts. If a decision has to change, ask the author and update this file. An entry is never rewritten: an amendment with its date at the end of the entry corrects it, or a new entry replaces it, and the old one stays where it is, marked "Superseded".
>
> Entries R01–R14 were made 2026-10-18, when the platform was founded. They rest on three grounds:
> - the author's answers of that day and his dialogue with Gemini about the platform (not in the repository; the arguments we rely on are retold here);
> - MathTrail's decisions that carry over here;
> - the plan of these documents, which the author approved 2026-10-18.
>

## Scope and product

**R01. NovaTrail is a universal platform for any subject and any age, and the successor of MathTrail; MathTrail is frozen, and we carry over from it selectively.** The project is the same, the organization is new — `altnovatrail`. MathTrail's repositories are no longer developed: their decisions, code and content are a source from which we take what we need (repositories 7). — *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-18.
- MathTrail's mechanics — AI reads, a program decides, the tutor asks — were meant to be independent of the subject (R37 canvas-api).
- Being tailored to olympiad maths for grades 1–6 shut out the other subjects and ages.
- MathTrail cannot be carried over as it is: canvas-api is a monolith, and NovaTrail is split into repositories from day one (R10).

— *Rejected:* developing MathTrail further and generalizing later; keeping MathTrail as a separate product beside the platform; finishing epic E2 of canvas-api and only then moving. — product 2.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* "MathTrail's repositories are no longer developed" is not true of standalone: it changed after 2026-10-18 too. R309 and R310 standalone added 102 tasks of grades 5–6 and replaced eight calendar tasks of grades 1–2 (2026-10-25 and 2026-10-26), and R316–R322 standalone settled the tasks that are solved from a picture: 48 more reference tasks and two topics wait for T105.10 and T105.11 standalone (commit 89986bc, 2026-11-01). So MathTrail's content is carried over from a pinned commit: olympiad maths — from standalone at 89986bc (R05 modules), and what standalone adds after it enters the module only by a new decision of `modules`. The documents of `spec` name the numbers of standalone's content together with the commit. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `modules` В10 (RUN.md `modules`, `main` 67bc6d1). — product 2, 10; repositories 6, 7; COORDINATION.md, row 3.7; RUN.md, Д84.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **the new decision of `modules` that the 2026-11-02 amendment waited for is the 2026-11-08 amendment to R05 modules: the rest of the port takes standalone at commit 42b4408 of 2026-11-07, and the first batch stays at 89986bc.** At 42b4408 standalone has 19 topics and 753 reference tasks: 705 written in words and 48 that are solved from a picture (R316–R322 standalone), — 30 in two new topics, `counting.figures` and `geometry.cubes_paper`, and 18 in five earlier ones, — and there are 39 templates with solvers, six of them new and also reading the picture (`content/examples/`, `content/solvers/` and SPEC 1.6 standalone at 42b4408, read 2026-11-08). Epic E3 of `modules` carries over 726 tasks — all but the 27 of the first batch. The documents of `spec` name the numbers together with the commit: 89986bc is the commit of the first batch, 42b4408 — of the rest of the port. "its 705 solvers" in the [format text](../format/README.md), section 24, is a measurement of the solvers' steps at 89986bc, not an inventory, and stays as it is. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `modules` В24 (RUN.md `modules`, branch `e3`, commit ac445f4), by the recommendation of `modules`, with the triage's refinements: repositories 7 names 19 topics, and О-10 — the same rule about the wording of the 48 new tasks. — product 2, 10, 13.2 and 14; repositories 6, 7; architecture 3.10; COORDINATION.md, row 3.7 and «Первое приложение»; RUN.md, Д118.

**R02. A subject is a module: data, not core code and not instructions to a model.** A module gives a skill graph, lessons, tasks, trap and technique catalogs, solving steps, canvas settings, media files, an eval set and, if needed, widgets.
- The core knows no subject.
- A new canvas kind or check kind is platform code, shared by all modules; a module chooses it and sets its parameters.
- Prompts belong to the platform: one per AI capability, each with its own eval set. A module's free text reaches the model only as a separate marked block of data, like the notes about the child in standalone (R16 standalone).
- A module's eval set is synthetic samples or samples that adult volunteers and authors made for the eval; there is no learners' work in a module (concepts 3).
- The platform's prompts and the make-up of the eval set are a proposal of the plan.

— *Why:*
- «Движок под каждый предмет и каждую форму записи — тупик поддержки» ("An engine for each subject and each form of writing is a dead end of maintenance") (R37 canvas-api).
- Data are checked by a schema and versioned. Instructions to the model from third-party authors are a channel for injections and unpredictable behaviour, and the platform promises the same result on the same input (R03).
- The author wanted modules «наподобие навыков Claude, только продвинутее и детерминированнее» ("like Claude's skills, only more advanced and more deterministic"). Determinism is what giving up instructions in favour of data gives.

— *Rejected:*
- a module as a set of prompts, after the pattern of a Claude skill;
- a subject's code in the core;
- a subject as "tasks, a prompt and an eval set" (R37 canvas-api): the module's prompt is replaced by its fields.

— concepts 3, 9, 10; product 1.

**R03. The core is deterministic, perception is probabilistic.**
- Whether an answer is correct is decided by a program, by the task's key or predicate.
- The next lesson or task is chosen by the engine, by a rule.
- The learner model is computed by code.
- AI only reads the learner's work, turning it into an observation, and chooses the words.

The same module of the same version and the same state of the learner give the same choice and the same verdict on the same observation; randomness comes only from the seed. — *Why:* MathTrail Canvas (canvas-api: R37, R38) and standalone are built the same way: "Ratings are computed by code, never by the model". Reproducibility is needed for the trust of the learner and the adult, for debugging and for the learner simulator. — *Rejected:*
- the model itself decides whether an answer is correct: it may call a correct answer incorrect, and the key will not catch it (R37 canvas-api);
- the model chooses the next task.

— concepts 9, 11, 12.

**R04. A false alarm is worse than no check; no deterministic check — no verdict.**
- A doubt about a reading is a request to rewrite or circle, not "not yet". A failure of AI or an exhausted limit is a neutral phrase.
- A verdict is given only where there is a key or a predicate that a program checks.
- An assessment by a rubric — a drawing, pronunciation, an essay — is feedback, not a verdict.
- The provenance of the key and of the tags decides whether a verdict is possible and how much the evidence weighs. A task from paper without a verified key gets no verdict and does not move the rating.

— *Why:*
- As R38 canvas-api and product 5.6 canvas-api: «Ложная ошибка хуже, чем отсутствие проверки» ("A false mistake is worse than no check").
- For subjects without a key it is the only honest way: a verdict of the model by a rubric would be its opinion in the guise of an assessment.
- Provenance is what holds R03 when photos, rubrics and widgets appear.

— *Rejected:*
- a verdict of the model where there is no key;
- the rule "no key — no verdict" in its narrow form: a predicate check has no single key, and yet it has a verdict.

— concepts 9; product 7.

**R05. The tutor does not name the answer itself and does not touch the learner's work; the learner sees what was read.**
- A hint is one short question about a place in the learner's work: the Socratic method.
- The task's key does not go to the learner's device until the task is solved: the app gets the task's open view, without the key, the solution and the traps.
- The tutor writes only on its own canvas layer: frames, marks and a sketch do not change or cover the learner's writing.
- After the check the learner sees what AI read: «Я прочитал 6» ("I read" and the number).

— *Why:* this is how MathTrail Canvas is built: canvas-api: R39, R43; product 5.4 and 8 canvas-api; the task's open view without the answer — spec 8.6 canvas-api. — *Consequence:* the keys of open modules are public, as the modules themselves are. The rule guards no secret; it only keeps the key out of the learner's app. — *Open:* whether to show the solution at the learner's request (О-7). — concepts 6, 8, 10; product 7; repositories 4.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **О-7 is solved — R82.** The task's key and solution go to the device when the attempt is closed by a correct answer or by the solution shown: "until the task is solved" above reads "until the attempt is closed by either of them". An attempt that the learner left, that they abandoned or that was closed "unchecked" gives no key. The item "Open" is answered by this. — R82; concepts 6 and 15.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-02:* **a task with a rubric is solved when its attempt is closed by the learner's "Done"** (R87). Then its criteria and its solution, if the task has one, go to the device, and the lesson's segment with it ends. "Left", "abandoned", "unchecked" and "not suitable" do not open it, as a left attempt of a task with a key gives no key. The list of criteria with marks does not go to the learner: they see feedback, not an assessment (concepts 9.1). The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В19 (RUN.md `api`, `main` d896943), by its recommendation. — R87; concepts 6, 9.2 and 15; [format text](../format/README.md), section 21; RUN.md, Д83.

— *Third amendment 2026-11-02:* **the example «Я прочитал 6» above reads «Прочитано: 6» ("Read:" and the number).** The learner sees what was read in a line of `app`, and in it AI does not speak of itself in the first person, and the line has no grammatical gender: «Я прочитал» ("I read") is the masculine gender and a person where AI reads (R10 app; П-15). product 7, concepts 9.1 and the diagram of architecture 4.1 now write it the same way. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В32 (RUN.md `app`, `main` 375a09b). — R91; R10 app.

**R06. A learner is of any age. A child learns under an adult's account, an adult under their own. The learner's age is given by the account owner, and the platform stores not the date of birth but the age category.**
- The age category decides the rights, the consent and the AI routes: under 13; from 13 to the country's age of digital consent; from it to 18; 18 and over. So the country is given together with the age.
- The presentation style decides how the platform speaks and shows.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-18: the project is now not only for children, adults will be able to learn too — for example, Spanish; the learner's age is given by the user. The categories with the country and the refusal to store the age are a proposal of the plan. The category is enough for every rule: its boundaries are 13 years, the country's age of digital consent and 18, and these are the thresholds both of consent and of the AI providers' terms. The date of birth and the age in years are superfluous personal data. — *Rejected:* only children and their parents, as in MathTrail (R06 canvas-api); storing the date of birth or the age in years; "13–15" as one category — it does not express the country's age of consent. — *Open:* a teenager's account (П-13); how to confirm that the account owner is an adult (П-6). — concepts 13; privacy 3.

**R07. AI comes through several AI providers and by two routes: platform AI by subscription or one's own key for free. The providers' rules about age are kept; a model is admitted only after an eval.**
- The providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others — are connected through ports, as in canvas-api.
- An own key is the key of the learner or of the account owner; with it the platform is free.
- A learner's data do not go to a provider whose terms forbid their age category.
- Each AI capability has its own list of exact model IDs that passed the eval. An own key does not open a model without an eval.

— *Why:* two routes, several providers and keeping their age rules — the author's decision of 2026-10-18. An own key makes the platform free, a subscription makes it convenient, and several providers remove the dependence on one. Admitting models by an eval is a proposal of the plan, after the pattern of R22 canvas-api: a change of model passes the eval sets. — *Rejected:* one provider — Gemini on Vertex AI, as in canvas-api; any model of the user's choice — by the plan: a weak model would read the work with false alarms. — *Consequence:* the reconciliation of the terms of 2026-10-18 (privacy 5.3) showed that the Gemini API in its AI Studio variant does not suit a platform open to children on any route, and an own OpenAI key does not suit a learner under 13 or under the age of digital consent of their country. — *Open:* for whom an own key is (О-4, П-4); a free route for children (О-5); where to keep the key (Т-9). — product 6; concepts 14; privacy 5.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **"An own key is the key of the learner or of the account owner" above reads so: an own key is the key of an account owner who learns themselves, whose profile has the category `adult`** (R84; R08 app). An account without a profile of an owner who learns connects no key: the key is needed by whoever learns themselves. For whom else it is — still О-4 and П-4. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В39 (RUN.md `app`, `main` 375a09b), by its recommendation: with the former words the vocabulary would promise a key to an owner who does not learn themselves, and this key would be used only by children, to whom an own key is closed (О-4). Rejected: keeping "the key of the learner or of the account owner". — R84; R08 app; product 6; concepts 14 and 15.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **a model is admitted only by a runner's report whose verdicts `module-kit` gave, as in the platform's work; a report with the verdicts of the runner's own code is a measurement, not an admission** ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 14; R95). The admission rule — the bounds, the thresholds, the repeats — is still `tutor`'s. The author's answer while T60 was planned (RUN.md), by the plan's recommendation. — *Rejected:* the admission rule of `tutor` decides which code is fit for admission.

**R08. The first slice is two dissimilar modules. Module format v1 is fixed only after both have passed through the platform with no subject code in the core.** Module 1 is olympiad maths 1–6 from MathTrail; module 2 is unlike it, the recommendation is Spanish A1 for adults (О-1). — *Why:* two modules — the author's decision of 2026-10-18; when the format is fixed — a proposal of the plan. An abstraction without a second consumer bends to the first: "Introduce an abstraction when there is a second consumer" (CLAUDE.md canvas-api). — *Rejected:*
- only maths: the format would be universal only on paper;
- a specification first, without an app.

— product 10.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* О-1 is solved — R41. There are three modules in the first slice: olympiad maths 1–6, school maths of grade 3 on a workbook, and short essays in English for any age. There are still two subjects — maths and writing —, and "both" above reads "all three": format v1 is fixed when all three modules have passed through the platform with no subject code in the core.

**R09. Data are kept to a minimum, and they belong to the learner or the family.**
- The learner model and the learner's work can be exported in an open format and deleted in one step.
- Strokes with time and pressure stay on the device. What goes to the check is a picture or a crop, which the server does not store.
- Logs carry no direct identifiers, no work, nothing read and no text of hints.

— *Why:* as privacy 1 canvas-api and the family's profile file in standalone. — *Open:* where the learner model lives (П-7). — privacy 1, 4.

— *Amendment 2026-11-10:* **the open format of the export is [the part `export/`](../export/README.md): a ZIP of JSON files, and what the platform holds as protobuf bytes is the JSON of the same value with its `.proto` (R135).** The author's answer of 2026-11-10 while T101 was planned (RUN.md). Strokes with time and pressure still do not leave the device for the server: `app` puts them into the export from the device, into the owner's file.

## Structure

**R10. The platform is split into repositories from day one; `spec` is the shared source of truth.**
- Repositories of the organization altnovatrail, without a prefix: spec, cognitive-model, engine, sim, canvas-api, canvas-shell, map-ui, module-registry, dataset-pipeline, module-template-ui and the repositories of the official modules.
- Libraries do not depend on services, services do not depend on each other at build time, there are no cycles.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-18, following the dialogue with Gemini. A narrow context for AI agents and independent releases. Modules and widgets are written by third-party authors, so the format must live apart from the code. — *Rejected:* a monolith, like canvas-api; the client and the API in one repository, like R13 canvas-api. Versioned contracts in `spec` remove the argument of R13 canvas-api («API и клиент меняются вместе, одним pull request» — "the API and the client change together, in one pull request"); the price is several pull requests instead of one. The dependency rules are a proposal of the plan. — *Open:* the order of appearance and the refinement of the list (Т-1 — Т-6). — repositories 1, 2, 6.

— *Amendment 2026-10-18:* the make-up and the names of the repositories are replaced by R18. The dependency rules are in force; checking the libraries by the simulator in CI is not a dependency at build time (repositories 1). Т-1 — Т-6 are closed (R16–R18).

**R11. The technology base is as in MathTrail Canvas.**
- Go — for services and libraries.
- Cloud Run and managed services that scale to zero, with no clusters or queues of our own.
- API contracts — protobuf and buf.
- Terraform; GitHub Actions with signed releases.
- Development — only in the devcontainer; only exact versions.

The rest each repository decides in its own documents: storage, sign-in, access rights, realtime. In canvas-api these were Neon, Firebase, OpenFGA and Centrifugo. The differences from canvas-api are several AI providers (R07) and several repositories (R10). — *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-18: the technologies and the architecture will be partly or almost wholly the same as in canvas-api. This base already works. standalone lives in prod on Cloud Run. Its skeleton, CI/CD and Terraform were carried over into canvas-api (R11 canvas-api), and canvas-api checked the deployment of a signed release and the rollback in prod on 2026-10-14 (self-hosting canvas-api). — *Rejected:* k8s and EDA at once: MathTrail's platform on them remained a vision (R01 canvas-api). — repositories 1.

— *Amendment 2026-10-19:* this decision closes Т-7 in its part about the API — API contracts on protobuf and buf. What stays open in it is the module format (RUN.md, В12).

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* Т-7 is closed in its part about the module format too — R45: the module format is JSON Schema 2020-12, and the API contracts stay on protobuf and buf. "What stays open in it is the module format" in the amendment above is no longer so.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* how the API contracts are written — where they lie, by which rules of buf, of which version and which code comes out of them —, and what `app` and `api` speak, R83 decided: proto3 files in `contracts/`, the generated code — from the releases of `spec`, the transport — Connect. The rest each repository still decides. — R83; RUN.md, T54.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **the infrastructure is described by OpenTofu, the open fork of Terraform, at an exact version: the code in HCL after the pattern of `infra/` of canvas-api, and the tool and the commands — `tofu`. Read the line "Terraform" above so. OpenTofu goes into the `toolchain` stage of the devcontainer of `infra` by an `ARG` of its version and the sha256 sums of the publisher's archives (R34) — as a named exception of the license, MPL 2.0, in the decision of `infra` that brings it in (R12). Т-29 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-08 to the row «в реестр spec» `infra` В10 (RUN.md `infra`, `main` e56c8bc) — an inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, option (a), by the recommendation of the row and of Т-29. The facts of the row were checked by the triage on GitHub on 2026-11-08: the latest release of [OpenTofu](https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/releases/tag/v1.13.9) is v1.13.9 of 2026-11-05, the repository's license is MPL-2.0, and among the release's files are `tofu_1.13.9_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, `tofu_1.13.9_linux_arm64.tar.gz` and `tofu_1.13.9_SHA256SUMS`; the latest release of [Terraform](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/releases/tag/v1.17.1) is v1.17.1 of 2026-10-28, under the Business Source License 1.1 (Т-29).
- The providers `hashicorp/google` and `hashicorp/google-beta` are in the OpenTofu registry under MPL 2.0, and `tofu test` holds `mock_provider`, `override_resource` and `command = plan`, on which the tests of canvas-api stand (architecture 4 infra): the code and the tests carry over. What changes against canvas-api: the providers come from the OpenTofu registry, and the sums of `.terraform.lock.hcl` are its; the tool is in `toolchain`, not on the runner, and CI calls it through `spec/tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` (R30).
- This does not change the 2026-10-22 amendment to R12, where Terraform is named as an example: it is about the rule, not the choice.

**R12. The license of the code is Apache-2.0.** — *Why:* the author's decision. Apache-2.0 is approved by OSI and suits grants that require open and free software. Unlike MIT, it explicitly grants a license to the contributors' patents (section 3 of the license). — *Rejected:* MIT, as in MathTrail; CC0 for the specifications. — *Consequence:*
- dependencies — only with licenses compatible with Apache-2.0; the license check from canvas-api (R48 canvas-api) is to be rewritten for this list;
- MathTrail's code under MIT carries over freely: MIT is compatible with Apache-2.0, and the MIT notice is kept.

— *Open:* the license of the modules' content (О-10). — product 9.

— *Amendment 2026-10-19:* Apache-2.0 — for the documents and for the content of the official modules too (R20).

— *Amendment 2026-10-19:* the rule "only compatible with Apache-2.0" is about what enters NovaTrail's code and packages and leaves together with them.
- Compatible means category A of the ASF policy: "we consider the following licenses to be similar in terms to the Apache License 2.0" ([ASF 3rd Party License Policy](https://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html), read 2026-10-19).
- A development or CI tool that never ships — the documents check, a code analyser — may also be under another OSI-approved license or under free terms for open source. Such a tool is always named: a package of the lock file — as an exception in the license check, with the reason; a service or an action — in the decision that brings it in.
- Now these are `elkjs` under EPL-2.0 inside `mermaid` of `docs-check` (RUN.md, T01), and from R30 — SonarQube Cloud on the OSS plan, with its terms in R30, and CodeQL CLI. The terms of CodeQL CLI allow one to "Perform analysis on the Open Source Codebase", and ""Open Source Codebase" means a codebase that is released under an OSI-approved License" ([GitHub CodeQL Terms and Conditions](https://github.com/github/codeql-cli-binaries/blob/main/LICENSE.md), read 2026-10-19).

*Why:* the author's decision on the question В4 (RUN.md, T15). Without the amendment the rule diverged from the lock file of `tools/`, and the license check in CI would not know the exception. *Rejected:* a record only in T01.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* how to read "free terms for open source" in the amendment above — the author's answer to В27 `canvas`. A development or CI tool that never ships may also be under terms free for everyone, not only for open source. Free terms — of both kinds — the rule accepts within two bounds:
- NovaTrail does not distribute the tool: it publishes no image or archive with it. The tool comes at build time — for `canvas` from the Playwright image pinned by tag and digest (R13 canvas) —, and the `toolchain` stage, where the checks run, is built on every run and is not published anywhere (R30);
- without it the platform can be built, run and deployed: it only checks it — runs the tests, reads the code.

Otherwise the rule is as before: the tool puts nothing of its own into what ships and is always named — as an exception in the license check or in the decision that brings it in. SonarQube Cloud and CodeQL CLI fit within the bounds: NovaTrail does not distribute them, and the platform is built, run and deployed without them. The first tool on terms for everyone is Chrome Headless Shell in the `toolchain` stage of `canvas`, a build of Google Chrome for Testing (R13 canvas).

*Why:* the recommendation of `canvas` in В27, with the bounds the executor proposed. Everything read 2026-10-22.
- The browser on which Playwright runs the tests is no longer Chromium under BSD-3-Clause. Since version 1.57 "Playwright now runs on Chrome for Testing builds rather than Chromium. Headed mode uses `chrome`; headless mode uses `chrome-headless-shell`", and since 1.63 on arm64 too: "On Linux arm64, Playwright now downloads the Chrome for Testing build of Chromium, the same build used on all other platforms" ([Playwright, release notes](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/docs/src/release-notes-js.md), tag v1.64.1). It downloads them from `https://cdn.playwright.dev`, from `builds/cft/<version>/` (`packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts` at the same tag). In the browser's folder `ABOUT` says "Google Chrome … All rights reserved … See the Terms of Service at chrome://terms", and `LICENSE.headless_shell` lists the open licenses of its sources, and the first is the BSD-3-Clause of Chromium (R13 canvas).
- Chrome's terms are free for everyone, not only for open source. "By using Chrome or ChromeOS, you agree to the Google Terms of Service located at https://policies.google.com/terms and these Google Chrome and ChromeOS Additional Terms of Service", and they "apply to the executable code version of Chrome and ChromeOS" ([Google Chrome Additional Terms of Service](https://www.google.com/chrome/terms/), the edition "Last modified: 30 September, 2025"). The license to Google's software is "royalty-free, which means there are no monetary fees for this license" and "personal, which means it doesn't extend to anyone else" ([Google Terms of Service](https://policies.google.com/terms), the edition "Effective July 30, 2026").
- The first bound comes from the same terms: "You may not copy, modify, distribute, sell, or lease any part of our services or software" (Google Terms of Service). The second holds the argument of Т-29: Terraform under BUSL is needed to deploy the platform, and its terms would be accepted by everyone who deploys it themselves, while the terms of the test browser — only by whoever runs the tests. Terms for open source need it no less: whoever deploys the platform at home may well not be an open project themselves. The bounds for both kinds of terms are a proposal of the executor.

*Consequence:*
- The terms are accepted by whoever uses the browser. CI uses it on behalf of the organization, and its representative — the author — accepts the terms for it: "To use our services on behalf of an organization: an authorized representative of that organization must agree to these terms" (Google Terms of Service). A contributor who runs the tests in their own container accepts them themselves.
- The image of the `toolchain` stage in GHCR, to which R30 says to return when the build becomes long, is not published with such a browser: such an image is without it, or the rule is read anew.
- RULES.md, Licenses, says the same. `.github`, by its move to a tag, names the browser of the wrapper's contract as a build of Chrome for Testing on these terms — by an amendment to R19 .github and in architecture 3.1 .github —, and `app` and `skill-map` name their browser by a decision of their own (RUN.md, Д16). Т-29 is added to.

*Rejected:*
- «бесплатные для всех условия — тоже free terms» ("terms free for everyone are free terms too") without bounds, as in В27: by the letter Terraform under BUSL would pass this way too, which Т-29 does not recommend;
- only OSI licenses — tests in WebKit under LGPL-2.1 and BSD-2-Clause or in Firefox under MPL-2.0 from Playwright. The wrapper's contract and R13 canvas would change for the sake of a route nobody has tried: they have 52 and 25 system packages, Chromium has 21 (R13 canvas);
- Chromium from an open build, by a route of our own: since 1.63 Playwright downloads no such builds on any platform, and each repository would have a route of its own.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* npm is a development and CI tool under Artistic-2.0, and this exception is named here. The author's answer to В26 `.github`, by its recommendation.
- **Where npm comes from.** It comes with Node: the Node archive that `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` installs (R34) carries it in `lib/node_modules/npm`. So npm is in every NovaTrail devcontainer, in the `toolchain` stage too. It installs the packages of `tools/` of `spec`, by the recipe `_tools`, and the packages of the repositories in TypeScript, and the shared release of `.github` publishes with it (the amendment to R18 .github).
- **The license.** Node 24.21.0 of the Dockerfile has npm 11.19.0, and it has "The npm application / Copyright (c) npm, Inc. and Contributors / Licensed on the terms of The Artistic License 2.0", and in `package.json` — `"license": "Artistic-2.0"` ([npm/cli, LICENSE](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.0/LICENSE), tag v11.19.0; the same lines are in the devcontainer, in npm's folder). The license is approved by OSI: "Artistic License 2.0 — Artistic-2.0" is in its list ([OSI Approved Licenses](https://opensource.org/licenses)). It is not in category A of the ASF policy, nor in the list of `tools/licenses/config.mjs`.
- **Why it is a tool.** npm puts nothing of its own into what ships: it installs the packages from the lock file, and their licenses are checked by the license check (R39). `npm pack` builds an archive from the package's files, and publishing sends the finished archive (В26 `.github`). npm itself is not in the lock file: `tools/package-lock.json` does not have it.
- **The list** of the 2026-10-19 amendment — "Now these are `elkjs` … and CodeQL CLI" — gains npm. If an image or an archive that NovaTrail publishes carries Node together with its npm — for example, the image of a service on Node —, npm will begin to ship, and the rule is read anew.

*Why:* the recommendation of `.github` in В26 (RUN.md `.github`, commit 9b1ea42). RULES.md, Licenses, says to name a development tool under another license as an exception, and npm is in every devcontainer, and no decision of `spec` named it. `.github` itself named it only at home, for the publishing step (the amendment to R18 .github). One entry in `spec` closes this for all repositories. Everything read 2026-10-22.

*Rejected:*
- leaving it as it is — against RULES.md, Licenses;
- an exception in `tools/licenses/config.mjs`: npm is not in the lock file, and an exception that the lock file does not know the check counts as an error ("An exception that no longer matches the lock file is an error", ibid.).

*Consequence:* RULES.md needs no change. `.github` closes В26 by its move to a tag, and its amendment to R18 .github may refer to this one (RUN.md, Д24).

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **for a model that ships with the platform, the code, the weights and the data it was trained on are all compatible with Apache-2.0 — by the same category A of the ASF policy.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В28 (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its first option, by the recommendation of `tutor`.
- **Why not only the code.** A model also has weights and training data. The weights are derived from the data, and the terms of the data follow the weights. `tutor` found no open model of handwritten maths whose data are under such a license too (architecture 2.6 tutor, T44; the sources read by `tutor` 2026-10-25):
  - TexTeller is assembled, in its authors' words, from open sets. By the estimate of `tutor`, among them are MathWriting and CROHME under "Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike", 4.0 and 3.0;
  - Pix2Text-MFR does not name its data, and its initial weights are from TrOCR, and from which one is not said. The handwritten TrOCR was fine-tuned on IAM, and IAM is "for non-commercial research purpose only".

  For the ASF such licenses are category X: "You may NOT include the following licenses within Apache products: … Non-commercial licenses: … Creative Commons Non-Commercial variants" ([ASF 3rd Party License Policy](https://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html), read 2026-10-28).
- **What a model of our own is trained on** — on data the platform can release under its license: on the synthetic data of `tutor` and on the samples of adult volunteers. A volunteer's sample goes into training only if their consent names the training of a model that ships with the platform (П-16).
- **A local measurement** that ships nothing may take a model on other terms only by the author's decision, in a task of its own. Such a decision names the model, as the 2026-10-19 amendment names a development tool.

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. The rule is about what "enters NovaTrail's code and packages and leaves together with them" (the 2026-10-19 amendment), and a model on the device would leave together with the app. The condition about the volunteer's consent is a proposal of the executor. Without it a sample that a person gave for an eval would become training data of the shipped weights without their knowledge (privacy 1).

*Rejected:*
- category A only for the code and the weights: the terms of the data follow the weights derived from them;
- for a local measurement — any terms without the author's decision: such a measurement would imperceptibly become the basis of what ships.

*Consequence:* П-16 is added to (privacy 9); reading on the device — R66. `tutor` closes В28 by its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

## Components and repositories

**R15. The backend of the first slice is one service, `api`. Of the platform's parts, only it stores learners' data on the server, and everything that calls the models is the library `tutor`, in its own repository.**
- `api` — accounts, learners, consent, attempts, verdicts, the learner model, the choice, the hint ladder, the quotas. `api` chooses its storage itself (R11).
- `tutor` — the AI capabilities, the platform's prompts with their eval sets, the AI providers' adapters, the admitted models, the AI route and the admission by age category, the eval runner. It stores nothing; the types of its requests have no fields for the identifiers of the learner and the account.
- The CI of `api` checks the full list of dependencies: the AI providers' SDKs enter the build only through `tutor`.
- `tutor` will become a service, with the same types, when it gets a second consumer. The first such is `module-pipeline` at stage 4; decide then whether it is a library or a service for it.

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-18; the dependency check and the request types without identifiers are a proposal of the plan.
- R03 is held by the pure check function in `module-kit` and by the observation type without a verdict, not by a network hop.
- An own key and the picture of the work pass through `api` anyway.
- A repository of its own gives a narrow context and keeps the eval next to the prompts.

— *Rejected:*
- `tutor` as a separate service from day one: a second contract, IAM between the services and a second cold start on a child's check;
- a service for each area — accounts, sessions, check, tutor, payment. Without queues and a bus (R11) one attempt would pass through all the services in a synchronous chain, that is, a distributed monolith would result.

— *Consequence:* the AI providers' keys are read by the service account of `api`. Т-12 is closed: the eval protocol is in `spec`, the runner is in `tutor`, the learners' work is outside the repositories. — architecture 1, 3.5, 3.6.

**R16. The interface is assembled from packages at build time; at run time only the modules' widgets are loaded — in an iframe sandbox.**
- `canvas` and `skill-map` are in their own repositories, with their own releases; `app` assembles them at an exact version.
- A module's widget runs in an iframe without `allow-same-origin` on a separate registrable domain.
  - CSP does not let its code go to the network.
  - It speaks with the app only by the protocol from `spec`.
  - The bundle is signed and pinned by hash in the module package that is pinned to the attempt.
- Official widgets run in the same iframe sandbox as other people's. Children get only widgets that passed a review (О-9).

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-18. The design of the iframe sandbox — the attributes, CSP, the signature and the hash, one sandbox for official and other people's widgets, a review for children — is from the recommendation of Т-8 and a proposal of the plan.
- In the dialogue with Gemini the author wanted the parts of the interface to be «микрофронтенды в своих репозиториях» ("micro-frontends in their own repositories"). Packages give a separate repository with its own release too, without loading at run time.
- Loading our own parts at run time with exact versions is useless: `app` would pin the version anyway. And it would pay with version drift, duplicates of the framework, more complex CSP and offline.
- Shadow DOM is not a means of protection: it isolates styles, not code (architecture 8).

— *Rejected:*
- micro-frontends that are loaded at run time: web components by URL, Module Federation;
- `canvas` and `skill-map` as packages inside the repository `app`;
- the modules' web components right in the page through `<script src>`, as Gemini proposed.

— *Consequence:* Т-5 and Т-8 are closed. A second consumer of a package — the site, the MCP channel — gets a second build of it. — architecture 3.4, 6.

**R17. The semantics of the module format is held by one library, `module-kit`, with a CLI for authors. Registry v0 is a signed index: the CI of the repository `modules` builds it with the CLI of `module-kit`.**
- In `module-kit`:
  - reading and checking a module;
  - the package and the index;
  - templates with a seed and the open view;
  - the check kinds and normalization;
  - whether a verdict is allowed by provenance;
  - the leak check;
  - the solver in Starlark;
  - the check of the package's signature. The signature itself is put by the shared release workflow from `.github`.
- The registry service will appear at stage 4 and will also be built on `module-kit`.

— *Why:* a proposal of the plan the author approved 2026-10-18.
- The verdict depends on the code of the check kinds, and the check of the keys at publication depends on the same code. One owner of the semantics and one set of test vectors (Т-18) hold R03 through updates.
- While the format changes (R08), a change to it is one for all consumers: `api`, the author's CLI, the eval runner.

— *Rejected:* a library `checker` and a CLI validator in `module-registry` — the recommendations of Т-1 and Т-4. The two parts would change together, and the registry's CLI would become a second owner of the format. — *Consequence:* Т-1 and Т-4 are closed; at stages 1–3 the registry is not a service but signed files. — architecture 3.7, 3.10; repositories 4.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* what is inside a package and how its digest is computed, R62 decided: two parts — the canonical view for the server and the files for the device — and the package inventory, and the package digest is the digest of the inventory. What the index names and what it signs, RUN.md, T44 decides. — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* what the index names and what it signs, R63 decided: the cumulative index `module-index.json` in each release of `modules` names each published version of each module by its package digest, with the release tag, the anchor skills and the withdrawal mark. The index is signed as a release file, and whoever checked it trusts the packages by the chain of digests. What the signature checks — still T37. — R63; RUN.md, T44.

— *Amendment 2026-11-01:* what the signature checks, R77 decided. The item "the check of the package's signature" reads so: `module-kit` checks the package by the chain of digests from the index that the pull request of `api` pinned (R63), and the signature of the release file is checked by the recipe `release-verify` of `spec` where the file enters NovaTrail. The library `module-kit` checks no signatures: it does not go to the network. — R77; RUN.md, T37.

- RUN.md is in Russian, like the documents in `docs/` (R14) and as in canvas-api (R25 canvas-api).
- The RUN.md of `spec` plans the work in `spec` and what is done for the whole organization: setting up the repositories, the shared files, the normative parts of `spec`. A component's RUN.md plans its own work; its first epic is the detailing of the component by its card (architecture 3).

There such a plan led the epics E1 and E2: a task for one review does not grow, and the author sees each step. A RUN.md of its own in each repository and a first epic of detailing are the plan's proposal. — *Rejected:* tasks in GitHub Issues or Projects — the agent reads the plan from a file, and the same pull request as the documents edits it; one shared plan for all the repositories — it would mix the order of work of twelve repositories. — *Consequence:* R14 has an amendment on the language of RUN.md; the repository template carries its own RUN.md (repositories 2.2). — RUN.md; repositories 2.2.

Тело — `docs/plan/E10.md`». The license check and contributions follow one rule. — *Rejected:* CC BY 4.0 for the content of official modules — the former recommendation of О-10. — *Consequence:* R12 has an amendment; О-10 is narrowed to third-party modules and other people's task sets. — *Open:* which licenses the registry accepts from third-party authors and under which licenses other people's task sets are, MathNet included (О-10). — RUN.md; repositories 2.2.
