Only runs on `main` write to the scope of `main`: "When a cache is created by a workflow run triggered on a pull request, the cache is created for the merge ref (`refs/pull/.../merge`). Because of this, the cache will have a limited scope and can only be restored by re-runs of the pull request"; the limit is "10 GB per repository" ([GitHub Docs, Dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching), read 2026-11-09), and the entry of the image of `canvas` is about 575 MB. — *Rejected:* buildx with the cache `type=gha` — two actions `docker/*` instead of one, as R57 canvas rejected too; only retries of downloads — longer, each job still downloads everything, and a long failure brings the check down; the cache for the release too — the image of the job with the signing permission would be held by a cache entry and not by the Dockerfile, and a failed release is rerun; not caching. — *Consequence:* `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` and its tests, the `ci.yml` of `spec` — task T104; the shared workflows of `.github` — RUN.md, Д146; rows 1.13 and 2.4 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md). — R30, R34, R40; R57 canvas; R03–R05 .github.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-09:* **`toolchain.sh build` takes the image file from the environment variable `TOOLCHAIN_IMAGE_FILE` — a full path that the caller sets — not from an argument; empty or unset means building the stage, as before, and the releases do not set it. With the variable: the file is there — `docker load --quiet --input <file>` and `docker image inspect novatrail-toolchain`, and if both succeed, the file is deleted and there is no build; the file did not load or gave no image — it is deleted, `::warning::`, the stage is built, and the file is not written; there is no file — the build and `docker save --output <file> novatrail-toolchain`, and a failed save gives `::warning::`, the unfinished file deleted, code 0; a failed build gives its code. The warning is a workflow command without the path, and the path is a line in stderr; it tells to delete a broken cache entry: the entry is immutable, and otherwise the hit would repeat. The script takes the cache from the release tag of the end of E4, `v0.13.0` (RUN.md, T102). The job "Go" of `spec` runs by the shared `go.yml` of `.github` and will get the cache with its release of epic E17.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 in planning T104 (RUN.md), by the recommendations, — and the request of `.github` (E17, pull request 109). — *Why:* the `documents.yml` of `.github` calls the script of the caller's submodule at any tag since `v0.2.17`, and the former `build` refuses any argument: the variable it can always set — the old script will not notice it and will build the image, the new one will take the cache, and the tag need not be checked. The check `image inspect` after `load` is needed because a file with another image would load "successfully", and the next `docker run novatrail-toolchain` would go for the image to Docker Hub. A file that was there is a hit, and no save follows it: a cache entry is immutable. — *Rejected:* an argument `build <file>`; an explicit `env -u` in the release — nobody sets the variable there. — R31; RUN.md, T104, Д146; rows 1.13 and 2.4 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md).

— *Third amendment 2026-11-09:* **`v0.13.0` comes out now, not with T102: the second branch `e4` merges into `main` before the end of the epic.** The author's decision of 2026-11-09 is the third amendment of that day to answer 5 of epic E4 (RUN.md): `.github` needs the cache for T53.

## The documents check

**R32. The documents of a component repository are checked by the `docs-check` of the `spec` its submodule is on. Citations of `spec` are checked against that submodule, and examples of citations are written in inline code.**
- **Running** — from the repository's root: `just -f spec/justfile docs-check-repo`. The dependencies of `tools/` are installed by the recipe `_tools` — into `spec/tools/node_modules` of the submodule, where they are in `.gitignore`. The repository needs no justfile of its own: it comes with code (repositories 1). The root is the folder above the submodule in which the script itself lies: the path is taken neither from the arguments nor from the working folder.
- **What is checked** — the repository's files, without `spec/`:
  - links and anchors, including in `spec/`;
  - its own sections — "architecture 2" without a suffix — and the sections of the documents of `spec` — "architecture 3.8 spec", "concepts 9, 10 spec";
  - its own log of R: while there are no decisions, it is empty, and the next is R01;
  - the numbers of `spec`: "R18 spec" — by the log of `spec`, О-, П-, Т- — always by the registers of `spec`;
  - the tables «В» and «Д» in RUN.md;
  - Mermaid diagrams.
- **How citations are read:**
  - «раздел N» without a link, in a document without sections of its own — RUN.md — is a section of `docs/architecture.md`;
  - «раздел N» right after an external link, after the name of a MathTrail repository — "`docs/spec.md` canvas-api, section 4.2" — or in a nested item under an item whose last link is external, is a section of another text, and it is not checked;
  - a document of `spec` without a suffix is an error, with a hint on how to cite it.

  Errors in `spec` itself are not its business: `spec` checks itself.
- **The tables «В» and «Д»** are checked both in the repositories and in `spec`: a number does not repeat in the table, and «следующий — В…» is greater than each number in it. Gaps are allowed — an answered row leaves —, so citations of «В» and «Д» are not checked.
- **An example of a citation** — `R03`, `R19` — is written in inline code: `docs-check` does not read numbers in code (RULES.md, Citations). The template writes so. The repositories already set up fix their five examples in the task of moving to the new tag.
- **`just new-repo-check`** runs the same mode on the copy. Links to `spec` are checked by its submodule, and for a draft, by the working tree of `spec`.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-19 in planning T18: running from the submodule, examples in code, the tables «В» and «Д» in `spec` too. The parsing of citations, the root above the submodule and the reading of «раздела N» are the plan's proposal. Until now the documents of the component repositories were checked by hand (rule 6 of their RUN.md), and the one-off script of T05–T14 was lost with the session's folder (RUN.md, Д2). The current `docs-check` on the root of `.repos/module-kit` gave 434 errors: it read the submodule itself as well, and took "architecture 3.8 spec" for its own architecture.

— *Rejected:*
- a justfile of its own in the template — before code, against repositories 1;
- not checking the numbers in guillemets — the check would then be blind to real citations in quotes too, and `spec` has many of them;
- the tables «В» and «Д» only in the component repositories — one tool would hold two rules for identical tables;
- the path to the repository from the command line.

— *Consequence:* Д2 closes when the repositories move to the tag with this check — each in a task of its own (Д6). In CI it is connected by T17 and T16; whether it is a shared workflow or an own one is decided by T01 `.github`. — RUN.md, T18; repositories 2.2, 5; RULES.md, Citations.

— *Amendment 2026-10-19:* Д2 is merged with Д6. They have one deadline — the repository's move to the tag with this check —, and they close together.

— *Amendment 2026-10-20:* Д6, and with it Д2, is closed in T21. All eleven component repositories are on `spec` `v0.2.9`, and in each this check is the required CI check "Documents / docs-check-repo". In CI it was connected by T17, T16 and T21 (RUN.md).

— *Amendment 2026-10-21:* which name of a NovaTrail repository is a citation's suffix. The author's answer to В22 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- A name that can be a word of prose — `modules`, `engine`, `sim`, `tutor`, `api`, `canvas`, `app`, `infra`, `site` — is still a suffix only where the sentence ends with it: in `R99 modules are data` the citation is the repository's own.
- `.github` and the hyphenated names — `module-kit`, `learner-model`, `skill-map`, `module-registry`, `module-pipeline`, `widget-template` — are never words of prose. After a number or a section, like the names of MathTrail, they are a suffix wherever a word boundary follows them: "R19 .github and its citations" and "R03 module-kit and its recipes" are citations of other logs. A list of the form "canvas-api: R37, R38" still knows only the names of MathTrail: that is how their logs are cited (RULES.md, Citations).

Which name is which, `tools/docs-check/citations.mjs` decides by the name itself: letters only means a word. *Why:* the restriction caught a natural sentence in every repository that cites these names, and the session of `canvas` rewrote a sentence because of it in its T27 (В22 `.github`). In `spec` itself, several citations of `.github` and `module-kit` were read so as its own — in the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30, in R37 and in the archive of E1 —, and the check compared them with the log and sections of `spec`. *Rejected:* writing a citation so that a sign follows the name — every author would have to remember this; a list of exceptions in the check's `config.mjs` — a second rule beside the first. — `tools/docs-check/citations.mjs` and its tests; RULES.md, Citations.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* **in a repository the check reads only the files that git tracks or does not ignore.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В29 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **What was.** The check walked the whole tree of the root and skipped only `.git`, `node_modules` and `spec/` (`tools/docs-check/config.mjs`). In `tutor`, the measurement reports that `tutor-eval report` writes are files `.md` in `samples/runs`, outside git (architecture 3.1 tutor), and the check read them. There is no handwriting in the reports, and in CI this folder does not exist at all. But the rule of the CLAUDE.md of `tutor` keeps agents out of `samples/`, and only the command `go` has an exception from it (R14 tutor).
- **Now.** In a root with its own `.git` — in a repository, in the submodule `spec/`, in a copy that `just new-repo` built — the check reads the files `.md` by the list `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-per-directory=.gitignore`: the tracked ones that are in the working tree, and the new ones that the repository's own `.gitignore` files do not keep outside git. It sees a document not yet committed, and does not see `samples/` of `tutor`.
  - git does not enter a folder it ignores at all. The trial of 2026-10-26 on git 2.56.0 showed it: a folder without read permission under the rule `/samples/` gave not a word, and without the rule — "could not open directory".
  - The rules come only from the repository's `.gitignore`. `--exclude-standard`, which `tutor` named, adds to them also ".git/info/exclude … and the user's global exclusion file" ([git-ls-files](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/Documentation/git-ls-files.adoc), v2.56.0, read 2026-10-26), and the list would depend on the machine.
  - If git gives no list — for example, `.git` points to a folder that does not exist —, the check says so, in one line.
  - The check takes the root only by itself: `spec`, where the script lies, or with `--component` the repository around the submodule. It accepts no path from the command line: having become git's working folder, the path would let whoever writes the command run git in any folder. And git runs commands from the settings of its `.git/config`: the trial of 2026-10-26 on git 2.56.0 showed that `git ls-files` runs the hook `core.fsmonitor`. So git also runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. A path on the command line was needed only by the tests, and SonarCloud found this on pull request #47 (jssecurity:S8705 and S8707).
  - A root without `.git` — the draft of `just new-repo` from the item above and the tests' copies — the check still walks whole. The skips of `config.mjs` apply in both cases.

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`: so the check sees exactly the repository's documents, in any component, and the components need to change nothing on their side. The rule is one — for `spec` and for the components. In `spec` itself the check reads the same files as before: git ignores `.repos/`, `coverage/` and `tools/node_modules/`, and it skipped `.repos/` and `node_modules` anyway. Rules only from `.gitignore` are the executor's proposal after the review.

*Rejected:* `--exclude-standard` — the list would depend on the rules of the machine and of the clone; skipping the paths from the component's `.gitignore` by our own parsing — a second rule beside git's rule, and they could diverge; the report of `tutor` not in `.md` — a change in `tutor` only, and another component with an ignored `.md` would meet the same; refusing in a root without `.git` — `just new-repo-check` checks the draft too, which has no `.git`.

*Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/main.mjs` and its tests. The components get the change with their move to the tag, and `tutor` closes В29 with it (RUN.md, Д33).

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **the name of a NovaTrail repository after a number or a section is a citation's suffix wherever a word boundary follows it, and so is a name that can be a word of prose: `R03 modules сравнивает граф` is a citation of R03 modules, and `R10 engine решил` of R10 engine. An own citation does not put the name of a repository after it as a word of prose. After О-, П- and Т-, a NovaTrail name is a word of the sentence, not a suffix: these registers are `spec`'s, and no other NovaTrail repository keeps them. The first item of the 2026-10-21 amendment is replaced by this.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `sim` В5 (RUN.md of `sim`, `main` 6887f07) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, not by the row's recommendation: its second option, with the triage's refinement about О-, П- and Т-.

In the middle of a sentence the citation was read as its own: `R10 engine решил` in `sim` went red, and `R03 modules сравнивает граф` passed, checked against its own R03.
- **What the trial of 2026-11-08 showed.** The rule of the row's first option on the `main` of `spec` and of the eleven repositories with documents found 113 such places. In `spec` there are 74 of them, with 105 errors — 24 in `docs/decisions.md` and 16 in the epic archives `docs/plan/` —, and in the others 39: in `tutor` 14, `app` 8, `canvas` 5, `.github` 5, `learner-model` 3, `api` 2, `module-kit` 1, `sim` 1; in `engine`, `modules`, `skill-map` and `infra` — none. *Why:* the first option requires rewriting 113 places, among them entries of decision logs, which are not rewritten, and the bodies of done tasks in the archives. *Rejected:* the row's first option — an error with a hint at each ambiguous place: 74 places in `spec` and 39 in other repositories, logs and archives among them; the same, where «и» or "and" after the name ends the sentence — still 48 places in `spec`, 11 of them in the log; the second option without the refinement — `П-15 app показывает` would become another repository's citation and would not be checked, although NovaTrail has no other registers О-, П- and Т-; leaving it as it is — 112 places where a citation of another log is checked against one's own.

## Analyzer findings

**R33. An analyzer's finding that a change cannot close stays open, and its reason is recorded here.** As R51 canvas-api. The findings of CodeQL and Scorecard come to the Security tab, those of SonarCloud to its project, and rule 12 of RUN.md closes them before a new task. The answer is given once, not on each scan, and the next reader tells an answered finding from a new one. The list was compared with the first runs of CodeQL and Scorecard on `main` on 2026-10-20: `spec` — commit f2769e1, Scorecard score 6.6; `module-kit` — 254452e, 6.3 (RUN.md, T17). It is shared by all repositories with the shared checks (R30): their template, devcontainer and author are the same.
- **Scorecard `Code-Review` and `Branch-Protection`** want approvals by a second person. The project has one author, and the ruleset of `main` does without approvals on purpose (R30). Setting up a second account for the sake of the score is worse than the score itself (R51 canvas-api).
- **Scorecard `Pinned-Dependencies`** is about the `npm install -g` of Claude Code in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`. The installation goes by exact version, and npm checks the archive against the hash that the registry publishes: that is the check available to a global installation (R51 canvas-api).
- **CodeQL in `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`** — `js/xss-through-dom` (high) and four `js/cross-window-information-leak` (medium). This is the loader of a single-file prototype that a design tool built, not the platform's code. The prototype does not ship, and the documents override it ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)); SonarCloud no longer reads it. CodeQL will stop reading it when the shared `codeql.yml` gets an input for exclusions (Д8).
- **Pass with time or with tasks:**
  - `Maintained` — the repositories are younger than 90 days;
  - `SAST` — in `spec`, some of the commits were made before CodeQL;
  - `CI-Tests` — some pull requests were merged before CI: in `spec`, CI checked 11 of 13;
  - `CII-Best-Practices` — there is no OpenSSF Best Practices badge. The author gets it on bestpractices.dev, as canvas-api got it (R51 canvas-api), if the author finds it needed;
  - `Fuzzing` — there is no code yet that parses outside input: `docs-check` reads the documents of the repository itself. Fuzz tests come with such code.

`Signed-Releases` and `Packaging` (−1) and `Contributors` (3 — one organization) give no alerts.

— *Why:* rule 12 of RUN.md and the author's decision of 2026-10-20 to exclude `draft/` from CodeQL, as it is already excluded from SonarCloud. A check that will be red for the whole life of a one-person project is not a defect (R51 canvas-api).

— *Rejected:* closing such findings with the mark "false positive" or "won't fix" — then a new finding of the same rule would disappear silently; leaving the prototype's findings forever, or fixing the generated code — a new prototype would bring them again.

— *Consequence:* a finding not on this list is new, and it is closed by a change (rule 12 of RUN.md). Excluding `draft/` from CodeQL is Д8. — RUN.md, T17; R30.

The shared `codeql.yml` of `.github` got the input `paths-ignore` as early as v0.1.1 ("Paths CodeQL leaves out of the analysis of javascript-typescript — draft/**, say", the input's description at v0.1.10, read 2026-10-22), and the `codeql.yml` of `spec` is on v0.1.10 from this day and passes `draft/**`. ## The development environment

**R34. An archive that `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` downloads is checked against the sha256 checksum written beside its version.** The checksum is an `ARG` for each architecture, `amd64` and `arm64`, from the publisher's own list of checksums: `SHASUMS256.txt` of the Node release, `SHA256SUMS` of the releases of just and just-lsp, `gh_<version>_checksums.txt` of the gh release. The check runs before unpacking, and a wrong checksum stops the build. The checksum changes in the same change as the version: Dependabot does not see these versions, and they are raised by hand (R30; `.github/dependabot.yml`). — *Why:* the author's answer to В12 of `.github` — 2026-10-20, narrowed in planning epic E3 of `.github`. An exact version does not prevent substituting the archive at the same address, while a checksum in the file itself lets in no other archive once this one has been read; this is how `.github` already checks the CI tools (R08 .github). The stage `toolchain`, in which the CI checks of each repository run, needs it no less. The checksums were checked on 2026-10-20 against the publisher's list, for the releases on GitHub also against the field `digest` of their API, and against the downloaded archives themselves. — *Rejected:* `npm ci` for Claude Code — the answer to В12 dropped this part, and the Scorecard finding about `npm install -g` stays open with its reason (R33); an exact version without a checksum. — *Consequence:* the rule of exact versions in RULES.md names the checksum too; the repositories get the Dockerfile with checksums with their move to a tag of `spec`. — `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; RULES.md, Hard rules.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **a CI tool that a GitHub action or the runner image puts on the runner, and that there is nothing to pin with, is pinned as narrowly as its installer allows, and the run writes the exact version into its artifact or log.** The rule of exact versions (RULES.md, Hard rules) and the checksums of this decision are about what `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` and `devcontainer.json` install; the runner is outside them:
- the runner image is set by a label — so the jobs of `spec` run too, `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`);
- the Android system image in the workflow `emulators.yml` of `canvas` is installed by `sdkmanager`: the action `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` is pinned by SHA, the emulator build by number, the image by API level, target and architecture, `system-images;android-36;google_apis;x86_64`, and the run writes the revision into an artifact, `sdk-installed.txt` (R54 canvas). `sdkmanager` does not let one pin the revision: in the list of Google's repository this path has one entry — revision 7, the archive `x86_64-36_r07.zip` —, and its checksum is only SHA-1, `<checksum type="sha1">` ([sys-img2-4.xml](https://dl.google.com/android/repository/sys-img/google_apis/sys-img2-4.xml), read 2026-11-08). A new revision comes into CI by itself when Google releases it, and is visible in the run's artifact;
- the rule reads the same way for what comes with the macOS runner image — Xcode, which the job chooses by version, and the iOS simulator runtimes (T80 canvas).

The boundary is R12 with the 2026-10-22 amendment: such a tool only checks the platform, puts nothing of its own into a release file or an image, and NovaTrail does not distribute it. What goes into what ships is still pinned by exact version and checksum. *Why:* the author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В63 (RUN.md of `canvas`, `main` 316349d), by its recommendation — option (a) —, with the triage's refinement: the rule is general, not only about Android. The image changes only when Google releases a revision, and the run reads it every time. *Rejected:*
- the image archive by the address and checksum from `sys-img2-4.xml`, bypassing `sdkmanager`: the checksum there is SHA-1, weaker than this decision's sha256, and instead of the action, an installation step of our own. The archives of past revisions are still served at their addresses — r05 and r06 answered 200 on 2026-11-08 —, but Google has no list that names them, and the sha256 checksum would have to be computed by us, not taken from the publisher;
- our own cache of the image, raised by hand, like the snapshot of the Ubuntu archive (R40): the snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself, while here NovaTrail would keep a copy of someone else's image itself, under terms about keeping a copy that nobody has read;
- an exception in the Hard rules of RULES.md: the rule there names where versions stand — an `ARG` of the Dockerfile and a literal of `devcontainer.json` —, and does not concern the runner, while each repository would take the exception with a new tag; R40 likewise rejected an exception for the packages of `apt`.

*Revisit* if a new revision brings down a run that passed on the previous one: then install the archive by a step of our own at the previous revision, with a sha256 checksum read once and checked against the SHA-1 of the list. — R11, R12, R40; R54 canvas; RUN.md, Д122.

## The task's review

**R35. A task's review is one round of `/code-review high`, and the executor may hand in a small change without a review.**
- Having fixed the round's findings, the executor does not repeat the review.
- Whether a change is small, the executor decides. The report says whether there was a review, and if not, why.
- The rule is written in rules 6 and 8 of the RUN.md of `spec`, of the template and of each repository, and for Codex in AGENTS.md.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-21: «теперь всегда только 1 код ревью. Если изменения небольшие то код ревью в этом случае не проводится - это решает сам агент». — *Rejected:* the former rule 6, «не больше двух кругов», where the second round ran if the first found something. — *Consequence:* the change in RUN.md and AGENTS.md of twelve repositories was made by the session of `.github` on the author's direct instruction, the same day. This is a one-off departure from R21, not an amendment to it. — RUN.md; `repo-template/`; AGENTS.md.

## UI packages and samples

**R36. UI packages enter their consumer as web components, and the data types that the repositories share are taken from the releases of `spec`. Each package names its own elements; `canvas` has one element, `<novatrail-canvas>`, for every canvas kind.**
- The element gets data through properties, gives the work through a method, and gives changes and requests through events. It needs no framework, and each consumer chooses its own framework itself. In `canvas`: the writing history comes as an event after each stroke, the crop for checking through the method `exportWork()`, a request to voice through the event `speak` (R07 canvas).
- The types of the element itself come from the package, and the data types — the open view of a task, the tutor's marks, the crop and the group boxes, the writing history — from the releases of `spec` (R21). Which ones and how is decided by RUN.md, T35.
- "Listen" on the text canvas is voiced by `app` on the event `speak` — by one speech synthesis for the whole app and with one set of rules for voices (Т-13).
- The submission context — where the crop lies on the sheet (`sheet_box`), the stroke group boxes and the table "group label → stroke IDs" — is held by `app`, not by the canvas: the canvas has no data of its own (architecture 3.2). These are data on the device, derived from the learner's work (privacy 4). They do not go to the server — the group boxes only by the answer to Т-31 — and how long to keep them is decided by `app`.

— *Why:* the answer of `canvas` to Т-21, В15 of `canvas`; Т-21 was closed by it, by the author's decision of 2026-10-21. The rest is the recommendation of the same row.
- The recommendation of Т-21: the packages have several consumers — `app`, the samples page, the site, the card of the MCP channel — and each one's framework is decided by its repository. The framework of `app` is not chosen (T01 app).
- React 19 and Preact take the element by themselves: «React 19 adds full support for custom elements and passes all tests on Custom Elements Everywhere» ([React 19](https://react.dev/blog/2024/12/05/react-19#support-for-custom-elements)), «Preact fully supports Web Components» ([Preact, Web Components](https://preactjs.com/guide/v10/web-components/)); both read 2026-10-21 (architecture 4 canvas).
- A new canvas kind is the platform's code (R02): with one element for every kind, a new version of `canvas` brings it without a change to `app`.
- The element's Shadow DOM is open, for the sake of styles: it isolates the styles and the DOM tree, but not the code (R16; architecture 8). Third-party code still runs only in a sandboxed iframe.
- `app` itself put off speech synthesis until Т-21 (architecture 2.4 app). One synthesis for the whole app holds one rule for voices — only local ones (Т-13).

— *Rejected:*
- components of the framework of `app` — they would decide for `app`, whose framework is not chosen, and would carry the framework into the second build and into the samples page, and give a consumer with another framework the duplicates R16 writes about;
- a mount function — each consumer would write the mounting, unmounting and cleanup itself, and each framework would need a wrapper of its own;
- the canvas voices by itself — the rules for voices would live in two packages;
- the submission context in the canvas's memory — the canvas would get data of its own.

— *Consequence:* Т-21 is closed. `skill-map` names its own elements in its detailing. — architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 6; repositories 8; R07 canvas.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* **`<novatrail-canvas>` has buttons of the sheet of its own (R28 canvas): the event `toolchange` and the attribute `lang` are a contract of `canvas` and `app`, and the button captions are the package's own table.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В40 (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 1b7f139), its first option.
- **`toolchange`.** The element announces the learner's change of tool by the event `toolchange` — a `CustomEvent` from the host, `bubbles` and `composed`, with a frozen `detail` `{ tool }`. It comes only when the learner changed the tool with a button of the element: there is no event on an assignment to `tool`, on a repeated press of the selected tool, or on the return of the pen with a new task. The event's type is issued by RUN.md, T35, like the data types above: the event is part of the contract, not only a type of the package.
- **The language** is the attribute `lang` on the element itself (R07 canvas). The element does not read the language of an ancestor.
- **The button captions** are the package's own table in English and Russian. A language is looked up in it as in [RFC 4647](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647), section 3.4, — «the language range is progressively truncated from the end until a matching language tag is located» — and one not found is English. The button row has its own `lang` — the language of its captions.
- **The accessibility of the button row:**
  - a toolbar by the APG: one Tab stop, the arrows, Home and End;
  - "Pen" and "Eraser" are radio buttons;
  - "Undo" and "Clear", when unavailable, have `aria-disabled`;
  - the target is 44 × 44 CSS px, as in criterion 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) of level AAA: «at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels» ([WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024);
  - in forced colors mode, the system colors.

  The RFC and the WCAG were read 2026-10-26.
- **The offset of the sticky row** is the CSS variable `--novatrail-canvas-top`.
- **The fifth button.** Since T35 of `canvas` (R29 canvas) the row has a fifth button — «Рисовать пальцем», "Draw with finger". The pen mode is a state of the page, with no property and no event, so T35 of `canvas` does not change the element's interface. This is from the text of the row that the author brought on 2026-10-26: T35 is not yet in `main` of `canvas`.
- **The shared schema.** The table of captions and the accessibility of the row are taken by T07 `app` as input to the schema of translations and the accessibility standard shared by the UI packages (architecture 3.1). How the sheet scrolls with one pointer is decided together with this standard — О-24.

*Why:* the recommendation of `canvas`. The names of the event and the attribute are a contract of `canvas` and `app`: without them in `spec`, `app` would learn it only from the package, and RUN.md, T35 would not issue the event's type. For the shared schema of T07 `app`, a package that already has buttons is useful: its table of captions is easy to move onto it.

*Rejected:*
- R36 names only the gist, and the names and the composition stay with `canvas`: the contract of `canvas` and `app` would remain without a record in `spec`;
- the button captions are given by `app`, and the UI packages have no tables of their own: each consumer would translate the button captions, the samples page too.

*Consequence:* architecture 3.1 and 3.2; «Вход» of RUN.md, T35. `canvas` closes В40, and `app` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д35.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* **the writing history and the work for checking of `<novatrail-canvas>` (R27 canvas) are a contract of `canvas` and `app` too: the property `history`, the event `historychange` and the method `exportWork()`, and the submission context also carries the integers of the crop and the submission digest.** The author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» `canvas` В38 and В37 (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 5feb06f), their first options. From В37 only the submission context is here, and the mark and the snapping rule went into epic E3 of RUN.md.
- **`history`** is a property for reading and assignment. Reading gives a frozen array of history events. Assigning the same history changes nothing, and another one, if the sheet could have written it, replaces the sheet and places the marks anew. The sheet does not take a history it could not have written — `TypeError` — and stays as it was.
- **`historychange`** is a `CustomEvent` from the host, `bubbles` and `composed`, synchronous after each action on the sheet: a stroke, an erasure, a clearing and an undo, not only a stroke, as said above. Its `detail` is frozen — `{ events, from }`: the new history events and the number of the first of them. A store whose length is not equal to `from` has missed events and rereads `history`. There is no event on an assignment to `history`.
- **`exportWork()`** is an asynchronous method: its promise gives `{ png, submission }` — the PNG of the crop and the submission context — and for an empty sheet, `null`.
- **The submission context**, beyond `sheet_box`, the group boxes and the table "group label → stroke IDs", carries:
  - the integers of the crop — the digit height on it, the size and the margins, from which `sheet_box` and the boxes are derived. By them snapping places the marks on the strokes (R26 canvas), and without them there is no exact snapping;
  - the submission digest — 16 hexadecimal digits of the table's strokes and the integers of the crop. By it the element takes the context back, together with the marks of that submission. The digest catches an accidental divergence, not a forgery.

  `app` keeps the history and the context as they are, through JSON. If the store rounds the numbers, the element does not take the context: with rounded points of the strokes the digest does not match, and with a rounded `sheet_box` the reconciliation with the integers of the crop fails, whose tolerance is a millionth of a sheet unit (R26 and R27 canvas). The integers of the crop and the digest are derived from the same work of the learner as the earlier context, lie on the device and do not go to the server (privacy 4).
- **The types** of the event, the property and `exportWork()` are issued by RUN.md, T35, like the type of `toolchange`.
- The digit height from В38 was settled by R51: the module manifest sets it.

*Why:* the recommendations of `canvas`. The names of the event and the property are a contract of `canvas` and `app`, like `toolchange`: without them in `spec`, `app` would learn them only from the package, and T35 would not issue their types. The new events in `detail` spare `app` comparing the whole history on each action. R36 already names the context's composition, and without the integers of the crop exact snapping is impossible.

*Rejected:*
- R36 names only the gist, and the names and the composition stay with `canvas`: the contract that R36 began would remain without a record;
- the event carries the whole history, not the new events: `app` would compare the whole history on each action;
- the contract has only the mark, and the context stays the business of `canvas` and `app`: R36 already names its composition, and without the integers of the crop in it `spec` would describe a context by which a mark cannot be placed.

*Consequence:* privacy 4; architecture 3.1 and 3.2; «Вход» of RUN.md, T35. `canvas` closes В38 and this part of В37, and `app` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д36.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* **`<novatrail-canvas>` takes the module manifest through the property `manifest`, and on the workbook the contract of `canvas` and `app` is the crops of the filled boxes, the property `filled` and the mark's slot by its place (R32, R34 and R37–R39 canvas).** The author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» `canvas` В42 and В46 (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 6b87374), their first options.
- **`manifest`** is a property: the open view of the module manifest of the task, as `app` has it (architecture 3.1). The element reads three fields from it and skips the rest:
  - `module_format_version` — the format version, otherwise `TypeError`: while the format is v0, the platform reads only its current version (R44);
  - `canvas.digit_height` — the digit height on the crop of the sheet and of a workbook box (R51). `exportWork()` takes it at the moment of the call;
  - `languages.explanation` — the language of the statement and of the workbook's lines.

  The canvas settings in the manifest are its own: a setting in `canvas` of the manifest that the element does not know is a `TypeError`, since without it the element would draw the module's canvas wrongly. Without a manifest the digit height is 32, and the statement is in the element's own language. `task` and `manifest` do not depend on each other. How `app` gets the manifest with the task is decided by RUN.md, T34.
- **`exportWork()` on the workbook** is a promise of `{ cells, submission }`:
  - `cells` — `{ item, slot, png }` of each filled box, in the order of the task. The PNG is a crop by the crop rule of R25 canvas: by the box's strokes, at the manifest's digit height, ink only. `item` and `slot` are the places of the item and the box, from 1 (R51);
  - `submission` — the submission context of the workbook `{ boxes, digest }`: the table "box → stroke IDs" and the digest of its strokes, of all the boxes of the page and of the table's rows. The element does not take the context of another page layout;
  - if not one box is filled, `null`, even if the page has a draft.

  The kind of work names its key: `png` for the sheet, `cells` for the workbook. Only the crops with their places leave the device (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53), and the table and the digest stay with `app`, like the context of the sheet (privacy 4).
- **`filled`** is a property for reading: per item, per box, whether it is filled, in the order of the task, and on the sheet, `null`. A box is filled if it has at least one stroke of those that would go into `exportWork()`. The value changes with an action on the page, before `historychange`, and on an assignment to `task` and `history`, with no event. On the workbook this is the exit condition `answer_slots_filled` itself (R57). What it means for the bindings `anywhere` and `sheet` is still decided by `app` and `canvas` (architecture 3.1).
- **A mark** names an answer slot by its place — `{ item, slot }`, from 1 — on both canvas kinds: slots have no IDs (R51). On the workbook a mark holds on to the strokes of its box from the table of its submission, and its box stands around the box and its ink. A group label and a box in fractions of the crop on the workbook are a `TypeError`.
- **The order:** `task` and `history` are given before `marks`. The element reconciles the workbook's context with the boxes of the page, and before the task it has no page.
- **The types** — `ExportedSheet`, `ExportedWorkbook`, `ExportedCell`, `SheetSubmission`, `WorkbookSubmission`, `Filling` and `CellPlace`, and with them the types of `filled` and of the manifest — are issued by RUN.md, T35. Until then they are temporary in `canvas`.

*Why:* the recommendations of `canvas`. R51 put the digit height and the explanation language into the manifest, and `app` already has the manifest: by it `app` asks for the learner's grade. Filling is a property, not an event: `canvas` rejected two events for one action (R27 canvas), and the `detail` of `historychange` was fixed by the second 2026-10-26 amendment. The digest holds all the boxes of the page, not only the filled ones: otherwise the context of another layout would pass when the filled boxes stayed in their places (R38 canvas). The names of the properties and the composition of the work are a contract of `canvas` and `app`, like `toolchange` and `history`: without a record in `spec`, `app` would learn them only from the package, and T35 would not issue their types.

*Rejected:*
- the module's settings in the open view of each task, where the package of T34 would put them: R51 rejected a digit height in each task;
- the element's own properties with the names of `canvas`: the names would not be from the format, and `app` would parse the manifest itself;
- `{ png, submission }` on the workbook too, where the PNG is the boxes glued together with their rectangles: the model would search for what is in which box (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53);
- filling in the `detail` of `historychange` or as an event of its own;
- `png: null` for an empty box: an empty entry would invite sending an empty box, and which ones are empty `filled` says anyway.

*Consequence:* architecture 3.1 and 3.2; privacy 4; «Вход» of RUN.md, T34 and T35. `canvas` closes В42 and В46, and `app` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д41.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* how `app` gets the manifest with the task (RUN.md, T34): `api` gives the open view of the manifest by the package digest of the attempt, once per package, and `app` caches it by this digest and gives it to the canvas through the property `manifest` (R62). This is not the copy of the settings in each task that the 2026-10-27 amendment rejected. The form of the messages is decided by the contract of epic E3. — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-10-29:* the Go types of the open view of the manifest, the task and the lesson are the package `types/formatv0/open` of the Go module `spec`, under the same names as in `types/formatv0` (R72). The types of the element of `canvas` are RUN.md, T46, in the same package. — R73; RUN.md, T49.

— *Amendment 2026-11-01:* **the types of the element `<novatrail-canvas>` are `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` from line 0.5, written by hand (R74).** They hold the element's properties, method and events, the writing history, the work for checking and the submission context, `Filling`, `CellPlace` and `Filled`. The tutor's marks — the property `marks` and the type of a mark — wait for the contract of epic E3, and until then they are temporary in `canvas`: this is how "the tutor's marks" among the data types "from the releases of `spec`" above are read. — *Second amendment 2026-11-01:* **the element takes the worked example of a lesson through the property `workedExample`, gives the state of its demo through the property `demoState` and the event `demochange`, and `filled` on the sheet says whether an `anywhere` or `sheet` slot has a stroke.** The author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» `canvas` В52–В54 (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 1ee71e0), by the recommendations of `canvas`: this is how R42 canvas decided them and T57–T60 of `canvas` built them.
- **`filled` on the sheet** (В52). For an `anywhere` or `sheet` slot — it is the only one in the task — `filled` equals `[[true]]` if the sheet has a stroke that `exportWork()` would take, and otherwise `[[false]]`. A sheet where all the slots are `choice`, a sheet without a task and an example give `null`; the type is as before. A task with a `zone` slot the element does not take at all — `TypeError`: no module of the slice takes zones yet (R51). "On the sheet, `null`" in the 2026-10-27 amendment above is read this way. `app` reads the exit condition `answer_slots_filled` by the slot binding: for `choice`, by its own choice of an option, for other slots, by `filled` (architecture 3.1).
- **The worked example** (В53) is the property `workedExample`: the open view of the lesson segment `worked_example`, the type `WorkedExample` (R58). The element shows a task or an example, not both: an example with a task or with a writing history is a `TypeError`, and a task with an example too. In example mode:
  - the sheet takes no input, and the tool is the pen alone, with no event, and the eraser is a `TypeError`; the button row is "Example";
  - `history` is only empty, `marks` is a `TypeError`, and `exportWork()` and `filled` give `null`.

  The module manifest of an example the element takes through the same property `manifest` as for a task. For each lesson segment `app` gives a new element (R20 canvas). On one element a task comes when the example is removed — `undefined` — and another example starts its demo from the beginning.
- **The demo** (В54). The learner opens the parts of the demo one at a time, and hides and shows the whole demo, with the element's buttons — "Next" and "Demo".
  - The state of the demo is `demoState`, `{ opened, hidden }`: how many parts are open, from the first, and whether the demo is hidden. A new example starts with `{ opened: 0, hidden: false }`, with no event, and without an example there is no state.
  - The element sends the event `demochange` only on the learner's press. `app` keeps the state and can return it through the same property — after the example, and then there is no event. A state that this example cannot have is a `TypeError`; what to do with a state saved for another version of the module is decided by `app` (architecture 3.1).
  - The lesson segments are led by `app` (architecture 3.1). Where the parts of the demo stand is decided by `canvas` ([format text](../format/README.md), section 21): above the sheet, under the statement.
- **The types** — the properties `workedExample` and `demoState`, `DemoState`, `DemoChangeEvent` and `demochange` in `CanvasEventMap` — are in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` (R74). This change needs no new line, as R74 says of a change to the element's types.

*Why:* the recommendations of `canvas`, and for В53 and В54, what it has already decided and built.
- `filled` by the binding needs neither a second property nor a new type, and `app` knows the binding from the open view of the task.
- An example is not a task: it has no slots, no key and no work of the learner ([format text](../format/README.md), section 21), and a mixed mode would be a third kind of element.
- The demo's buttons are the element's: the parts stand on its sheet and above it. The state is `app`'s: it leads the lesson and its segments and after a break returns the learner to where they were.

*Rejected:*
- `filled` by slot, with `null` for `choice`, and an `app` that folds the `replay` history itself (В52 of `canvas`);
- an example through `task` and an element of its own for an example (В53 of `canvas`);
- a demo led only by `app`, through a property, and only by the element, without a property (В54 of `canvas`).

*Consequence:* architecture 3.1 and 3.2 — who owns what; `types/canvas/index.d.ts` and the README of the npm package. Card 3.2 no longer speaks of temporary types "of the same composition": the types of the task and the manifest in `canvas` since `v0.4.1` are from the package of `spec`, and the element takes the task's fields since T55 of `canvas` (the answer to В51 of `canvas`, by its recommendation). `canvas` and `app` get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д58.

This is a contract of `canvas` and `app`, and the commands `undo()` and `clear()` are `canvas`'s own, outside the contract.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В58 (RUN.md of `canvas`, `main` e0ddfaa), by its recommendation; this is how R07 and R23 canvas decided it.

The element asks for each reference once, however many images show it. - *Rejected:* all three members in the contract: a contract that `app` does not carry out would bind `canvas` to no purpose; none, with `app` writing `media` by the type from the package of `canvas`: the contract's type would be on one side only, which R74 rejected.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-02:* **the element works under the consumer's CSP without inline styles: it sets the styles of its Shadow DOM with `adoptedStyleSheets` — a `CSSStyleSheet` with `replaceSync()` — and not with a `<style>` element or a `style` attribute in the markup. Of the consumer's CSP it requires only `img-src blob:`.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В28 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 14f5a54), by its recommendation, recorded as a requirement of the contract.
- Now the element puts a `<style>` into the Shadow DOM — `document.createElement("style")` and `style.textContent = STYLE` (`src/element/index.ts`, `canvas` 297849c). Such a `<style>` is connected to the document: «A node is connected if its shadow-including root is a document» ([DOM](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/), Last Updated 19 October 2026). A style block is checked by the CSP: «If the Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy? algorithm returns "Blocked" … then return» ([HTML](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html), update a style block, Last Updated 30 October 2026); both read 2026-11-02. By CSP3, «The styles will be blocked unless every policy allows inline style» (read by `app` 2026-11-02; architecture 4 app), and `app` has `style-src 'self'` (R09 app).
- `replaceSync()` has no CSP step: «Let rules be the result of running parse a stylesheet's contents from text» (CSSOM, Editor's Draft 13 October 2026, read by `app` 2026-11-02). That browsers do not block it is a conclusion from the texts. It is held by a test of the element of `canvas` under the policy `default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; img-src blob:` and by Д9 app.
- `ShadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets` is in Chrome since 73, in Firefox since 101, in Safari and Safari on iOS since 16.4 (`mdn/browser-compat-data`, `api/ShadowRoot.json`, commit a8813fc, read 2026-11-02).
- *Why:* the CSP of `app` does not change with the canvas version, and other consumers — the samples page, the site — need not allow inline styles.
- *Rejected:* a `sha256` hash of the canvas styles in `style-src` of `app` — each change to the canvas styles would change the CSP of `app`; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` — third-party markup could inline styles too.

— architecture 3.2; RUN.md, Д79.

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **the tutor's marks of `<novatrail-canvas>` are no longer temporary: the property `marks` and the types `Marks`, `Mark` and `Anchor` are in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas`, and their form and place are reconciled with the message `Mark` of the contract `novatrail.api.v1` (the second 2026-11-03 amendment to R74; R97). "Wait for the contract of epic E3" of the 2026-11-01 amendment above is fulfilled by this. О-24 from the 2026-10-26 amendment on the buttons of the sheet above — how the sheet scrolls with one pointer — is settled by R90: by the buttons "Up" and "Down" of the row of `canvas`.** — R74, R90, R97; R143; repositories 9.6, the example of T128; RUN.md, T131.

**R37. UI packages are published to npm, in the scope of the organization `@altnovatrail`; for `canvas`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`. The same file that is signed in the GitHub release goes to npm, by a step of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` — through trusted publishing, with no long-lived token.**
- The package is installed by an exact version and with no token, including by the authors of widgets from stage 4. Widget bundles are still pinned by hash in the module package (R16).
- The version in npm is tied to the signed release by a sum: the sha256 of its archive is in the signed `SHA256SUMS` of the GitHub release (R08 canvas). What checks the signature is Т-27.
- The publishing step is in the shared release of `.github`, not a job of its own in each repository with a package. How it is built is decided by `.github` with an amendment to its R18 .github: the shared workflows are its own (R30). What `canvas` asks of the step (В18 of `canvas`):
  - it runs on the runner, not in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: tokens do not go there (R18 .github);
  - Node and npm by an exact version and sum in the file itself, like cosign (R08 .github), no lower than npm 11.5.1 and Node 22.14.0;
  - it runs only if the caller named the package file: the author publishes the first version by hand, since a trusted publisher is configured for a package that is already in the registry;
  - `--access public` explicitly; with `publish: false` it publishes nothing;
  - on a rerun it takes the file from the release and checks the signature, does not publish a published version again but checks it by `integrity`; a version lower than the newest in npm it does not put under `latest`; on a refusal that `release-refusal` lets through, it publishes nothing.

  Whether the registry accepts provenance from a reusable workflow of another repository, the npm documentation does not say: the first publishing of `canvas` with this step will check it (T24 canvas).
- The types of `spec` are in `spec`'s own release (R31), and where their package is published is decided by RUN.md, T35. The recommendation of `canvas` is the same npm (В16 of `canvas`).

The criterion of Т-26 — install by an exact version and with no token — is met only by npm. All read 2026-10-21:
- in npm anyone installs a public package in a scope: «Scoped public packages can be downloaded and installed by anyone», and a version does not change: «Registry data is immutable, meaning once published, a package cannot change» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/tree/4e8e03b978033529bf8f50d74305b29939eb022c), commit 4e8e03b, `downloading-and-installing-packages-locally.mdx` and `policies/unpublish.mdx`). An organization for public packages is free — «the "Unlimited public packages" free plan» (ibid., `creating-an-organization.mdx`). The author created the organization `altnovatrail` in npm on 2026-10-21 (architecture 4 canvas);
- from a reusable workflow npm checks the caller: «validation checks the calling workflow's name instead of the workflow that actually contains the publish command», and «The `id-token: write` permission must also be given to both parent and child workflows»; «Trusted publishing requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher» (ibid., `trusted-publishers.mdx`). OIDC needs no secret, so the step does not break the rule "shared workflows take no secrets" (the 2026-10-20 amendment to R24);
- the publishing code is one for all the repositories with packages on the shared release, and the provenance certificate, by the Fulcio rule, names the shared `release.yml` in its SAN, like the cosign signatures (Т-27).

— *Rejected:*
- GitHub Packages — a token is needed even to install a public package: «You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages» ([github/docs](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/cca0c9d7299f760587d6601bd96acfd2f5cb8929/data/reusables/package_registry/authenticate-packages.md), commit cca0c9d, read 2026-10-21);
- only GitHub releases — npm 12 closes installing by a link by default: «As of npm 12 the default is `none`» for `allow-remote` ([npm/cli](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/ae98c62586b6fea44114f72e249e246a2981de70/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js), v12.2.1, commit ae98c62, read 2026-10-21), and each project would need `allow-remote=root`;
- a publishing job of its own in the `release.yml` of each repository — a copy for each repository with a package, and it needs a change to `.github` too: the shared `release.yml` has no outputs — neither the version nor a sign that the release came out;
- staged publishing — the author with 2FA approves each version, and the release again waits for a person, while it must come out by itself (R31; R18 .github);
- publishing each version by hand; a long-lived npm token in the secrets — a shared workflow takes no secrets (R05 .github).

— *Consequence:* Т-26 is closed. `.github` writes the amendment to R18 .github and the step, and T24 canvas waits for it. — architecture 3.2, 3.3, 3.11, 3.12, 6; repositories 8; R08 canvas.

- the package name is a literal, not an input, and there is no step `npm-name`: the name of the package file is given by the output `npm` of the step "Build the files", and it also decides whether the npm steps run;

The archive and its `package.json` are checked, then the package document from the registry by `?write=true`, then `npm publish --dry-run`. If the package is not in the registry, the run fails;
- publishing is after "Verify the release" and before the check of the Go module: `npm publish --access public` through trusted publishing. The outcome is decided by the registry, not by npm's exit code: npm may end successfully when the version is only prepared for publishing (staged), or fail on a version that came out ([npm/cli#9889](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9889), open as of 2026-10-29). So the step waits for the version in the registry and checks its `integrity` and the archive byte for byte against the release file;
- a version that is already in npm with the same `integrity` is skipped. With another one, the run fails. Beyond `.github`, the run fails the same way on a number that npm already gave out and that was unpublished — the `time` of the package document remembers it: «Once `package@version` has been used, you can never use it again» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/policies/unpublish.mdx), commit 514e6c9, read 2026-10-29). If the release has already come out, the package is published by the next release, with a new number, and the message says so. If not yet, all the releases of the line stop, since each would take the same number, until `RELEASE_LINE` is raised, and the message names this. A number in npm without a release of `spec` can come only from someone else's publishing;
- a version lower than the newest goes under the tag `previous`: without a tag npm 11 does not publish it — «Cannot implicitly apply the "latest" tag because previously published version … is higher than the new version» ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/lib/commands/publish.js), `lib/commands/publish.js`, read 2026-10-29). The step counts the newest as npm does there: among the versions without a pre-release and without `deprecated`. So the placeholder `0.0.0-stage` that the registry set up with the package (RUN.md, В26) does not count;
- a refusal of the Releases API that `release-refusal` lets through publishes nothing in npm: there is no release, and the release of the tip covers it;
- a rerun of an already released commit publishes the file from the release, not one built anew. It is checked by `gh release verify-asset` — the attestation ties the file to the release and its commit — and by `cosign verify-blob`: the signature of the `release.yml` of `spec` on `main`, in this repository. `verify-blob` does not check the commit of the signing run: it is the tip of `main` at the start of that run, and a new run of the same commit — for example, CI run on it again — goes from a later tip;
- a commit that is no longer the tip of `main` goes to npm too. npm's provenance names as its commit `GITHUB_SHA` — `gitCommit: env.GITHUB_SHA` ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/workspaces/libnpmpublish/lib/provenance.js), read 2026-10-29) — that is, the tip, like the cosign certificate of its files, and its own commit is named by the release's attestation.

The package's trusted publisher is the repository `altnovatrail/spec`, the file `release.yml`, without an environment, with direct publishing: `npm trust github @altnovatrail/spec --file release.yml --repository altnovatrail/spec --allow-publish`. 0.4.0 has no provenance: the author published this version by hand.

*Rejected:*

- a warning instead of a failure when the `integrity` differs — the version in npm would silently diverge from the release file;
- only the release of the tip goes to npm: an earlier commit would have a tag, and its version would not be in npm.

— architecture 3.11, 3.12; repositories 5; RUN.md, T51.
