## The license check in other repositories

**R39. The other repositories take the list of licenses and the check of an npm lock file by recipes of `spec`: `licenses-allowed` and `licenses-check-repo`. The check rejects a lock file without `packages`.**
- **The list.** `just -f spec/justfile licenses-allowed` prints the list of category A from `tools/licenses/config.mjs` (R12), one SPDX identifier per line. This is an interface, like the release recipes (the 2026-10-20 amendment to R31): the layout of `config.mjs` can be changed without breaking the caller.
- **The check of an npm lock file** is `just -f spec/justfile licenses-check-repo <lock-file> [<exceptions file>]`, from the repository's root. The paths are its own: a path that leads out of it, the check rejects.
  - Each package of the lock file is checked against the same list and the same parsing of SPDX expressions as in `licenses-check` of `spec` itself.
  - The exceptions are the repository's own. This is JSON: an object of packages, each with `license` — what the lock file says of it, or `null` — and `reason`: why it is accepted and by which decision. There are no other fields, and a file of another form stops the check.
  - The exceptions of `spec` do not pass to another lock file. An exception that has nothing to accept in the lock file is an error, as in `spec`.
- **A lock file without `packages`** — lockfileVersion 1, such as npm 5 and 6 wrote — the check rejects, and so does `licenses-check` of `spec` itself. Before, it read such a file as empty and answered "ok". «1: The lockfile version used by npm v5 and v6», and `packages` is «an object that maps package locations to an object containing the information about that package» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-21).
- **Who calls.** The recipes run in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: Node is there. How `go.yml`, `typescript.yml` and `self-ci.yml` call them is decided by `.github`: the shared workflows are its own (R30). The recommendation of `.github` is this:
  - `self-ci.yml` checks the copy of the list in `go.yml` against the output of `licenses-allowed`, not against a parsing of `config.mjs` as text;
  - the job `licenses` of the shared `typescript.yml` takes the submodule `spec` and calls `licenses-check-repo`. This is an exception to the checkout without a submodule (R16 .github): there the ban is held by the code that takes the files of `spec` from releases (R21), and here the submodule gives the check's tool.

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-21 to В19 and В20 of `.github`, by their recommendations; `.github` itself recommended recording them in one task.
- `go.yml` and `typescript.yml` of `.github` carry copies of the list, `ALLOWED_LICENSES`. The job "Workflows" of `self-ci.yml` checks them against `spec/tools/licenses/config.mjs`, reading the file as text, one quoted identifier per line (RUN.md of `.github`, commit b3ee1a8). This file had no interface, as `line.mjs` had none before the 2026-10-20 amendment to R31.
- The contract of the TypeScript wrapper has `ci-licenses` check each package of the lock file against this list, with exceptions by name (R19 .github). `spec` had such a check, but only for its own `tools/package-lock.json` and with its own exceptions. Without a recipe each TypeScript repository — `canvas`, `app`, `skill-map` — would write a script of its own, like canvas-api (R48 canvas-api), and the rule would diverge across the copies.

— *Rejected:*
- the list as a separate data file that `config.mjs` reads too: the caller would again read an internal file of `spec`, only another one;
- the check as a release file of `spec` or an npm package: the release of `spec` has no files (R31), and their path is decided by RUN.md, T35;
- leave it as it is.

— *Consequence:* `.github`, with its move to a tag, checks the copies of the list against `licenses-allowed` and calls `licenses-check-repo` from `typescript.yml`. `canvas`, `app` and `skill-map` move their `ci-licenses` and exceptions to the recipe with their move (RUN.md, Д15). — repositories 5; architecture 3.11; R12.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* an exception for a license outside the list in `licenses-check-repo` is only for a development tool, as in the check of `canvas` (R12 and R14 canvas). The author's answer, by the executor's recommendation: the divergence was found when the letter to `canvas` about its T08 was being written.
- **Only `dev`.** An exception that accepts a license outside the list — an SPDX expression or a text that does not parse as one — holds only a package that the lock file marks `dev`: «If the package is strictly part of the `devDependencies` tree, then `dev` will be true». Such a package without `dev` is an error: the exception is for a tool that never ships (R12; RULES.md, Licenses). `devOptional` is not `dev`: «If it is both a `dev` dependency _and_ an `optional` dependency of a non-dev dependency, then `devOptional` will be set» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-22), and a dependency of a package that ships may go out together with it.
- **Builds for platforms.** The same exception covers the packages that the tool itself names in `optionalDependencies` — this is how its builds for platforms come — as long as they too are `dev` and under the same license. Such a build without `dev` is an error with a reason of its own, and a package under another license is checked like any other. In `canvas`, one exception `lightningcss` covers in this way its 11 builds under MPL-2.0 (R14 canvas): on the lock file of `canvas` 88492c4 the recipe with it answers "ok — 115 packages, 1 exceptions", and without it names 12 packages.
- **An exception for `null` or for `SEE LICENSE IN <file>`** corrects what the lock file says, rather than accepting a license outside the list. This is how a lock file says that it has no license, or that the license is in the package's own file: «If you are using a license that hasn't been assigned an SPDX identifier, or if you are using a custom license, use a string value like this one» ([npm Docs, package.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json), read 2026-10-22). What license the package actually has, the reason says, and a person reads it, as before the amendment. Such an exception has no condition of `dev`.
- **`licenses-check` of `spec` itself** does not carry this condition: its `tools/` does not ship at all, and the packages in it are `dependencies`, and the lock file marks none of them `dev`.

*Why:* the check of `canvas` is built this way and passes its CI (R12 and R14 canvas), and Д15 expects `canvas` to move to the recipe. Without the amendment it would lose the `dev` boundary in the move, and the exception `lightningcss` would become twelve names — R14 canvas rejected this. The `dev` boundary carries the condition of R12, "never ships", from the reason that a person reads into the check itself. *Rejected:* leave R39 as it is; an open question while `canvas` keeps its own script — the rule would again live in two copies; the condition of `dev` for the exceptions with `null` and `SEE LICENSE IN` as well — then a shipped package whose license from the list lies in its file, not in the lock file, could not be taken; any text that does not parse as an SPDX expression, without the condition of `dev` — then a typo in a license would get around the boundary. — `tools/licenses/main.mjs` and its tests; RUN.md, Д15, Д16.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **an exception that accepts a license not from the list holds only a package of which nothing goes into any of the repository's deliverables — neither into an npm package, nor into a build, nor into a release file. A repository whose deliverable is a bundler's build keeps everything that the bundler embeds into it in `dependencies`, and `devDependencies` is for development and CI tools. Т-36 is closed.** The author's answer to Т-36, the first option, by the recommendation; T01 `app` came to the same by itself (R03 app; architecture 3.1 app, `main` of `app` 0849269).
- **What moved.** The mark `dev` says which tree the package came from: «If the package is strictly part of the `devDependencies` tree, then `dev` will be true» (the 2026-10-22 amendment above). Whether it goes into a deliverable, it does not say: `canvas` embeds the data of the icon set at build time from a package in `devDependencies` (R78). So the condition of R12, "never ships", is held not by the mark `dev` alone, but by it and the exception's reason together: the check compares `dev`, as before, and that nothing from the package goes into a deliverable is said by the reason and held by review. The amendment does not change the check's code.
- **An app** — `app`, later `site` — keeps in `dependencies` everything that its bundler embeds, and in `devDependencies` only tools. Then `dev` in it again means "never ships", and an exception under `dev` accepts nothing embedded. T01 `app` has already decided so: in `dependencies` are `react`, `react-dom`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`, later `skill-map`, and the package of the icon set, and its `ci-vuln` — `npm audit --omit=dev` — depends on the same boundary.
- **An npm package** — `canvas`, `skill-map` — keeps in `dependencies` what its consumer needs, and a package whose data it embeds at build time — the icon set — in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need it. Such a package has no exception (R78). Where a package stands that only the repository's second build embeds — the samples page of `canvas` (R25) — is decided by `canvas` together with its build, by the same rule of exceptions.

*Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-02 to Т-36, by the recommendation. The rule is for everyone, not only for `app`: for `site` and for the second build of a package (architecture 6) the deliverable is a build too. *Rejected:* close Т-36 with a rule of `app` alone, without a rule in `spec` — `site` and the samples page would decide anew; a check of the exceptions against the bundler's manifest in `licenses-check-repo` as well — new code in `tools/licenses`, and each bundler has an input of its own; `app` has no exceptions for licenses not from the list — it would lose `lightningcss`, a tool that R12 allows (R03 app). — repositories 8, Т-36; architecture 3.1 and 6; R78; RUN.md, Д61.

## System packages in the devcontainer

**R40. A system package that `apt` installs in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is taken from the Ubuntu archive as of a date — by a snapshot. The snapshot ID is an `ARG` beside the list of packages, and it is raised by hand, like a version.**
- In one `RUN`: `apt-get update --snapshot "$UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT"`, then `apt-get install --snapshot "$UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT"` with the list of packages. Each package is then an exact version, the one that was in the archive at that moment, and the rule of exact versions (RULES.md, Hard rules) is met without a version for each package.
- `apt` checks the archive's signature itself, as on any update.
- The snapshot is raised by hand, like a version that Dependabot does not see (R30): when the list of packages changes and when the build fails after a new digest of the base image (R13 canvas).
- The rule is about the packages of the Ubuntu archive. A package from another `apt` archive, which has no snapshots, brings a decision of its own.
- The Dockerfile of `spec` has no `apt` packages. `canvas` was the first to need the rule: 21 Chromium libraries on Ubuntu 24.04 and fonts, in its T08 (R13 canvas).

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-21 to В21 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- `apt` does not pin versions itself, and the Playwright image by digest gives the browsers but not their system libraries: in the image those lie outside `/ms-playwright` (architecture 4 .github).
- Snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself: «The Ubuntu snapshot service makes it possible to see and use the Ubuntu archive as it was at any specified date and time», «Snapshots of the Ubuntu archive are available for any date and time after 1 March 2023» and «We intend to ensure snapshots are available for dates up to at least 2 years in the past, which we may extend if there is demand». Ubuntu 24.04 finds them by itself: «The apt included in Ubuntu 24.04 and later automatically detects when snapshots are supported for a repository». The order of the commands: «the apt update --snapshot [snapshot] command needs to be run immediately before the other apt commands», and «These commands will also fail if the snapshot format is incorrect or the snapshot does not exist» ([Ubuntu Snapshot Service](https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/), read 2026-10-21).
- Checked in a build. The Dockerfile of `canvas` on `main`, commit 88492c4 (pull request #18, T08 canvas), installs the packages with `ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT=20261021T000000Z` and `--snapshot`. In CI run 39691386053 on this commit the `toolchain` stage built, and all 61 packages came from `https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20261021T000000Z` (the log of the job "TypeScript / test", read 2026-10-21).

— *Rejected:*
- a version for each package, `package=version`: the Ubuntu archive does not keep all old versions, and the build will break when it removes them (the argument of В21 of `.github`);
- the `toolchain` stage from the Playwright image by tag and digest: it has the libraries, but its user is `pwuser`, while the `devcontainer` stage of the template comes from `vscode`;
- an exception in Hard rules for `apt` packages.

— *Cost:* snapshots are promised «up to at least 2 years in the past», not forever. A snapshot that is no longer there will stop the build — then it is raised, like a version. — *Consequence:* the rule of exact versions in RULES.md names the snapshot; `canvas` already installs its packages this way (R13 canvas), and the other repositories get the rule with their move to a tag (RUN.md, Д15). — RULES.md, Hard rules; R34.

## The modules of the first slice

**R41. The first slice is three modules of two subjects: olympiad maths 1–6, school maths of grade 3 on a workbook, and short essays in English for any age.** О-1 is solved: instead of one second module, two.
- **Olympiad maths 1–6** is module 1 by R08: the learner is a child, the canvas is a handwriting sheet, the answer is a number or an option.
- **School maths of grade 3.** The learner is a child, the canvas is a workbook (concepts 8): the task's items stand on the non-erasable layer of the template, and the answer to each is a number or a fraction by hand in its answer slot. A verdict is given on each item (concepts 6, 9.2).
- **Short essays in English.** The canvas is a handwriting sheet, the essay is written by hand in free form. This is writing, not a language module: the explanations are in English, there is no target language (concepts 3).
  - AI reads the essay — reading of handwriting — and assesses it by the author's criteria — assessment by a rubric (concepts 10). The learner gets feedback by the rubric, not a verdict (R04).
  - Tasks with a key — for example, choosing the best first sentence — get a verdict.
  - The module is for any age, and the presentation style is by the learner's age (concepts 13). So an adult learner has a module of their own in the first slice, and the adult learner's account (R26) and the own key (О-4) stay in the slice.
- There are no third-party authors in the first slice (product 10), so all three modules are official. The canvases of the slice are the handwriting sheet and the workbook; there is no text canvas in it.
- The screens of the prototype — a page of ten examples on fractions and the essay «My best day» — are illustrations, not content: the solving steps, the traps and the topics are written by `modules` (R02).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22, by the screens of the prototype, which he updated the same day ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). The arguments are the plan's proposal:
- The main hypothesis — that AI understands the learner's free solution and reads the answer correctly (product 2) — all three modules test on handwriting: on a number on the sheet, on fractions in answer slots and on a whole text. The answers of Spanish — an edit and typing — a program would check without AI (architecture 4.2).
- The workbook brings what an olympiad task does not have: a task of many items with answer slots of their own on one sheet (concepts 6), the non-erasable layer of the template (concepts 8), the check kind "fraction and form" (concepts 9.2) and a series of items of one type that weighs less than the sum (concepts 11).
- Essays are the second subject and a path without a key: feedback by a rubric instead of a verdict (R04; product 4), the author's order for skills with a rubric (concepts 4, 5) and the learner's work as their artifact (concepts 8). One module serves both a child and an adult, with a different presentation style and different AI routes (R06, R07).
- The two maths give the first real reference between modules: the olympiad one rests on school skills only through the shared taxonomy (concepts 4; Т-14). In the prototype one module depends on another by package name, and the documents do not allow this ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)).

— *Rejected:*
- Spanish A1 for adults — the recommendation of О-1. Its answers do not test AI reading, it needs a text canvas of its own — a kind of its own on the page markup, not a sheet (R05 canvas) — and the step "pronounce" waits for voice input (О-6). It stays a module for later;
- olympiad maths and essays, without the workbook: format v0 would not meet tasks of many items with answer slots on one sheet;
- physics with a bench: it needs a widget, and widgets are stage 4 (architecture 3.4);
- school maths alone — a sheet with fractions, the third option of О-1: the format would be tested on one subject (R08).

— *Consequence:*
- R08 by an amendment: there are three modules, and still two subjects — maths and writing.
- The first slice has assessment by a rubric (architecture 3.6). What to measure it by is О-22. Whether feedback by a rubric affects the learner model is О-17, and it now concerns the first slice.
- An essay has no incorrect answers, and so no hint ladder (concepts 10): what a hint on request gives is О-21 and RUN.md, T30. The leak check has nothing to look for — there is no key — and the tutor must not write the essay for the learner (R05): how to hold this is decided by the detailing of assessment by a rubric (architecture 3.6).
- The path without AI — a typed answer or a choice (architecture 4.2; О-5) — the first slice tries only with tasks with a choice.
- An essay is the learner's free text: what the server keeps of an attempt is П-19, what a module may ask to write about is П-20, whether to keep the essays themselves is П-8.
- The text canvas, the check kinds "text" and "edit", and a language module where the target language is not the explanation language are not tested by the first slice. What happens to them in format v0 is decided by RUN.md, T29, and how a new canvas kind or check kind fits the format versions, by T23.
- The explanations of the essays module are in English. Translations in the module are RUN.md, T26, and the interface and explanation languages of the slice are О-2, which is open.
- The components that were planned for Spanish A1 get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д18.

— product 10, 13.1; architecture 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.10; repositories 2.1, 6.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* "Translations in the module are RUN.md, T26" was settled by R46: a module has one explanation language, and format v0 has no translations. The explanations of the essays module, as said above, are in English.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* what happens to "text" and "edit" in format v0 was decided by RUN.md, T29 (R56): neither is in v0. An edit needs an edit binding, which v0 does not have (R51), and signs and words written by hand are checked by a choice with the options in the check itself. There is no text canvas in the slice, and the recommendation of an input field without autocorrect (architecture 2.5 canvas) waits for it.


## Normative texts

**R42. The normative texts for authors are in English and outside `docs/`. The module format lies in the folder `format/` at the root of `spec`: the schemas, the format text and the test vectors.** О-3 is solved.
- The normative texts are what an author writes a module by, and what the platform's code reads and checks it by: the module format, the widget protocol and the guides for authors.
- **The module format** is the schemas with descriptions (Т-7), the format text and the test vectors of the format.
  - **The format text** is the rules that a schema cannot express: a graph without cycles, the references and keys that `module-kit` checks (architecture 3.7), the meaning of the check kinds and of normalization (concepts 9.2), open fields (R05), the format versions (Т-11).
  - The test vectors are normative: an implementation that does not pass them does not conform to the format.
  - The examples show the format and test the schemas, but add no rules.
- The format is normative: what a module may and must contain and how the platform checks it is said by the schemas, the format text and the test vectors, and `docs/` describe it. A divergence is an error, and one change fixes it. The field names are the English terms of concepts 15, and a new or changed term goes there first; a decision changes only by an amendment (RULES.md, How we work).
- `docs/` stay descriptive and in Russian (R14).
- The layout inside `format/` and the file names are decided by RUN.md, T24. Where the random generator and its test vectors lie — they are shared by `module-kit`, `engine` and `sim` (R27) — is decided by T32, and where the widget protocol and the guides lie, by epic E5. The language of all of them is this one.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22 by the recommendation of О-3: a standard that "any author" writes by cannot be in Russian only, and the descriptive documents stay in Russian. RULES.md already requires the descriptions of schemas in English, and the format text beside the schemas is changed by the same change as they are. The code of `module-kit`, which carries out the format, is in English too (R14). A separate folder is the plan's proposal: in `docs/` everything is in Russian (R14).

— *Rejected:*
- normative texts in Russian, like the documents (R14): an author who does not read Russian could not read the standard;
- only the descriptions in the schemas, without a format text: the rules that a schema does not express would live in the descriptive `docs/`, in Russian;
- the format text in English in `docs/`: the folder would mix language and role;
- two languages with a translation: at each divergence one would have to decide which of them is normative.

— *Consequence:* R14 by an amendment. The rule on language in RULES.md and rule 10 of RUN.md name the normative texts, repositories 5 the folder `format/`, and concepts 15 the terms "module format" and "format text". The folder appears with the first schema, and then CLAUDE.md names it too (RUN.md, T24). — repositories 5; RULES.md, Hard rules.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the format versions that the format text writes about were decided by R44 — the author's answer to Т-11. "The format versions (Т-11)" above reads "the format versions (R44)": the format text writes about them by R44, and its section on versions comes together with the folder `format/` (RUN.md, T24).

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the folder and its layout were decided by R45 — the author's answer to Т-7 and to the questions of T24.
- "The folder appears with the first schema" no longer holds: the folder `format/` appeared before the schemas, in RUN.md, T24, with the format text and the version number `format/VERSION`. The author agreed to this by approving the plan of T24.
- "The layout inside `format/` and the file names are decided by RUN.md, T24" is decided in R45.
- "The schemas with descriptions (Т-7)" in the item "The module format": Т-7 is closed by the same R45, and the schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the random generator and its test vectors lie in `format/`: in the [format text](../format/README.md), section 22, and in `format/vectors/random/` (R59): the generator belongs to the format version (R44), though both `engine` and `sim` take it.

— *Amendment 2026-11-12:* the documents of `docs/` are in English now, but for the epic archives `docs/plan/`: the 2026-11-11 amendment to R14 and R143 moved them, and T136–T139 of RUN.md translated them. "`docs/` stay descriptive and in Russian (R14)" above reads "`docs/` stay descriptive (R14)". What this entry decided holds: the normative texts are outside `docs/`, in their folders, and a divergence between them and `docs/` is decided by the normative text; the folder no longer separates the languages, only the roles.

## The first code of stage 2

**R43. The first code of stage 2 is the review board of `tutor`, and the large measurement of AI reading is put off until the author decides by the board's data.** The answer to the rows «в реестр spec» `tutor` В15 and В20 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 3660eac).
- **The review board** (R19 tutor). The author solves five fixed tasks by hand — sometimes with an error on purpose or illegibly. Two models of two providers read the solution and assess it themselves: correct, an error in line N, or cannot read. Under each answer the author marks whether the model is right, and the summary counts how often each is right. There is no program check on the board.
- **Where.** The command `tutor-eval board` — the eval CLI of `tutor` (R15) — listens only on the local address 127.0.0.1 in the devcontainer, and the page opens in the browser on the author's computer. This is not a service: `tutor` still has no process of its own (R15). The board has its own simple sheet, not the sheet of `canvas`.
- **Data.** The handwriting and the marks are only the author's own, an adult's. The pictures and the log lie with the author, outside git (R05 tutor), and the models are called with keys for eval only (R24).
- **The model's assessment on the board is what the board measures, not a verdict for a learner.** For the product, R03 and R04 stand: a program delivers the verdict. Whether to revisit them, the author decides by the board's data.
- **The large measurement** — about 110 sheets and statistics (architecture 3.1 tutor) — is put off: it will be returned to if the board shows that it is needed. What waits with it, rather than being cancelled: the release of `tutor` with the open views of the measurement's tasks for CI of `canvas` (the 2026-10-21 amendment to R25), the check of the synthetic samples of `canvas` in CI of `tutor` (R38), and the measurement's conclusions, by which Т-23 and О-8 are decided.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22 in `tutor` (R19 tutor): «на этапе MVP мне всего лишь нужно чтобы ты на канве показывал 5 статичных задач. Я сам буду их решать. Иногда специально ошибаться или писать неразборчиво. ИИ будет пытаться понять что я написал и выдавать свою оценку — решил правильно или с ошибкой. Далее я жму кнопку ИИ был прав или нет. Всё. Никаких проверок с твоей стороны не нужно вообще». The record in `spec` follows the recommendations of `tutor` in В15 and В20: the card and repositories 6 named as the first code of the stage what is put off, and `canvas` would build the samples page for a release of `tutor` that will not come for now.

## Versions of `spec` and of the module format

**R44. The module format has a version of its own, MAJOR.MINOR, and a module is checked, built and executed by the version its manifest names. A new version of the format opens a new line of `spec`. While the format is v0, the platform reads only its current version, and from v1 the current major and the previous one; v0 leaves the window with the release of v1.** Т-11 is closed.
- **Two versions.** The tag of `spec` is the version of the repository: of its documents, rules and recipes, and, once RUN.md, T35, brings them, of the release files too (R31). The module format version is the version of what a module may and must contain and how the platform checks it (concepts 15).
  - The number is written in `format/` once, in a place that does not change from version to version: a reader finds it before it knows the schema. Where this place is and how the `$id` of the schemas carry the number, RUN.md, T24, decides.
  - The module manifest names the number (concepts 3), and the attempt keeps it (architecture 1).
  - The format version has no patch. An edit of the descriptions, examples and words of the format text that does not change the rules, and a test vector that pins what is already written, do not change the number: such an editorial change is named by the tag of `spec`.
- **The line of `spec`.** Each release is the next patch of the line (R31), and a patch does not change the format version: in one line there is one format.
  - A pull request that gives the format a new version raises `RELEASE_LINE` in the same change.
  - While the format is v0, `spec` stays 0.x. Format v1 comes out with `spec` v1.0.0, and after that a major version of the format raises the major version of `spec` too.
  - R44 does not decide the versions of contracts and protocols, the contract `app` ↔ `api` among them: whether they raise the line, epics E3 and E5 decide.
- **What changes the format version.** The rule is one for everything the format sets: what a module contains and how it is checked, built into a package and an index, and executed — the check kinds and normalization, the generator and the derivation of seeds, the templates, the open view.
  - **A minor version** is an addition. After it, every module of the previous version passes the check and on the same inputs — module, seed, read value — gives the same verdict, open view and numbers, and a package and an index built by the previous version read as before. Such are an optional field — a new field is closed until it is opened explicitly (architecture 1) —, a new check kind or canvas kind, a tool, a value of a list, a parameter whose default value is the previous behaviour, and a new place of randomness that does not shift the numbers of the previous ones. A module that takes an addition names the new minor version.
  - **A major version** is everything else: a field removed, renamed or made required; what was correct became incorrect; on the same inputs another verdict, open view or other numbers are possible. So are changed the behaviour of a check kind (Т-18), the numbers of an existing place of randomness (R27) or the templates, and so is opened a field that was closed.
  - **The generator and the derivation of seeds** change by the same rule, wherever RUN.md, T32, puts them. In each format version the generator is one for the whole platform (R27), and the numbers of a module's template and widget depend only on the format version of its manifest. Whether the generator has a version of its own and which places of randomness it covers, T32 decides.
  - **While the format is v0,** compatibility is not promised, and any change of the format is the next version 0.y.
  - **The number of a released version does not go back** and is not reused: reverting a change is a new version too.
  - **An error of `module-kit`** that the test vectors catch is not a change of the format: an implementation that does not pass them does not conform to the format (R42).
- **A module is executed by the version of its manifest.** `module-kit` checks, builds and executes a module by the format version its manifest names.
  - A module takes only what its version has. A module of a version newer than those the release of `module-kit` knows is rejected with a reason.
  - A new format version changes neither the verdict, nor the open view, nor the numbers of a published module until the author moves the module to it. The move is a new version of the module: its manifest changed. Which version part of the module it raises, the semver rules of `module-kit` decide (T04 module-kit).
  - The canonical view and the package digest depend only on the module's sources and the format version in its manifest (RUN.md, T34). So the verdict, the open view and the numbers are decided by the package digest, not by the version the server chose (R03).
  - Within a major version the implementation is one — minor versions only add —, and `module-kit` holds no more than two: of the current major version and of the previous one.
- **Which versions the platform reads is the window.**
  - While the format is v0, only the current version 0.y. The official modules move to a new one in one pull request of `modules` (R18), and there are no third-party modules before v1 (product 10; repositories 6).
  - From v1, version v0 leaves the window. After that the window is the current major version with all its minor ones and the previous major one. The previous one leaves when the next major one comes out — by count, not by time.
  - The window is a rule for everyone who reads modules and packages. That is `module-kit` — in CI of `modules`, in `api`, in the eval runner of `tutor` and in CI of `canvas` (architecture 3.7); `sim`, which reads packages by the types of the canonical view (architecture 3.9); `app` and `canvas`, which get the open view by the types from the releases of `spec` (R36). A module of a version outside the window is rejected with a reason.
  - How a new version passes through the repositories is repositories 4.
- **The attempt and the replay of a verdict.**
  - The attempt also keeps the version of `module-kit`, as the engine choice keeps the versions of `engine` and `learner-model` (architecture 1). A fixed error of `module-kit` changes the verdict on the same inputs although the format is the same, and an exact replay takes the release that delivered the verdict.
  - An attempt begun on a version that has left the window, `api` no longer checks in its process. What to do with it, the detailing of `api` decides (architecture 3.5). The recommendation is as for a withdrawn version (Т-30): "unchecked" and a neutral phrase, since this is not the learner's error (R04).
  - A replay of the verdict for such an attempt goes outside `api` — by the release of `module-kit` that checked it.
- **The first version and v1.**
  - The first version is 0.1. The number appears with the first schema, and the version comes out with the first release of `spec` where the schemas are files for code (RUN.md, T35): the code of other repositories takes them only from there (R21). Until then the tasks of epic E2 edit 0.1 without raising the number, and the patches of line 0.2 carry its drafts. The rules of the number apply from the release of the version: before it, 0.1 is a draft, the format text calls it so, and the code of other repositories does not take it (R21). So the implementation knows only the released 0.1, and the number in code has one meaning: a module written by the draft is checked by the released version. That pull request raises `RELEASE_LINE` to 0.3, and from line 0.3 one line has one format.
  - The format becomes v1 by the author's decision — a record in this log —, when R08 is met: all three modules have passed through the platform without subject code in the core, and the success criteria of product 10 are met. v1.0 is the last version 0.y without what no module of the first slice took.
- **A new canvas kind or check kind** is platform code (R02) and an addition, that is, a minor version.
  - In v0 a kind may enter even without a module that takes it: RUN.md, T28 and T29, decide this.
  - Only what the modules of the first slice took enters v1. The text canvas and the check kinds "text" and "edit" (R41), if no module of the slice takes them, do not enter v1.
  - After v1 a new kind enters together with the module that needs it first.
  - A kind can be fixed later by a new kind or a parameter — a minor version, and the previous behaviour leaves with the next major one —, or by a major version.
- **What R44 does not decide:**
  - the versions of contracts and protocols — epics E3 and E5 decide them;
  - whether the vocabulary of the shared taxonomy (RUN.md, T27) and the eval set format (the eval protocol, epic E3) enter the format version: their tasks decide this by the rule above;
  - which format versions the publication of third-party modules accepts — the publication rules (О-9; epic E5).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22 in the planning of T23, by the plan's recommendations. Т-11 recommended semver, the format version in the manifest and support of the current major version and the previous one. The link with the line of `spec`, the execution by the version of the manifest, the rules of v0, the path of a new kind and the version of `module-kit` in the attempt are the plan's proposal. All sources were read 2026-10-22.
- **Two versions.** The tag of `spec` grows with every edit of a document: 21 releases, v0.2.0–v0.2.20, came out from 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22, and not one has a schema. A format version equal to the tag would change without the format. One line for everything does not do either: neither the contracts of E3 nor the widget protocol of E5 could raise it without giving the format a new version. So in Kubernetes too: "The API versioning and software versioning are indirectly related" ([Kubernetes, API Overview](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/#api-versioning)).
- **The link with the line** gives whoever takes `spec` one rule: within a line the format is the same.
- **Without a patch** — as in OpenAPI: "The `major`.`minor` portion of the version string (for example `3.1`) SHALL designate the OAS feature set. `.patch` versions address errors in, or provide clarifications to, this document, not the feature set" and "The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling" ([OpenAPI Specification v3.1.1, Versions](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html#versions)). An editorial change of `spec` is named by the tag anyway.
- **The execution by the version of the manifest** — as for a Go module by its `go` line: "A `go` directive indicates that a module was written assuming the semantics of a given version of Go", "Go toolchains refuse to use modules declaring newer Go versions" and "the compiler rejects use of language features introduced after the version specified by the `go` directive" ([Go Modules Reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-mod-file-go)). So Go 1.22 changed the meaning of loop variables: "the new semantics will only apply in packages contained in modules that declare `go 1.22` or later in their `go.mod` files", and "Old code will continue to mean exactly what it means today: the fix only applies to new or updated code" ([Fixing For Loops in Go 1.22](https://go.dev/blog/loopvar-preview), David Chase and Russ Cox, 2023-09-19).
  - The format is stricter than Go: Go changes meaning in a minor version too, and the format only in a major one. So `module-kit` has one implementation per major version.
  - R03 holds the package digest, not the server's choice, and an edit of behaviour reaches the learner through the module's CI — its check and eval set.
- **v0 without promises** — by semver: "Major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development. Anything MAY change at any time. The public API SHOULD NOT be considered stable", and "Version 1.0.0 defines the public API" ([Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), items 4 and 5). A window in v0 would be a cost without benefit: the official modules lie in one repository so that an edit of the format is one for all (R18), and there are no third-party ones before v1.
- **Only what is tested in v1** — the argument of R08 for a single kind: an abstraction without a consumer bends to the first one, and a kind can be fixed after v1 only by a new version.
- **The version of `module-kit` in the attempt:** without it a replay of the verdict would not tell a fixed error of `module-kit` from a change of the format.

— *Rejected:*
- one version, the line of `spec`: the format would take the line, and a breaking edit of a contract of E3 would come out as a patch;
- two independent versions, and the line at discretion, as before this record (R31): a breaking edit of the format could come out as a patch, and the line would not show whether the format changed;
- a patch for the format version: the tag of `spec` names an editorial change;
- execution by the newest version within its major one, with the version in the attempt: the verdict of the same module of the same version would change without its CI and eval set, and `module-kit` would keep the behaviour of every minor version for the replay;
- the window "current and previous" already in v0, as Т-11 recommended: `module-kit`, `sim` and the types of the open view would hold two versions each while the format changes most often, and there is nobody to move one by one;
- preliminary kinds — with a mark that a module takes explicitly, and outside the promise of compatibility, like the alpha versions of an API in Kubernetes: "Built-in alpha API versions are disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled in the `kube-apiserver` configuration to be used" and "The API may change in incompatible ways in a later software release without notice" (Kubernetes, API Overview). The mark would go into the schema and into `module-kit`, and a replay of the verdict would require behaviour for every minor version. The format already has a preliminary stage — v0;
- all of v0 into v1: a kind without a module would set untested.

— *Consequence:*
- Т-11 is closed (repositories 8). R21, R31 and R42 have amendments: the rules of format versions that they left to Т-11 are now here.
- concepts 3 and 15 — the module format version and its term. architecture 1, 3.5, 3.7, 3.9 and 3.10 — the execution by the version of the manifest, the window and the version of `module-kit` in the attempt; architecture 3.1 and 3.2 — the open view of the versions in the window at `app` and `canvas`. repositories 4 — how a new version passes through the repositories; repositories 5 — the normative parts come out with tags of `spec`, and the format has a version of its own.
- What R44 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-22, T23)» at table 1 of RUN.md:
  - the place of the number and `$id` — T24, the manifest — T26, the taxonomy — T27;

  - the release of 0.1, line 0.3, the check of the link with the line in CI and the types per version — T35;
  - the modules' requests — T38.
- The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д20.

## The module format: JSON Schema and conventions

**R45. The module format is JSON Schema 2020-12, and the author writes a module in YAML 1.2.2 with restrictions. The format text, the schemas, the examples and the test vectors lie in `format/` and are written by one set of conventions.** Т-7 is closed. Normatively the conventions are written in English in the format text, [format/README.md](../format/README.md), and here is what is decided, why, and what is rejected.
- **The schemas** are JSON Schema 2020-12, JSON files `format/schemas/<term>.schema.json`. The term is the English term of the part from concepts 15, in kebab-case; the common definitions of the parts lie in `common.schema.json`.
  - `$id` is `https://altnovatrail.github.io/spec/format/`, the number from `format/VERSION`, a slash and the file name. References between schemas are relative. An absolute reference to this prefix is forbidden: it would silently tie the schema to one version.
  - The root of a schema has `title` and `description`, each property has `description`, there too where it has only `$ref`; all in English (R42).
  - An object is closed by `unevaluatedProperties: false` in the schema that describes it whole in its place. A schema that another takes and extends — through `allOf` or through `$ref` beside its own `properties` — is open: closed, it would reject the fields of the extension. `additionalProperties: false` is not used: it does not see properties declared through `$ref` and `allOf`. A dictionary whose keys are data is set by `additionalProperties` with a schema and `propertyNames`.
  - A module is checked by the schemas of exactly its MAJOR.MINOR (R44). So an unknown field is an error, and a module does not take a field of a version newer than its own.
  - The check does not rest on `format`. A `pattern` is written only from the tokens that 2020-12 advises, without `\d`, `\w` and `\s`. The subschema `false` stands only at `unevaluatedProperties`.
  - Marks of our own carry the prefix `x-`, and the format text lists them. For now there is one mark — `x-open`.
- **The names** of fields and of the values of enumerations are the English terms of concepts 15 in snake_case: `answer_slots`, `trap_advice`. A field without a term — `id`, `title`, `version` — is a plain English word, an array is in the plural. A new term first enters concepts 15 (R42). A module writes the format version number as a string: `"0.1"`.
- **The author's YAML** is YAML 1.2.2 with the Core schema, and rules beyond it, each with an ID `yaml.<name>`:
  - UTF-8 without BOM; one document, `---` allowed at the start; without directives, anchors, aliases `*` and tags;
  - keys are strings: quoted or plain by the rule below, but not `null`, `true`, `false` and not a number. After escapes are processed they do not repeat;
  - the plain scalars `null`, `true`, `false` and JSON numbers are these values. A number fits in a double, an integer lies within ±(2^53−1), and `-0` is an error;
  - any other plain scalar is a string. It is not empty, does not start with a digit, `+`, `-`, `.`, `~`, `<` or `=`, and is not equal, case-insensitively, to `y`, `n`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `true`, `false` or `null`. Such a string is quoted;
  - strings hold no surrogates and no Unicode noncharacters, and no escape `\/`.

  Comments, block strings and flow collections are allowed. The order of keys carries no meaning, and the reader does not normalize Unicode. A file in JSON syntax is read by the same rules.
- **An open field** is marked by `x-open: true` in the subschema of a property under `properties`, `patternProperties` or `additionalProperties`, beside `$ref` if there is one.
  - A place in a module is open when its parent is open and it itself is an element of an array or is marked; the root of a part is open.
  - A mark counts only if its subschema applies and passes, in the branches of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `if`/`then`/`else` and `dependentSchemas` too.
  - The field by which an open object chooses a branch of `oneOf` is open.
  - Without the mark a field is closed, so a new field is closed until it is opened explicitly (architecture 1). The key or the predicate, the solution, the traps and the leak phrases are never opened (R05).
  - Opening a closed field is a major format version, and a new field open at once is a minor one (R44).
- **A format rule** is what a schema does not express: a graph without cycles, references, keys (architecture 3.7), and also the rules of YAML.
  - A rule has an ID `<part>.<name>` in kebab-case, where the part is the one in which the violation is reported, and a statement with the word MUST. The ID is not reused.
  - The rule is checked by `module-kit`, and its refusal names the ID. A new rule or one stricter than before is a major version (R44).
- **The test vectors** are normative (R42).
  - The vectors of a rule lie in `format/vectors/rules/<ID>/`. A case is a file, and if the rule links several files, a folder laid out as a module (RUN.md, T26). It passes the schema of its part and breaks only this rule; a vector of a YAML rule breaks only its YAML rule. CI of `spec` checks both, and CI of `module-kit` that the case is rejected with the rule's ID.
  - The valid examples meet the format rules that are checked within a part too, and CI of `module-kit` runs them as well. So each rule also has cases that it lets pass. A rule between parts is checked on examples laid out as a whole module (RUN.md, T26).
  - The vectors of the open view are in `format/vectors/open-view/` (RUN.md, T28); the verdict vectors — T29, of the open view of a template — T33, of the generator — T32, if it puts them in `format/`.
- **The examples** are `format/examples/<term>/valid/<case>.yaml` and `…/invalid/<case>.yaml`. A valid one passes its schema. An invalid one breaks one thing and names in its first line the error it must give: `# error: <keyword> at <place>`.
  - The place is a JSON Pointer in a URI fragment: `#` is the whole file, `#/answer_slots/0` an element. It is the place where the schema with this keyword applies. For `required`, `additionalProperties`, `unevaluatedProperties` and other keywords about an object the place is the object, for keywords about an array the array, for `type`, `enum`, `const`, `pattern` and other keywords about a value the value.
  - `$ref`, `allOf`, `properties`, `items` and `if`/`then`/`else` are not named: the keyword that failed inside is named. `oneOf` and `anyOf` are named when no branch passed.
  - The check looks for this pair among all errors of the validator, not for the text of the message: validators have different texts.
  - The examples show the format and check the schemas, but add no rules (R42).
- **The folder `format/`:**
  - `README.md` — the format text, in English, with normative words by BCP 14 and numbered sections;
  - `VERSION` — the version number, now `0.1` (R44);
  - `vectors/` will be started by RUN.md, T25: it writes the vectors of the YAML rules together with their check. `schemas/` and `examples/` will come with T26 and the following tasks.

  The folder and the number appeared in this task, before the first schema — amendments to R42 and R44.
- **What R45 does not decide.** The packages for code from the releases of `spec` are still R21, and how they come out, RUN.md, T35, decides. How the open view goes into the contract `app` ↔ `api` on protobuf, epic E3 will decide.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-22 in the planning of T24, by the plan's recommendations: Т-7, the version of JSON Schema, `$id`, the mark of an open field, the error of an example, YAML and the style of names. The rest — the rules for `$ref`, the closing of objects, `pattern`, the format rules and the vectors — is the plan's proposal after an independent review of the draft. All sources were read 2026-10-22.
- **JSON Schema 2020-12.** "The current version is 2020-12!" ([JSON Schema, Specification](https://json-schema.org/specification)). It is implemented by validators in both languages of the platform — `spec`, `canvas` and `app` are written in TypeScript, `module-kit` in Go:
  - ajv 8.20.0 under MIT: "Supports JSON Schema draft-04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12" ([ajv-validator/ajv](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv), README);
  - santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema 6.0.3 under Apache-2.0, whose README marks 2020-12 with a Bowtie badge ([santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema](https://github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema)).

  In draft-07 a mark beside `$ref` would be lost: "All other properties in a "$ref" object MUST be ignored" ([JSON Schema draft-07 core](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/draft-handrews-json-schema-01), §8.3). The author writes data, not API messages: JSON Schema checks the author's YAML directly and expresses enumerations, string patterns and conditions.
- **`$id`.** "Note that this URI is an identifier and not necessarily a network locator" ([JSON Schema 2020-12 core](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core), §8.2.1). The address of a project on GitHub Pages is "http(s)://<owner>.github.io/<repositoryname>" ([GitHub Docs, About GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/about-github-pages)): this is the organization's space, nobody else will take it. The address is hierarchical, so the references between schemas are relative, and the version number stands only in `$id`.
- **`x-open`.** "Unknown keywords SHOULD be treated as annotations, where the value of the keyword is the value of the annotation" (2020-12 core, §4.3.1). The next version of JSON Schema will not allow unknown keywords, and for user marks "the prefix `x-` has been selected" ([json-schema-spec, ADR 2023-04-sva-prefix](https://github.com/json-schema-org/json-schema-spec/blob/main/adr/2023-04-sva-prefix.md), accepted 2023-04-04). A mark in the schema itself will not diverge from the schema, as a separate list would.
- **The error of an example.** The output unit of 2020-12 names the keyword and the place: "The JSON key for this information is `keywordLocation`" and likewise "`instanceLocation`" (2020-12 core, §12.3). So the comparison does not depend on the texts of messages. The whole document in a URI fragment is `#` ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901), §6).
- **YAML.**
  - YAML 1.2 was conceived as a superset of JSON: "Its primary focus was making YAML a strict superset of JSON" ([YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), §1.2). Keys in it are unique: "each of the keys is unique" (ibid., §3.2.1.1). The Core schema is "the recommended default schema": a plain scalar that resembles nothing it reads as a string, while the JSON schema counts such a scalar an error, and then the whole text would have to be quoted (ibid., chapter 10).
  - Parsers read the same thing differently. `go-yaml`, which the YAML organization maintains, "Supports octals encoded and decoded as `0777` per YAML 1.1, rather than `0o777` as specified in YAML 1.2" and "Supports YAML 1.1 bools (`yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) as long as they are being decoded into a typed bool value" ([yaml/go-yaml](https://github.com/yaml/go-yaml), README, commit 32734c3), while the Core schema reads `0777` as 777. So the format leaves plain only the scalars that all read alike, and the others are quoted.
  - Characters, numbers and repeated keys follow I-JSON ([RFC 7493](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7493), §2.1–2.3):
    - strings "MUST NOT include code points that identify Surrogates or Noncharacters";
    - numbers no larger than a double allows, and integers in "[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]";
    - repeated names are counted "after processing any escaped characters".

    Then Go and TypeScript get the same JSON value from a file.
- **snake_case** — as the content of standalone, which is carried over into `modules`, writes: `grade_level`, `correct_answer`, `builds_on` (mathtrail-standalone, commit c6cbeb2). And as the fields of protobuf: "Use snake_case for field names, including extensions. Use pluralized names for repeated fields" ([Protocol Buffers Style Guide](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/style/)).
- **The normative words** follow BCP 14: they are normative "when, and only when, they appear in all capitals" ([RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)).

— *Rejected:*
- protobuf for the modules too — one format for everything, the second option of Т-7: the author would write the text format of protobuf or its JSON, and protobuf does not itself express enumerations, string patterns and conditions;
- draft-07: without `unevaluatedProperties` and `$defs`, and keys beside `$ref` do not act in it;
- `$id` on a domain of our own: there is no domain, and the purchase waits for О-16. If a domain appears before v1, `$id` moves to it with the next 0.y;
- `$id` as a URN: there are no relative references, and the version number would stand in every reference;
- a separate list of open fields — it is edited apart from the schema and can diverge from it;
- a JSON Schema vocabulary of our own with its own metaschema — it would have to be written and released together with the format;
- a file of expectations at the invalid examples — a second place that can diverge from the example;
- one keyword without the place — an example could fail not where it was meant to;
- YAML 1.2.2 Core without restrictions: numbers and booleans would depend on the parser, and anchors and aliases make a file not a tree;
- JSON only: without comments and multiline strings it is harder for authors to write, and `modules` already plans to write YAML;
- camelCase: standalone and `tutor` write in snake_case, and carrying the tasks over would rename every field;
- `additionalProperties: false` for closing an object — it does not see properties declared through `$ref` and `allOf`.

— *Consequence:*
- Т-7 is closed (repositories 8); amendments to R11, R42 and R44.
- CLAUDE.md, README.md and repositories 5 name the format text and the version number.
- concepts 1 and 15 — snake_case in the schemas; the terms "open field", "format example", "test vector" and "format rule", and with them "solution" and "leak phrase", which the format text names; "open view" — at any part of a module. architecture 1 and 3.7 — the open view by `x-open`, YAML with restrictions and the format rules by ID. repositories 3 — the vectors of the rules.
- What R45 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-22, T24)» at table 1 of RUN.md. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д21.

— concepts 1, 15; architecture 1, 3.7; repositories 3, 5, 8; RUN.md, T24.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* what the format check `just format-check` made precise (RUN.md, T25). The author's answer in its planning: where the check needs an exact reading, the format text gives it, together with the limits of Go for `pattern`. Version 0.1 is a draft until T35, and the number does not change (R44). Normatively the refinements are written in English in [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 4, 5 and 7.
- **The keywords of a schema** are only the list of the [format text](../format/README.md), section 5: the keywords of 2020-12 and `x-open`, and `$schema` and `$id` only at the root. The strict mode of `ajv` does not hold this: it lets through `nullable`, `definitions` and `dependencies`, which 2020-12 does not have. Of 2020-12, the list leaves out:
  - `$anchor`, `$dynamicRef`, `$dynamicAnchor` and `$vocabulary` — a reference names only `$defs`;
  - `minContains` and `maxContains` — `ajv` names their error `contains` (`dist/vocabularies/applicator/contains.js`, 8.20.0), and an invalid example would name a keyword the specification does not name;
  - `unevaluatedItems` — the test runner of `ajv` skips the cases of the JSON Schema suite where it meets `contains` (`spec/json-schema.spec.ts`, v8.20.0), and an array has enough with `items` and `maxItems`;
  - the content vocabulary — the format does not need it.
- **`$ref`** is one of three forms: `#/$defs/<name>`, `<file>.schema.json` or `<file>.schema.json#/$defs/<name>`. A ban on the prefix of `$id` is not enough: `../0.1/common.schema.json` would also tie the schema to a version, and `ajv` allows it.
- **`description`** is at the subschema of each field: under `properties` and `patternProperties` and at the schema of the values of a dictionary. A condition — what `if` and `not` hold — does not need it.
- **Closing is by place**, as the text said: "Only the schema at the object's place closes it".
  - A place is the root of a schema or a subschema directly under `properties`, `patternProperties`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `prefixItems` or `contains`, outside a condition. The entries of `$defs`, the targets of `$ref` and the branches of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `not` and `dependentSchemas` are parts of the place.
  - If the parts of a place describe an object, the place has `unevaluatedProperties: false`. `unevaluatedProperties` stands only at a place and only as `false`, and beside a `$ref` to an object there is the line `"unevaluatedProperties": false`. A dictionary is closed by `additionalProperties` with a schema and `propertyNames`.
- **A name from `if` or `not`** is declared also by a part of the place that always applies: the place itself or where its `$ref` and `allOf` lead. By 2020-12 a subschema that failed gives no annotations, while `ajv` counts a field of a failed `if` as evaluated when there is an `else`. The test runner of `ajv` skips this case of the suite: "unevaluatedProperties with if/then/else, then not defined" — "when if is false and has unevaluated properties" (`spec/json-schema.spec.ts`, v8.20.0). Without the rule, `spec` would let through a value that the validator of `module-kit` rejects by 2020-12.
- **`pattern`** — and the keys of `patternProperties`. Beyond the tokens of 2020-12 — so that Go and JavaScript, into which `ajv` compiles a pattern in mode `u`, read alike:
  - in a class `[` and `]` are escaped, `-` is first, last or between the ends of a range, a range is ascending, there is no empty class. Go reads `[]a]` as a class of `]` and `a` — "] and - are okay as first char in class" (`parseClass`) — and rejects `[^]`, while JavaScript rejects `[]a]` and accepts `[^]`;
  - outside a class `{`, `}` and `]` only in a quantifier or escaped: Go reads them as letters, while JavaScript rejects them;
  - a count has no leading zeros — "Disallow leading zeros" (`parseInt`): `a{01}` in Go is letters, and in JavaScript `a{1}`;
  - neither a count nor the product of nested counts is greater than 1000, and Go counts them so: `{x}` and `{x,y}` by the largest, `{x,}` by `x`, and `{0,}` as 1: "Implementation restriction: The counting forms x{n,m}, x{n,}, and x{n} reject forms that create a minimum or maximum repetition count above 1000" (`doc.go`; `repeatIsValid` in `parse.go`).

  Go — `src/regexp/syntax`, commit fb3c20e; JavaScript — `new RegExp(pattern, "u")` in Node 24 of the devcontainer.
- **`yaml.json-scalars`**: an integer is a number written without a fraction and an exponent, as go-yaml divides int and float. Any number is finite as a double, and precision is not a criterion: otherwise `0.1` would be a violation too. There is no negative zero in any notation, as there is no negative number that a double rounds to zero, such as `-1e-400`: it reads as the same −0.
- **`yaml.characters`**: an escaped surrogate is forbidden both in a pair and in the form `\U`. `yaml` joins a pair into one character, while go-yaml rejects any such escape: "found invalid Unicode character escape code" (`internal/libyaml/scanner.go`, commit 32734c3). Escapes are read from left to right, and `\\/` is a backslash and a slash.
- **Not YAML** — also a character outside the printable set of [YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), section 5.1, even in a comment. `yaml` lets through the C0 control characters and U+FFFE, while go-yaml rejects them: "control characters are not allowed" (`internal/libyaml/reader.go`, commit 32734c3). This is YAML itself, not a rule `yaml.*`.
- **The rules of a part** are listed in the [format text](../format/README.md) as a table whose first column is the ID, like the YAML rules in section 4. By the tables, `just format-check` matches the rules with their vectors.

*Why:* the author's answer in the planning of T25 and the review of the plan's draft by an independent agent: it found where the draft diverged from 2020-12, from `ajv` and from Go, and this was checked against the primary sources. All was read 2026-10-22.

*Rejected:*
- the rule of "extensible" subschemas from the draft: the branches of `allOf`, the targets of `$ref` beside their own fields and the branches at a schema with its own fields are open, and the other objects closed. It let through an open object — `if`, `then` and `else` without fields of their own — and rejected a lawful one — a common base with `oneOf` —, and an edit of the base in one file pulled edits of places in others;
- a dynamic probe — an unknown field in each object of the valid examples: it sees only what is in the examples;
- the strict mode of `ajv` instead of the list of keywords;
- an integer by value: then `1e300` too would be an integer out of bounds;
- snake_case for the values of `enum` too: they hold `"0.1"`, SPDX identifiers and BCP 47 tags;
- to leave the text as it is and put what is disputed into an open question: the check and the text would say different things.

*Consequence:* `just format-check` checks all this, and T26–T34 write the schemas so. The components get the amendment together with R45 (RUN.md, Д21). — [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 4, 5, 7; RUN.md, T25.

The check of the conventions and the open view still go through the branches of `dependentSchemas`, so what stands in them is checked too, and a new amendment will lift the ban when `ajv` fixes the errors and the test says so.
