## Module manifest and layout

**R46. A module is a folder: the manifest `manifest.yaml`, the files of its parts, `media/`, `eval/` and an optional `NOTICE`. The module ID is `<publisher>/<name>`, skills, tasks, traps, techniques and lessons have a local ID, and the module version is semver `X.Y.Z`. A module has one explanation language.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T26. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10 and 11, and in the schemas `common.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **Identifiers.**
  - The module ID is `<publisher>/<name>`, both in kebab-case starting with a letter: `novatrail/olympiad-math`. A publisher owns the namespace of its modules, so the module IDs of two authors will not coincide (concepts 3).
  - A skill, a task, a trap, a technique and a lesson have a local ID: kebab-case starting with a letter, no longer than 64 characters, unique within its kind inside the module. The module's files name its parts only so.
  - The full ID is the module, the kind and the local ID joined by `/`: `novatrail/olympiad-math/skill/counting-gaps`. The kinds are `skill`, `task`, `trap`, `technique` and `lesson`. The learner model, the engine and progress know a part of a module by its full ID, and the module's files do not hold it.
  - Neither the publisher and the name in the module ID nor a local ID is ever the name of a Windows device — `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`: a local ID becomes a file name, and a module ID may become a folder path.
- **The module version** is semver `X.Y.Z`, as a quoted string, with no pre-releases and no build metadata. To allow them later is to widen the pattern, and that is a minor format version (R44).
- **The layout.** A module is a folder, and what lies in it is set by the table of the format text: the path, the part the schema checks, and what is in the file.
  - `manifest.yaml` is the manifest; `media/` holds pictures and sound; `eval/` is the eval set, and its format will come with the eval protocol (epic E3); `NOTICE` holds the license notices and is optional.
  - A part of which a module has one is a file in the root, named by its term: `skill-graph.yaml`. Parts of which a module has many — tasks and lessons — lie in a folder, a file for each: the file is named by its local ID and carries it in the field `id`. So the open view and the canonical view get the ID from the part itself. The rows of the layout come with the tasks of their parts, T27–T33, and the rule "a file's name is its `id`" with the first such part, T28.
  - Names are compared exactly as the folder lists them, case-sensitive. Files and folders starting with `.` are not part of the module, a folder without files holds nothing, there are no symbolic links, and the order of files carries no meaning.
  - Where the module's folder lies and what it is called, the format does not say: `modules` decides that (architecture 3.10).
- **The manifest** is `manifest.yaml` by the schema `manifest.schema.json`, and all its fields are open:
  - `module_format_version` — the format version, as a string: `"0.1"`. It stands in the root of the manifest in every format version (R44), and the schema gives it the pattern MAJOR.MINOR, not a single value. A version the reader does not read is rejected by the rule `manifest.format-version`;
  - `id` and `version`; `title` — in the explanation language;
  - `subject` — the subject code: `mathematics`, `physics` or `writing`. `physics` is for the manifest of a third-party module, as in concepts 16.3. A new code is a new value of the list, that is, a minor version (R44), and v1 will hold only the codes of the modules of the first slice;
  - `audience.age_categories` — a non-empty list without repeats of the age category codes of concepts 13: `under_13`, `from_13_to_consent`, `from_consent_to_18` and `adult`. The platform offers the module only to learners of these categories (privacy 3.2);
  - `languages.explanation` — the explanation language, and `languages.target` — the target language, only in a language module. A language is a BCP 47 tag of the language, the script and the region, and the script and the region are optional. The case of letters is as in the registry: `en`, `zh-Hans`, `pt-BR`, `es-419`. The schema checks the form of the tag, but not that it is in the registry;
  - `authors` — a non-empty list of `{ name }`;
  - `license` — an SPDX identifier: letters, digits, `.` and `-`; the official modules have `Apache-2.0` (R20). Whether it is in the SPDX list, the schema does not check.
- **One explanation language per module** in v0. All the module's texts are in it, except the material of a language module: that is in the target language. There are no translations in format v0, and the same content in another explanation language is another module, with its own ID and its own progress. Translations later are most likely files by language on top of the module's texts. That is an addition, a minor version, and earlier modules do not change.
- **Media files** are PNG, JPEG, WebP and MP3, with one extension for each format: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp` and `.mp3`. A part refers to a file by its path from `media/`: names in kebab-case joined by `/` and an extension, no longer than 128 characters — `pictures/ladder.png` (`media_path` in `common.schema.json`).
- **Rules.** The rules of the whole module have the part `module`, and it has no schema of its own:
  - `module.manifest` — the module's folder has `manifest.yaml`;
  - `module.layout` — every file stands at a path of the layout table, and the module holds nothing but files and folders.

  A module may break both rules — for example, with `Manifest.yaml` instead of `manifest.yaml` — but each vector breaks exactly one. What lies in `media/` the rule `module.media` will say (T28). The rules `module.manifest` and `module.layout` and the manifest's rule `manifest.format-version` `just format-check` checks itself, like the YAML rules, and it reads the layout table from the format text.
- **Examples and vectors.**
  - An example of a whole module is a folder `format/examples/module/valid/<case>/`, laid out as a module: the files with a part pass their schemas, and the module breaks no rule. There are no invalid examples of a whole module: a module that breaks a rule is a vector of that rule.
  - A vector of a rule that links files is a folder laid out as a module. A vector of a rule of the whole module breaks only that rule, and a vector of a part's rule passes the rules of the whole module and holds the file of its part.
  - The manifest in an example and a vector names the version from `format/VERSION`, except the vectors of `manifest.format-version`: they name a version outside the window of the reader of this version (R44). One names `"0.0"`, which the format never had, the other the next minor version.
- **Common definitions** are `common.schema.json`: the format version, the module ID and version, the local ID and, on it, the ID of a skill, a task, a trap, a technique and a lesson, the language tag, the license, the age category, the subject, the media file path, and text — a non-empty string. The patterns are of the subset of R45: with classes, without `\d` and `(?:`.
- **What R46 does not decide:**
  - translations — and what they will have to cover: leak phrases, the keys of text answers, the open view, the types of `app` and `canvas`;
  - the presentation style — О-23;
  - the field `dependencies` and the grade as a label of the module and a starting point — RUN.md, T27, together with the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary. This departs from «Сделать» of T26: «зависимости от общей таксономии — поле»;
  - the rule `module.media` with file signatures and binary vectors, the rule of the file name of a part, and standalone's description pictures — T28;
  - what goes into the module package — `NOTICE` and the license text — T34;
  - who may publish under which publisher — the publication rules (О-9) — and which licenses third-party modules carry (О-10);
  - SPDX expressions such as `MIT OR Apache-2.0` and BCP 47 tags with variants and extensions: to widen the pattern later is a minor version.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-22 when planning T26, by the plan's recommendations: the form of the ID, a module as a folder, one explanation language, the presentation style outside the manifest, `dependencies` with T27 and `module.media` with T28. The rest — the manifest's fields, the rules and the layout of the vectors — is the plan's proposal after an independent check of the draft. All sources were read 2026-10-22.
- **A local ID, and the full ID outside the module.** A module's file does not repeat its module's ID in every reference, and renaming the module does not touch its files. The full ID is needed where parts of different modules lie side by side: in the learner model, the engine and progress.
- **A folder, not one file.** The olympiad maths module has 603 tasks (product 10). In one file an edit of a task is an edit of the whole module, and in a folder of one file, and a pull request of `modules` shows it separately. A file per task, not per topic as in standalone (c6cbeb2): a topic is a label of the task, and a task that changes its topic does not move.
- **The format version as a pattern.** A single value, `const`, would reject the manifests of the earlier version already in the schema of the next minor version, though a minor version only adds (R44). A refusal by version is a rule with its own vectors, and the reader names its ID.
- **The case of language tags.** BCP 47 compares tags without case: "language tags and their subtags, including private use and extensions, are to be treated as case insensitive", but "The format of subtags in the registry is RECOMMENDED as the form to use in language tags" ([RFC 5646](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646), §2.1.1). The format takes the registry's form, and one tag is always written as one string.
- **semver:** "A normal version number MUST take the form X.Y.Z where X, Y, and Z are non-negative integers, and MUST NOT contain leading zeroes" ([Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), item 2). The regular expression of its FAQ writes `\d` and `(?:`, which the `pattern` subset of R45 lacks, so the pattern is written with classes.
- **SPDX.** An identifier is "idstring = 1*(ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." )" ([SPDX License Expressions](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/annexes/spdx-license-expressions/)); the list is SPDX License List 3.29.0 of 2026-09-16 ([spdx.org/licenses](https://spdx.org/licenses/)).
- **The media formats** are those every browser shows ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/), mdn/content, `main` 8bc3252):
  - PNG, JPEG and WebP — "All versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, and Safari" ([Image file type and format guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Image_types));
  - MP3 — "MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III) is supported by all major browsers" ([Web audio codec guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Audio_codecs)).
- **The names of Windows devices** — "Do not use the following reserved names for the name of a file: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1, …, LPT9 … Also avoid these names followed immediately by an extension; for example, NUL.txt and NUL.tar.gz are both equivalent to NUL", and also "Do not assume case sensitivity" ([Microsoft, Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file), revision of 2024-08-28). Hence IDs and names in lowercase only, and names compared by the folder's listing.
- **`NOTICE`** is for the notices that licenses require to be kept. Apache-2.0: "If the Work includes a "NOTICE" text file as part of its distribution, then any Derivative Works that You distribute must include a readable copy of the attribution notices contained within such NOTICE file" ([Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), section 4(d)), and the recipient gets a copy of the license too: "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), section 4(a)). MIT: "The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software" ([MIT License](https://opensource.org/license/mit)). standalone's tasks are under MIT, and whether to keep their notice or to re-release the content under Apache-2.0, `modules` decides (RUN.md `modules`, T03).

— *Rejected:*
- full IDs in the module's files, as in the illustrations of concepts 16: every reference would repeat the module's ID;
- IDs in standalone's styles — `logic.knights_liars`, `off_by_one`, `cal-12-d1-1` (c6cbeb2): an ID becomes a file name, and one style is needed. Carrying over standalone's IDs — `.` and `_` into `-`, with a check for collisions — is the work of `modules` (RUN.md, Д22);
- a module as one file and tasks in groups by topic, as in standalone;
- translations in the module at once: what they are to cover is not decided, and to add them later is a minor version;
- the presentation style in the manifest: there is no list of styles either in the documents or in the components, and a field without a list would fix only a name (О-23);
- `dependencies` in a temporary form now: T27 decides the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary, and an edit of the temporary form would be breaking;
- `const` for the format version — the argument above;
- SVG: it is code that the browser draws, and the ban on scripts in it is "For security purposes, some browsers place restrictions on SVG content when it's being used as an image. Specifically, the following limitations may apply: JavaScript is disabled" ([MDN, SVG as an image](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Guides/SVG_as_an_image)): "some" and "may" are no promise;
- AVIF: "As support is not yet comprehensive (and has little historical depth) you should provide a fallback in WebP, JPEG or PNG format" (MDN, Image file type and format guide);
- Opus and Vorbis in Ogg: "Safari 18.4+ (on macOS 15.4+, iOS 18.4+, iPadOS 18.4+, and visionOS 2.4+) added support for Opus and Vorbis codecs in Ogg containers" ([MDN, Media container formats](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Containers)) — devices older than that will not play them;
- `.jpeg` beside `.jpg`: two extensions of one format would give one file two names;
- SPDX expressions now: О-10 is open, and one license is enough for the official modules.

— *Consequence:*
- concepts 3, 13 and 15 — the module ID, the local ID, the full ID, the module layout, the subject, the audience, the explanation language, the target language, the license notices, the age category codes and the field `module_format_version`. О-23 is in product 13.2; architecture 3.10 — what is inside the module's folder.
- Amendments to R41, R44 and R45: translations, the place of the format version in the manifest and the layout of folder vectors were decided by R46.
- What R46 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-22, T26)» at table 1 of RUN.md. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д22.

— concepts 3, 13, 15; product 13.2; architecture 3.10; [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 10, 11; RUN.md, T26.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* of what R46 left to RUN.md, T27, the grade as a label of the module was decided by R49 — the field `audience.grades` —, and the starting point by grade comes with the scale of task difficulty in RUN.md, T28. The field `dependencies` and the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary are decided by RUN.md, T42: when planning T27 the author split the shared taxonomy off into that task.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* the field `dependencies` and the form of the dictionary's ID were decided by R50 (RUN.md, T42). `dependencies` is a non-empty list without repeats of the anchor skills on which the module's skills rest: exactly those that the skill graph names as prerequisites — this is the rule `manifest.dependencies`. The ID of an anchor skill is `core.<name>`. An anchor skill is not part of a module and has no full ID: outside a module the same ID names it. Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10 and 11.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* what R46 left to the task RUN.md, T28, was decided by R51.
- The layout row `tasks/<id>.yaml` and the rule `module.file-ids`: a file at a path with `<id>` carries that name in the field `id`. The rule `module.media`: a file in `media/` stands at a path of the form `media_path` and begins with the signature of its format. Both, like `module.manifest` and `module.layout`, `format-check` checks itself.
- A skill, a task, a trap, a technique and a lesson are in the format text an "entry" of the module, not an "item": an "item" is an item of a task.
- The manifest got the difficulty bands `bands` and the digit height on the crop `canvas.digit_height`, and with them the rule `manifest.bands`.

Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10 and 11.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the layout rows `traps.yaml`, `techniques.yaml` and `solving-steps.yaml` (R57). These are parts of which a module has one each — files in the root: the solving steps are named by their term, and a catalog by the entries it holds, in the plural. A published ID of a trap, like that of a skill, never names another trap: the learner's progress counts traps by their full IDs. The manifest got the rung templates `rung_templates`, and with them the rule `manifest.rung-templates`.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the layout row `lessons/<id>.yaml` (R58): a module has many lessons, and each has its own file, named by its ID, as tasks do.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the module layout holds a required `LICENSE`, the text of the license the manifest names, with the rules `module.license` and `module.plain-text`: `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` are UTF-8 without a BOM, and lines end with a single LF. Both go into the package byte for byte, in the device part, and the notices the licenses require stand only in `NOTICE`: comments of the module's files do not get into the package. The eval set is not part of the package. So the item "what goes into the module package — `NOTICE` and the license text" of "What R46 does not decide" is answered. — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **the format of the samples of `eval/` is the eval protocol, not the module format:** which files of `eval/` are samples and what is in them is said by the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), sections 11 and 13 (R95). A sample is every file under `eval/` whose name ends in `.json`. The layout `eval/<path>` does not change, and the format gets no new version: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 10, is amended in words only.

## AI providers and age

**R47. Google's generative AI is closed on the platform — both the Gemini API and Vertex AI: for all learners on both AI routes and for the other parts of the platform — until a lawyer answers otherwise.** The author's answer to the `tutor` row В5 «в реестр spec» (RUN.md `tutor`, commit 3029dfb), by its recommendation.
- **What the terms say.** Google Cloud's Service Specific Terms, section "20. Generative AI Services", item "d. Age Restrictions": "Customer will not, and will not allow End Users to, use a Generative AI Service as part of a website, Customer Application, or other online service that is directed towards or is likely to be accessed by individuals under the age of 18". Item "f. Suspected Violations": "Google may immediately suspend or terminate Customer's use of a Generative AI Service based on any suspected violation of … subsection (d) above" — a reference to another item of the same terms is left out ([Google Cloud Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms), "Last modified October 12, 2026").
- **Vertex AI is generative AI of these terms.** Among the Generative AI Services is "Generative AI on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Generative AI on Vertex AI)", and also "Generative AI Services also includes any generative AI features or functionality of a Service" ([Google Cloud Platform Services Summary](https://cloud.google.com/terms/services), "Last modified October 21, 2026"). Both pages were read 2026-10-22.
- **What follows from it** is our conclusion, not a legal one, as in privacy 5.3. The condition concerns the service as a whole, as for the Gemini API in the AI Studio variant, and NovaTrail is open to children (R06). So Google's models are closed for all learners, adults too — both through platform AI and with an own key: with an own key the key's owner accepts the terms, but the service in which the call runs is still NovaTrail.
- **Not only learners.** The condition speaks of the service, not of who calls the model. So a part of the platform that serves not learners — for example, the authors' pipeline of stage 4 — takes no Google models either: it goes to AI providers through `tutor` (architecture 3.13).
- **What is open** is for a lawyer, together with П-3: whether Google's models are allowed in a separate deployment or service for adults only. Until the answer the route is closed.

— *Why:* the recommendation of `tutor` in В5. privacy 5.3, checked 2026-10-18, wrote of Vertex AI: «В Service Specific Terms такой фразы не нашлось». But item (d) is there, and with the same text it stood already in the revision of 2024-07-18: `tutor` checked it by the archive of the terms 2026-10-21 (architecture 4 tutor). The study "A child's handwriting on the canvas and the AI tutor" («Рукопись ребёнка на канве и ИИ-наставник»), by its own reading, also not a legal one, comes to the same (ibid.). And item (f) lets Google stop the service on a mere suspicion: a platform that kept learners on Google's models would risk this AI route as a whole. The item "Not only learners" is the executor's proposal, by the same reading of the condition.

— *Rejected:*
- Google's models in a separate deployment for adults — now: by the study's reading the ban concerns a platform open to children as a whole, and that is a question for a lawyer (П-3);
- asking Google for an exception, and leaving the route open until the answer: the answer would come when learners' data had already gone;
- closing Google only to learners and leaving it to the other parts of the platform: the condition is about the service, and they are parts of the same NovaTrail.

— *Consequence:*
- privacy 2, 5.3 and 10, П-3, Т-20, product 6 and architecture 3.6 speak of Google by R47. Without Google the platform keeps OpenAI and Anthropic: privacy 5.3 has not checked other providers yet.
- R07 does not change: "The providers' rules about age are kept" — R47 applies it.
- `tutor` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д26. The measurement is not affected: Google was removed from it already on 2026-10-21 (R06 tutor).

— privacy 2, 5.3, 9, 10; product 6; repositories 8; architecture 3.6, 3.13; RUN.md, Д26.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **the Prompt API in Chrome — Google's generative AI on the device, Gemini Nano — is closed too, by this decision.** The author's answer to the `tutor` row В27 «в реестр spec» (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), by the recommendation of `tutor`; reading on the device is R66.
- On Chrome's pages about this API `tutor` found no age terms, and it did not read Google's general terms, to which their footer refers. For the same model on Android, the [ML Kit GenAI terms](https://developers.google.com/ml-kit/genai-terms) say: "You must be 18 years of age or older to use the APIs" (architecture 2.6 and 4 tutor, T44; read by `tutor` 2026-10-25).
- Until a lawyer's answer (П-3) the route is closed, like Google's models in the cloud. Besides, this API has no tablets and no Russian (ibid.).

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. This is Google's generative AI in a service open to children, and the terms of the same model require 18 years. *Rejected:* leaving the route open until Chrome's terms are checked: the terms of the same model on Android require 18 years, and the route would open to children at once.

*Consequence:* privacy 5.3; `tutor` closes В27 — RUN.md, Д47.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **"until a lawyer answers otherwise" is read by R112, and the answer is that Google's models stay closed, including in a separate deployment for adults only: it would do only as a truly separate service, and Google may stop a service on a mere suspicion. Return if a product for adults only appears. The part of П-3 about Google is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 when planning T94 (RUN.md), by the analysis's recommendation (R112). Read 2026-11-09: [Gemini API Additional Terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) — a redirect to the [Google AI Studio terms](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms), "Effective March 23, 2026" — the text on age is the same as in privacy 5.3, and beyond it — "Use of Google AI Studio and Gemini API is for developers building with Google AI models for professional or business purposes, not for consumer use"; [Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms), "Last modified October 30, 2026", in "20. Generative AI Services": "d. Age Restrictions" is the same, and "f. Suspected Violations" is "Google may immediately suspend or terminate Customer's use of a Generative AI Service based on any suspected violation of `Section 17(b)` or subsection (d) above"; [Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service](https://cloud.google.com/terms), "Last modified October 12, 2026": ""Customer Application" means a software program that Customer creates or hosts using the GCP Services", and para. 3.3(d)(iii) forbids "creating multiple Customer Applications, Accounts, or Projects to simulate or act as a single Customer Application, Account, or Project". Each text judges a separate site, application or service, and "likely to be accessed" is defined nowhere. — *Rejected:* allowing Google's models in a deployment for adults on conditions — its own project, domain, accounts and build — and with a second admission table for it: a deployment with shared code, content and modules is easily held to be one service, and a suspension on suspicion would close it too. — privacy 5.3; П-3.

## Status badges

**R48. The README of every repository carries MathTrail's status badges — up to 14 in two rows, and a badge stands only when what it speaks of exists. Coverage goes to Codecov by OIDC, without a secret, and `codecov/patch` ≥ 90 % holds the merge; OpenSSF Best Practices comes first at `spec`.** The author's answer to Т-34 when planning T39 (RUN.md), 2026-10-23.
- **The set** is as at mathtrail-standalone (`main` c6cbeb2) and canvas-api (0901af0). The first row is CI, Release, CodeQL, the release number, the language, coverage, OpenSSF Best Practices, OpenSSF Scorecard and the license; the second is the five measures of SonarCloud: code smells, reliability, security, maintainability and vulnerabilities. The addresses, the captions and when which badge appears are in repositories 2.3.
- **A badge stands only when what it speaks of exists**: no "no releases", no "not found", no "unknown".
  - From day one, from the template: CI, CodeQL, Scorecard, the license and SonarCloud's measures. In all 13 repositories they work already now. A new repository gets their answers when it is set up to the end: with the shared checks (repositories 2.2), a SonarCloud project (R30) and the first run of Scorecard.
  - Release and the release number come with the first release, the language with the first code, coverage with the first upload to Codecov, Best Practices with the passing level.
  - These badges are put up by the repository's own session, as is what code adds to the CI files (the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30).
- **Coverage goes to Codecov by OIDC, without a secret:** "Any token supplied will be ignored, as Codecov will default to the OIDC token for verification. Note that the codecov action must have write permission for `id-token` for this to work" ([codecov/codecov-action, README](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/blob/v7.1.1/README.md), tag v7.1.1). Only the upload job gets the permission `id-token: write`.
  - A pull request from a fork does not get this permission, and Codecov accepts its upload even without a token: "Codecov should work smoothly on pull requests from forks out of the box" ([Codecov Tokens](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-tokens)).
  - An upload for `main` without OIDC Codecov will not accept if the organization's settings turn on the token requirement: "For public repositories, a token is required if the upload is for a commit on a protected branch and the repository owner has not disabled token authentication for public repositories". The author turns it on: a new organization by default has "new organizations will start with tokens Not required" (ibid.).
- **`codecov/patch` holds the merge:** the changed lines are covered at least 90 %, as in R38 standalone. It is a required check of the ruleset of every repository whose coverage goes to Codecov, and `codecov/project` only reports. The amendment to R30 is given by T40, when the check appears at `spec`.
  - The cost: no upload means no status, and the merge waits. This happens when Codecov fails, and for a Dependabot pull request if GitHub does not give it OIDC; whether it does is not checked yet. How such a pull request does not get stuck, T40 decides.
- **OpenSSF Best Practices.** The project on bestpractices.dev is set up by the author, signing in through GitHub (rule 4 of RUN.md). First `spec` (T41), then every repository with code and automated tests: without them the passing level cannot be had.

The changelog of 2021-10-06 says that such runs "will begin to respect the permissions specified in your workflows" ([GitHub Changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2021-10-06-github-actions-workflows-triggered-by-dependabot-prs-will-respect-permissions-key-in-workflows/)). And the page of the workflow syntax does not name this exception: "Workflow runs triggered by Dependabot pull requests run as if they are from a forked repository, and therefore use a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions-for-workflow-runs-triggered-by-dependabot)). ## Skill graph

**R49. The skill graph is the file `skill-graph.yaml`: the module's skills are a dictionary by local ID, with a title, a description, prerequisites and assessability. The tier is computed from the graph, and the author gives the tiers names. The mapping table is `retired_skills`, and the grade is the label `audience.grades` in the manifest.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T27; О-18 is decided. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 11 and 12, and in the schemas `skill-graph.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **The skill graph** is `skill-graph.yaml` by the schema `skill-graph.schema.json`.
  - `skills` — the module's skills under their local IDs: `title`, an optional `description`, `prerequisites` and `assessability`. Prerequisites are skills of the module, and all are needed: "to take on B, you need A". Skills outside the module — the anchor skills of the shared taxonomy — come with RUN.md, T42.
  - A module has one graph or none, and a module without a graph is without skills.
  - Rules: `skill-graph.acyclic` — prerequisites make no cycle, and a skill that names itself as a prerequisite is a cycle too; `skill-graph.known-skills` — a prerequisite and a skill in `replaced_by` are skills of the module; `skill-graph.retired-ids` — the ID of a retired skill does not name a skill of the module. `module-kit` checks them, and `spec`'s CI checks the YAML and the schema of their vectors ([format text](../format/README.md), section 9).
  - `tiers` and `skills` with all the skill's fields are open: by them the app draws the skill map. `retired_skills` is closed: the server transfers progress.
- **The tier (О-18)** is computed from the graph and is not written in the module. A skill without prerequisites among the module's skills has tier 1, the others 1 above the highest tier of their prerequisites in the module. So the tier is the number of skills in the longest chain of prerequisites that ends in the skill, and a prerequisite always stands a tier lower. There is no limit on the number of tiers. `module-kit` computes the tiers when it builds the package (architecture 3.7).
  - Names for the tiers are an optional list `tiers` in the explanation language: the first name is tier 1's. A tier without a name is shown by its number, and a name past the last tier names nothing.
- **A skill's assessability** is one of three: `verdict` — the skill's tasks are checked by a key or a predicate, and their verdicts are evidence for the learner model; `rubric` — on the skill the learner gets feedback by a rubric, without a verdict; `none` — the skill is trained but not assessed. The engine adapts to the learner only for a skill with `verdict` (concepts 4).
- **Retired skills are a mapping table.** A published ID of a skill does not name another skill, and a skill whose meaning changed gets a new ID: a change of meaning cannot be seen from the module. `retired_skills` are the skills of earlier versions that the module no longer has, under their earlier IDs, and each has `replaced_by`, the skills of this version that replaced it:
  - a renamed one has one skill, a split one several, and merged ones each name the same one;
  - `[]` — nobody replaced it, and the progress in it passes to no skill;
  - if a skill from `replaced_by` is later retired itself, the record names its replacement instead;
  - the evidence of a retired skill goes to each skill that replaced it, and with what weight `learner-model` decides (architecture 3.8);
  - the record stays in all the following versions, so that progress of any age passes over. To retire a skill is a major change of the module (concepts 3).

  That each skill of the earlier version stayed in the module or was retired, and that no record went missing, is seen only by comparing two versions. They are compared by `diff` of `module-kit` (T04 module-kit), and its rules will come to the format text as a row «в реестр spec».
- **The grade** is the module's label `audience.grades`: school grades from 1 to 12, as the module's author counts them; the platform does not convert one country's grades into another's. A module with grades asks the learner's grade, and the answer may be outside the list. Unlike the age categories, the grade closes nothing: a skill opens by its prerequisites (concepts 4). The starting point by grade — a point of the scale of task difficulty — comes with that scale (RUN.md, T28). There is no grade 0 and no grades above 12 in version 0.1: to add them later is a minor version (R44).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 when planning T27, by the plan's recommendations: the tier is computed, and the author gives the names; the table is `retired_skills`; the grade is a label now, and the starting point comes with T28; three values of assessability; the MIT notice in the example; the shared taxonomy as a separate task T42. The rest — a dictionary of skills instead of a list with `id`, the rule `retired-ids`, a name past the last tier, an optional graph, `minItems` and `minProperties` — is the plan's proposal after an independent agent checked the draft. All was read 2026-10-26.
- **The tier is computed** — as in standalone: "a topic's layer is the longest chain of bases below it — 0 the foundations, 1 the rules, 2 the hard problems — computed rather than drawn" ([SPEC.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/SPEC.md), section 8.12.2, line 1706; commit c6cbeb2). Tiers that the author types R164 standalone rejected: "layers typed by hand, which drift from the links" ([docs/decisions.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/docs/decisions.md), ibid.). A computed tier will not drift from the graph.
- **There is no depth limit.** standalone's map draws three layers, the catalog's test keeps chains within three, and for that one edge is not drawn: "a link from divisibility would make a fourth layer through calendar and divisibility, and the map draws three" (R164 standalone). And an edge is a teacher's judgement: "which topic is a good base for another is a teacher's judgement the data only supports" (ibid.). The format should not fit the graph to the map's drawing, and the map can fold the far tiers into a row, as the prototype does ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)).
- **The author gives the tiers names** — as in the prototype: the module Goroutines has its own steps — Basics, Waiting, Many goroutines and Review — and the caption is "Step N · name" or, without a name, "Step N" (`draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`). The olympiad module has standalone's names: Foundations, Rules, Hard problems.
- **Three values of assessability.** A key and a predicate both give a verdict, and the engine and the learner model behave the same with either. And for a skill that is trained by tasks both with a key and with a predicate, none of the four values of the table of concepts 4 would be right.
- **A dictionary of skills by local ID.** The uniqueness of IDs is held by the rule `yaml.unique-keys`, not by a rule of its own, and the order of skills carries no meaning, like the order of keys (R45).
- **The table is in the graph, with skills without replacement too.** A skill retired without replacement is recorded in the same place as the others, and its ID is protected from reuse too. standalone has no mapping table.
- **The grade is a point on the ladder of tasks, not at the skills.** In standalone the grade decides one thing: "Start is where a child of this grade begins: the shift of the level the grade falls into. It is the one thing the grade decides" ([`internal/domain/rating/ladder.go`](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/internal/domain/rating/ladder.go), commit c6cbeb2), and a task's level is "the band of grades it is written for" (SPEC 1.1 standalone). So the starting point is given by the scale of task difficulty (T28), and the label is needed already now: by it the app asks the grade (privacy 4).
- **The MIT notice** on the example of the olympiad graph is by R12: "MathTrail's code under MIT carries over freely: MIT is compatible with Apache-2.0, and the MIT notice is kept". standalone's topics and their links are under MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 MathTrail" ([LICENSE](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/LICENSE), commit c6cbeb2). A file `NOTICE` beside the example `format-check` would not accept, so the notice stands in the example's opening comment.

— *Rejected:*
- the author sets the tier: it would drift from the graph, which is what R164 standalone warns against;
- computing the tier, but no deeper than three, as standalone's map: the graph would be fitted to the drawing;
- tiers without names: the steps that the module names itself would be lost;
- four values of assessability — key, predicate, rubric and none;
- skills as a list with a field `id`, as in the illustration of concepts 16.3: the uniqueness of IDs would be held by a rule of its own;
- `formerly` — a list of earlier IDs on the new skill: a skill retired without replacement is recorded nowhere, and its ID has nothing to protect it;
- the table as a separate file `skill-mapping.yaml`: a layout row of its own, and the references to skills a rule between two files;
- everything about the grade in T28; grades on skills, like the `grade_levels` of standalone's topics: there the starting point was given by the level of tasks, not by the grades of topics;
- an example without standalone's topics, and their re-release by the author under Apache-2.0;
- the graph and the shared taxonomy as one task — by rule 11 of RUN.md.

The [format text](../format/README.md), section 9, now says what `spec`'s CI checks and what `module-kit`'s CI checks: the graph's rules are the first that `format-check` does not check itself.
- What R49 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-26, T27)» at table 1 of RUN.md, and the shared taxonomy by RUN.md, T42. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д30.

## Shared taxonomy

**R50. The shared taxonomy is a dictionary of anchor skills in the module format: the schema `format/schemas/shared-taxonomy.schema.json`, where each anchor skill is a branch of `oneOf` with the ID `core.<name>`, a title and a description. A module's skill rests on an anchor skill as a prerequisite and teaches it with the field `teaches`, and the manifest names the anchor skills on which the module's skills rest in `dependencies`. The dictionary is part of the format version.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T27, and the task T42 recorded them; Т-14 is closed. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), section 13, and in sections 2, 11 and 12, and in the schemas `shared-taxonomy.schema.json`, `skill-graph.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **The dictionary** is the format's schema `shared-taxonomy.schema.json`. Its instance is the ID of an anchor skill: at the root a string and the form of the ID, and each anchor skill is a branch of `oneOf`, where the ID is `const`, the title `title`, the description `description`. An ID that is not in the dictionary the schema itself rejects. It describes no part of a module and is never a module's file: it is referred to by the parts that name anchor skills. The platform curates the dictionary, in `spec`.
- **The ID** is `core.<name>`, where the name is in kebab-case starting with a letter: `core.multiplication-table`.
  - The dot separates the namespace: the ID of an anchor skill cannot be confused with a local ID or with a module ID, which have no dots.
  - The ID has no subject: a module of any subject may rest on an anchor skill.
  - The ID is the same in a module and outside it. An anchor skill has no full ID: it is not part of a module, and the learner model, the engine and progress know it by this ID.
- **The title and the description** are English text of the schema, not text of a module: an anchor skill has no explanation language. The description says what a learner who knows the skill can do, and it is normative: it is the meaning of the anchor skill.
- **Where a module names anchor skills:**
  - in a skill's prerequisites — what it needs. A prerequisite is a skill of the module by its local ID or an anchor skill by its own ID: in the schema this is an `anyOf` of the two;
  - in a skill's `teaches` — what it teaches: a learner who knows the skill can do what the description of each anchor skill says. One anchor skill may be taught by several skills of one module or of different ones;
  - in the manifest's `dependencies` — what the module's skills rest on. A module whose skills need no anchor skills does not write the field. So one manifest shows what the module rests on.
- **Rules:**
  - `skill-graph.own-anchors` — a skill does not name as a prerequisite an anchor skill that a skill of the same module teaches, itself included. A skill that needs what its own module teaches names the module's skill: so the module's graph holds this link, and the tiers and the check of cycles see it;
  - `manifest.dependencies` — `dependencies` names exactly the anchor skills that the prerequisites of the module's skill graph name: each, and no other. The rule links two files, and its vectors are folders laid out as a module.

  `module-kit` checks them, and `spec`'s CI checks the YAML and the schemas of their vectors ([format text](../format/README.md), section 9). Anchor skills do not count toward the tier: they are not skills of the module, and a skill all of whose prerequisites are anchor skills stands in tier 1.
- **Versions.** The dictionary is part of the format version (R44):
  - a new anchor skill and the mark `"deprecated": true` are a minor version: a module may name a marked anchor skill until a major version removes it;
  - the removal of an anchor skill and a change of its meaning are a major one. The meaning under the same ID does not change: a skill with a new meaning comes under a new ID, and the earlier ID is removed;
  - other words of the same meaning in the description are an editorial change, without a new version;
  - the ID of an anchor skill is not reused;
  - v1 holds only the anchor skills that a module of the first slice names.
- **The learner model and the engine.** Whether a learner knows an anchor skill `learner-model` decides by the skills that teach it, in the learner's modules (architecture 3.8). An anchor skill that no module of the learner teaches does not hold back a skill that needs it: the engine counts it as unknown (concepts 4). The format checks each module separately, so it does not see a cycle of prerequisites between modules through anchor skills.
- **The first anchor skills** are `core.multiplication-table`, `core.division-with-remainder`, `core.fractions-of-a-whole` and `core.linear-equations`. In the format's examples the first three are taught by the school mathematics of grade 3, and the olympiad one rests on division with remainder and fractions of a whole. The fourth is taken by no module of the slice: it is for the third-party module of concepts 16.3, and it will not enter v1 unless a module of the slice takes it (R44).
- **What R50 does not decide:**
  - how a third-party author proposes an anchor skill of their own — that is the publication rules (О-9);
  - the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill — RUN.md, T34;
  - whether a supporting skill of a task may be an anchor skill, as in concepts 16.3 — RUN.md, T28;
  - how `learner-model` derives knowledge of an anchor skill from the skills that teach it — and from skills with `rubric` or `none`, which have no verdict (О-17) — and what the engine does with a cycle between modules: that is their detailing (architecture 3.8);
  - which version part of a module an edit of `teaches` or `dependencies` raises — the semver rules of `module-kit` (T04 module-kit). To remove `teaches` is to take an anchor skill away from the modules that rest on it;
  - translations of the titles and descriptions of anchor skills: there are no translations in format v0 (R46).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 when planning T27, by the plan's recommendations: the dictionary as a schema of the format, an anchor skill as a branch of `oneOf`, the ID `core.<name>`, the dictionary in the format version, the prerequisite and `teaches` on the skill, `dependencies` in the manifest and the first four anchor skills (RUN.md, T42, «Решено автором»). The rest — the rules `skill-graph.own-anchors` and `manifest.dependencies`, the meaning of `teaches`, the tier without anchor skills and what an anchor skill means for the learner model and the engine — is the proposal of the plan of T27, which the author approved. All was read 2026-10-26.
- **A schema, not a data file.** An unknown anchor skill the schema itself rejects, and no format rule of its own is needed for it. `const` "is functionally equivalent to an "enum" … with a single value" ([JSON Schema 2020-12 validation](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation), §6.1.3), and a branch of `oneOf` carries a title and a description besides: "A title will preferably be short, whereas a description will provide explanation about the purpose of the instance described by this schema" (ibid., §9.1). The mark `deprecated` in a branch concerns only its own anchor skill: it "applies to each instance location to which the schema object containing the keyword successfully applies", and it means that "applications SHOULD refrain from usage of the declared property. It MAY mean the property is going to be removed in the future" (ibid., §9.3). The dictionary goes into the releases as one more schema, together with the others.
- **The prerequisite and `teaches`** are as in schema.org. `teaches` — "The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term", and `competencyRequired` — "Knowledge, skill, ability or personal attribute that must be demonstrated by a person or other entity in order to do something such as earn an Educational Occupational Credential or understand a LearningResource". Among the values of both is `DefinedTerm`, a term of a vocabulary ([schema.org, teaches](https://schema.org/teaches) and [competencyRequired](https://schema.org/competencyRequired), V30.1 of 2026-09-16). So both what a skill needs and what it teaches are linked to an anchor skill.
- **Modules only through the dictionary**, as Т-14 recommended (concepts 4). In the prototype a module rests on another module by the package name and a range of versions — `math-g3 ^1.5` ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)) —, and then renaming or retiring a skill in one module would break another. An anchor skill a module will neither rename nor retire.
- **`dependencies` is exactly the anchor skills of the graph's prerequisites.** A list that the author writes by hand beside the graph would drift from it, as tiers typed by hand would drift (R49). The rule holds them together, and the manifest shows what the module rests on, without the graph.
- **The tier is without anchor skills.** The tier is difficulty within a module (R49), and an anchor skill from another module would shift the tiers, though nothing changed in the module itself.
- **A new meaning is a new ID**, as for a module's skill (R49). The learner model knows an anchor skill only by its ID, and from v1 the platform reads two major format versions at once (R44): if the meaning changed under the same ID, the evidence of the earlier meaning would count toward the new one. This reading of the author's answer «удаление и смена смысла — мажорная, ID не переиспользуется» was proposed by the review of T42.

— *Rejected:*
- the ID `core.<subject>.<name>`, as in the illustration of concepts 16.3: the subject would bind the anchor skill to itself forever;
- a data file `format/shared-taxonomy.yaml` with a schema of its own: it needs code of `format-check`, a rule for an unknown anchor skill and a second file in the release;
- the shared taxonomy as one task with the skill graph — by rule 11 of RUN.md;
- dependencies without a field in the manifest, which `module-kit` computes into the package, like the tier. The field in the manifest the author decided (R46; RUN.md, T42, «Решено автором»): the manifest shows what the module rests on, without the graph, and the rule `manifest.dependencies` — the plan's proposal — does not let the field drift from the graph.

— *Consequence:*
- Т-14 is closed (repositories 8). Amendments to R44 — the dictionary in the format version —, to R45 — the dictionary's schema describes no parts, and `teaches` is a link named by a verb —, to R46 — the field `dependencies` and the ID of an anchor skill — and to R49 — a prerequisite may be an anchor skill.
- concepts 3, 4, 11, 15 and 16.3 — the anchor skill, module dependencies, the prerequisite and the shared taxonomy; architecture 3.7 and 3.8; repositories 5 — the dictionary in `format/`.
- RUN.md, T34 — the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill (the record at table 1). The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д31.

— concepts 3, 4, 11, 15, 16.3; architecture 3.7, 3.8; repositories 5, 8; [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 2, 3, 5, 10–13; RUN.md, T42, Д31.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* a supporting skill of a task may be an anchor skill, and the primary one only a skill of the module (R51; RUN.md, T28). An anchor skill that a skill of the same module teaches the task does not name; it names that skill — the rule `task.own-anchors`, like `skill-graph.own-anchors` for prerequisites. A supporting anchor skill does not enter `dependencies`: it still holds what the graph's prerequisites name.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill was decided by R63: each record of the index has `teaches`, the anchor skills that the skills of its graph teach. "RUN.md, T34" about the index in "What R50 does not decide" and in "Consequence" reads as RUN.md, T44 and R63. — R63; RUN.md, T44.

## Task

**R51. A task is a file `tasks/<id>.yaml`: the task statement, the canvas, the items with their answer slots, the skills, the band and the difficulty, and where needed the age categories it suits. A module's difficulty scale is the bands in the module manifest, and the digit height on a crop is there too. An item's key is RUN.md, T29. The rule `module.media` checks the media files, and `spec` builds the open view itself.** The author's answers in planning RUN.md, T28. Normatively this is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 6, 9, 10, 11 and 14, and in the schemas `task.schema.json`, `manifest.schema.json` and `common.schema.json`; here is what is decided, why, and what is rejected.
- **A task** is `tasks/<id>.yaml` by the schema `task.schema.json`, and its `id` is the file's name without `.yaml`: the rule `module.file-ids`. An item's key or predicate — the check kind — RUN.md, T29 will add, and until it the tasks of the examples have no keys: version 0.1 is a draft (R44).
- **The task statement** is parts in order: a paragraph `text` or a picture.
  - A paragraph is plain text in the module's explanation language. There are no formulas and no sound in a statement in v0: each will come with a minor version.
  - A picture has `picture`, a path in `media/` to a PNG, JPEG or WebP file; `alt`, what is on it in words: a screen reader reads it, and it stands in the picture's place until the picture has arrived, and it is empty only for a decoration; `width` and `height`, the size in CSS px.
  - The statement is part of the author's template, which the learner neither erases nor changes. Whether it is above the canvas or on it, the canvas kind decides: the handwriting sheet shows it above the sheet (R23 canvas). This answers В34 `canvas`, and concepts 6 and 8 are amended.
- **The canvas belongs to the task,** one for all the items. `kind` is `handwriting_sheet` or `workbook`.
  - The handwriting sheet is 1000 × 1400 units from the top left corner, and the size is a constant of the kind (R06 canvas). The task gives it a grid `grid` — `squares`, `lines` or `dots`, without the field squares — and its step `grid_step` from 20 to 500 units, without the field 50.
  - The workbook is a page of lines, a line per item, and how the lines lie on the page is decided by `canvas`.
  - Every task has a pen and an eraser. There is no field of tools in v0: it will come with a minor version, with the first module that needs a ruler or a calculator.
- **Items and answer slots.** An item is named by its place in the task, from 1, and an answer slot by its place among the item's slots.
  - On the sheet, an item has slots `answer_slots` and, where needed, `text`: what it asks, "a)".
  - In the workbook, an item is a line `line`: pieces of text and boxes in order, at least one box, and a box anywhere — "7 × [ ] = 56", "56 [ ] 65", "[ ] apples". The line's boxes are its answer slots. A two-storey fraction and column arithmetic will come later, and what cannot be written so, RUN.md, T38 will gather.
- **The bindings of v0** are what the three modules of the slice need:
  - `anywhere` — anywhere on the sheet: AI finds the final answer (R61 canvas-api);
  - `sheet` — the whole sheet, the work as a whole, like an essay;
  - `zone` — in a zone: a rectangle of the sheet, `left` and `top` from the left and top edges, `width` and `height`, in units of the sheet. The names are not `x` and `y`: a plain `y` breaks `yaml.plain-strings`;
  - `choice` — a choice among the options `options`: two or more, without repeats, in order;
  - `box` — a box of a workbook line.

  On the sheet, `anywhere`, `sheet`, `zone` and `choice`; in the workbook, `box`. A slot `anywhere` or `sheet` is the only one in its task: AI would not tell two final answers "anywhere" apart. Keyboard input, an edit in a text and a widget's state will come later, with a minor version, and v1 will take in only what a module of the slice took (R44): nobody takes `zone` yet.
- **Skills** — `primary`: the module's skills by local ID that the task trains, and a wrong answer is evidence against them; `supporting`: the skills the answer needs and that a wrong answer does not lower — skills of the module or anchor skills. An item's own `skills` replace the task's skills for it.
- **The difficulty scale is bands and a difficulty inside a band, as in standalone.** The module manifest lists the bands `bands` in order, from the easiest: `id`, `title` and, for a module with grades, `grades`. A task names its band `band` and its difficulty `difficulty` from 1 to 5 inside it. A learner of a grade starts in the band of their grade; where a learner outside the bands starts and how far apart the bands are, `learner-model` decides.
- **The digit height on a crop** is `canvas.digit_height` in the module manifest: whole px from 1 to 256, without the field 32. The setting is one per module, and how the app gets it with a task RUN.md, T34 decides. This answers В38 `canvas` in its part on the digit height.
- **A task's age categories** are `age_categories`: fewer than the module's, and the platform gives the task only to learners of those categories. This is the mark that П-20 awaited: a module can give a topic about the learner's life to adults alone.
- **There is no provenance in a module:** everything in a module comes from the author, and a task has no field for it. A key from the solver will come with the templates (RUN.md, T33), and "entered by an adult" and "derived by AI" are the provenance of tasks from paper (О-11), which modules do not have.
- **standalone's pictures** are files in `media/`: in the port, `modules` draws them into files with a description (RUN.md of `modules`, T03). Kinds of pictures that `canvas` draws will come later, with a minor version.
- **Open and closed.** Open are `id`, the statement, the canvas and the items with all their fields: the app shows them. Closed are the skills, the band, the difficulty and the age categories: the server reads them. Opening a field later is a major version (R44).
- **Rules:**
  - of the module manifest — `manifest.bands`: if bands are written, their IDs differ; in a module with grades each band names its grades, and each grade of `audience.grades` is in exactly one; in a module without grades the bands name no grades;
  - of a task — `task.known-skills`, `task.skill-roles`, `task.own-anchors`, `task.known-band`, `task.known-pictures`, `task.age-categories` and `task.zones`; zones touching at their edges is not an overlap. `module-kit` checks them, and the CI of `spec` checks their vectors' YAML and schemas;
  - of the whole module — `module.file-ids` and `module.media`. These, like `module.manifest` and `module.layout`, `format-check` checks itself.
- **Media files** go by the signatures of [WHATWG MIME Sniffing](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/), "Last Updated 19 October 2026", read 2026-10-26: PNG — `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`, JPEG — `FF D8 FF`, WebP — "RIFF", four bytes and "WEBPVP" (§6.1); MP3 — "ID3" or a frame header of layer III (§6.2). The signature is what `module.media` reads: the rest of the file is the author's concern.
- **The open view** `spec` builds itself: the vectors `format/vectors/open-view/` and their check in `format-check` (the amendment to R45).
- **What R51 does not decide:**
  - the key, the check kinds, and whether a skill's assessability matches how its items are checked — RUN.md, T29;
  - traps, the solution, hints, the givens and the unknown — RUN.md, T30;
  - templates and the key from the solver — RUN.md, T33;
  - how the app gets the digit height and the explanation language with a task — RUN.md, T34;
  - sound and formulas in the statement, the field of tools, styling for the learner's interests and kinds of pictures that `canvas` draws — with minor versions, with the module that needs them;
  - what a module may ask a learner under 18 to write about — П-20 and epic E4.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 in planning T28 — sixteen, all by the plan's recommendations but the first: the author kept the task as one (RUN.md, T28, «Решено автором»). The rest — the rules, the forms of the schema, the names of the fields, the check of the media and of the open view — is the plan's proposal after an independent agent checked the draft. All read 2026-10-26.
- **Bands and difficulty are as in standalone,** commit c6cbeb2: "a task has a level — the band of grades it is written for — and a difficulty inside that level" ([SPEC.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/SPEC.md), section 1.1), and the starting point is the band of the grade: `Start(grade)` in `internal/domain/rating/ladder.go` returns the offset of the band the grade falls in. The bands are 2.5 apart and overlap: a task's hardness there is its band's offset plus the difficulty minus 3. One scale of rungs would not express the overlap, and the numbers are the model's business, not the format's.
- **The term is "difficulty band":** "level" in concepts 11 already means the learner's level, and a term means one thing.
- **The bindings follow the slice.** Anywhere on the sheet is as in canvas-api: «Поля ответа нет: ребёнок решает и пишет итоговый ответ где угодно на листе … а итог находит модель» ("There is no answer field: the child solves and writes the final answer anywhere on the sheet … and the model finds the final answer") ([docs/decisions.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/blob/0901af0/docs/decisions.md), R61 canvas-api). The box is for the workbook, the whole sheet for an essay, and the choice for the assignments with a key among the essays and for standalone's tasks: there an answer is always a choice among five options. What the slice does not take will not enter v1 (R44), and so it is not in v0 either.
- **The workbook line** is the author's answer: a box in a workbook example happens both at the start and in the middle, and text and boxes in order write any such example without a markup language.
- **The statement above the sheet** is how `canvas` shows it (R23 canvas), and, by В34 `canvas` (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 5feb06f), so do the others: "So in canvas-api — «текст над листом, а не часть листа» ("the text above the sheet, not a part of the sheet"), — on the review board of `tutor` and in the prototype of `spec`". The picture's description and size are also by В34: without a description a picture that has not arrived cannot be read, and without a size the sheet shifts under the pen when it arrives.
- **The skills are closed:** a skill's title — "gaps and posts" on a task about a staircase — hints at the way to solve it, and R05 closes what gives that away. Opening it later is a major version, and then it will also be decided what to show before the solution.
- **There is no provenance:** standalone has none either — "Nobody else's wording, anywhere. The ideas come from open sources; the text is ours" (SPEC 1.5 standalone) —, and the tasks that AI helped to write the author checks before publication (concepts 9.3).
- **Pictures are files:** standalone's 13 kinds of pictures are drawn by its card — "an object of one of thirteen kinds, which the card draws as SVG" (SPEC 4.4 standalone). Taking them into the format would mean 13 schemas and 13 drawers in `canvas` for the sake of one module, while a file with a description any browser shows.
- **The open view goes by the annotations of 2020-12:** the definition "a mark counts only where the subschema passes" is exactly the collection of annotations by the 2020-12 core, §7.7.1.2, and the two implementations — `format-check` and `module-kit` — are compared by the vectors.
- **Two bugs of `ajv` 8.20.0** were found in this task. `unevaluatedProperties` counts a place's fields as unevaluated when beside it stands `dependentSchemas` without its own key, or `$ref` together with `oneOf` or `anyOf` whose passing branch is not the first. By 2020-12 such a part is valid, while `format-check` would reject it. The format's schemas take neither, and a test of `format-check` pins the behaviour of `ajv`: if it changes, the test will say so. What to do about this further is the question В25 of RUN.md.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **the default digit height is 24 px, from format version 0.2.** The author's decision on the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В39 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its third option. It differs both from the recommendation of `tutor` and from the rule that `tutor` wrote down before the run: that gave 16 px (R48 tutor).
- **The measurement of E4 `tutor`** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера чтения» and «Итог замера тетради»; R37 and R42 tutor). The heights 16, 24 and 48 px were compared with 32 px in pairs, by sheets, without the key, on Haiku 5.5 · `low` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking:
  - on 68 test sheets, 16 and 24 px are no worse than 32 px on both. 48 px on Haiku · `low` is worse: 12 extra "unreadable" against 5, p 0.033. There were no other errors at the heights;
  - on 15 test workbook pages, 16, 24 and 48 px are also no worse than 32 px on both, and there are no new false "correct";
  - a sheet's picture at 16 px is about 90 tokens against about 200 at 32 px. The crop of a workbook box at 16, 24 and 32 px is one and the same: 200 × 200, 64 tokens.
- **Why 24 and not 16.** The handwriting of the measurement is synthetic data, even and large, while live handwriting is smaller and less even: 24 px leave a margin. The gain in price at 16 px is small — the whole input about 1,300 tokens against 1,400. On sheets with lowercase letters the digits on a crop are, besides, larger than the height from the module manifest (RUN.md, epic E3, the crop rule).
- **When this enters the format.** A new default value changes the behaviour of a module without the field, and that is a new format version. "A minor version only adds", and of default values the text puts among the patch changes only "a parameter whose default keeps the previous behaviour" ([format text](../format/README.md), section 2; R44). So 24 px come with version 0.2, in a new line of `spec`, and a task of its own makes it — RUN.md, T48. Until then a module of format 0.1 without the field is read at 32 px, and `canvas` without a module manifest draws the crop at 32 (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R36).
- **Recheck** on the handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16) before the modules of the slice come out without the field (R48 tutor).

*Why:* the author's decision: the middle between the rule's advice and the former height (R48 tutor). To record the decision now and to make format 0.2 task T48 is also the author's decision: the format version is in about 140 examples and vectors of `format/`, and the digests of the package and index vectors depend on it.

*Rejected:*
- 16 px — the advice by the rule, but checked only on synthetic data;
- keep 32 px — 24 px is no worse on both parts of the measurement;
- 24 px in format 0.1, without a new version: R44 does not allow it;
- format 0.2 in the same change as this amendment.

*Consequence:* RUN.md, T48 — format 0.2. `canvas` takes 24 px with format 0.2, `tutor` closes В39 — RUN.md, Д47.

So it did not wait for 0.2 and comes with the same tag as this amendment (the 2026-11-01 amendment to R44).

*Rejected:*

- leave it as it is: on dark paper the picture will not be seen;
- a MUST rule instead of a SHOULD.

## The course of writing and AI

**R52. Nothing of the learner's writing history goes to AI — neither the order of writing, nor the action log, nor the frames before erasure, neither into reading nor into analysis: what goes to the check is an image or a crop, as by R09. So it stays until a measurement on live handwriting and free notation shows that the course of writing helps.** П-21 is closed. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В30 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **What the measurement of `tutor` measured**, 2026-10-26 (R24 and R27 `tutor`; architecture 3.1 tutor, «Итог замера»). The model assessed the finished sheet — `correct`, `error` or `unreadable` — and placed the box of the first error. This went in one call: the model saw the key and the reference solution, as on the review board (R43). By the vocabulary of `spec` this is reading and analysis in one call (architecture 3.6; Т-23), and there was no reading without the key in the measurement. What П-21 calls the course of solution is the course of writing: the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures, what is not on the final image (R55). The forms are the four options of П-21:
  - (A) only the final image;
  - (B) the image and the action log: the lines in the order of writing, pauses from 6 s, erasures and returns to a line — without time, pressure, coordinates and what was erased;
  - (C) the image and up to two frames before erasure: on a frame is what was erased itself;
  - (D) both.

  There are 40 sheets, 30 of them test sheets, with 3 repeats per form. The judges are Opus 5.5 · `high`, Haiku 5.5 · `low` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking. The criterion was written down before the first run: form D against form A by sheets, the exact sign test, the threshold p < 0.05. Forms B and C against A the measurement counted without a threshold.
- **The answer by the criterion is "not shown" for all three judges.** On 30 test sheets, 90 answers per form, A → D:
  - Opus 5.5 · `high` — correct 90 and 90, false alarms 0 and 0;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` — correct 84 and 72, false alarms 3 and 9, p "harms" 0.10;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking — correct 65 and 77, false alarms 14 and 8, p "helps" 0.061.

  There is no false "correct" in any answer. Of the comparisons without a threshold, «Итог замера» names one thing for forms B and C: the log without frames gave a false alarm less often for Haiku without thinking — 14 in A, 5 in B and 8 in D. But even in D this judge is right less often than Haiku · `low` by the image alone: 77 against 84.
- **The measurement's caveats.** 39 sheets of the 40 were drawn by code (R26 tutor): the handwriting is even, without blots, and the erasures are exactly to plan. The solutions are written in lines from top to bottom, and there is no free notation — a number line, a drawing, a note at the side — on the sheets. Opus is right already by the image alone, and a help from the course of writing is not visible for it on these sheets by construction. The call "analysis of the course of solution and the hint" with a trap and a rung (architecture 4.1) the measurement did not measure: the model only assessed the sheet and looked for the first error.
- **So** the rule of the recommendation of П-21 applies: of the kinds that give the same benefit, take the one poorest in data. The benefit of the course of writing is not shown: form D, which has both the log and the frames, gave it to no judge, and the log and the frames separately were not measured by the criterion. So one image goes to AI — both into reading and into analysis. R09 and privacy 4 do not change. The check request in the contract `app` ↔ `api` (RUN.md, epic E3) carries the work as an image or a crop, without fields of the course of writing. `tutor` already reads the work by one final image (R27 tutor), and nothing changes in the code.
- **A measurement is not a check of a learner.** The measurement samples from adults carry a writing history (П-18), and the next measurement of `tutor` sends the model the forms with the course of writing — that is how it measures. R52 is about a learner's work that the platform checks.
- **When to return** — with the measurement of `tutor` on the live handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16) and on free notation: it is the first item of epic E4 of RUN.md of `tutor`, and there the answer "not shown" may become another. If a kind beyond the image shows a benefit, it will come with a new decision. As before, it needs an amendment to R09 and privacy 4 and the lawyer's answer: how to count «процесс картинками» and a trace without time and pressure (the recommendation of П-21).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 — option (a) of `tutor` in В30. The argument of `tutor`: the recommendation of П-21 came true in its part on reading, while nobody has yet measured the benefit of the course of writing in analysis. A frame before erasure carries what was erased itself, and the log the order and the pauses of the learner's writing: without a shown benefit there is no reason for them to go to the provider (privacy 1).

What the measured call is named is the executor's proposal, named in the question to the author. R27 `tutor` and the row В30 call this call reading. But the model in it saw the key and the task's solution and looked for the first error, and by architecture 3.6 that is the work of analysis, only in one call with reading (Т-23). So the argument of `tutor` holds for the call of analysis and hint (architecture 4.1): its measurement did not measure that. And for the search for the first error with the key there are data, and they did not show a benefit of the course of writing.

— *Rejected:*
- the image in reading, and into analysis the log without what was erased, as the former recommendation of П-21. The log without frames against the image alone the measurement counted only without a threshold, and one thing is visible from it: fewer false alarms for the weakest judge. Opus, though, is right by the image alone, and no help is visible for it on these sheets by construction. To let the log go to the provider without a shown benefit is against the rule of П-21, and it would need an amendment to R09 and the lawyer's answer anyway;
- to wait with the answer for the measurement on live handwriting, option (c) of `tutor`: epic E3 would plan the contract with the question open, while the answer of this measurement is already there — "not shown";
- the course of writing into reading for Haiku without thinking: its gain is not significant (p = 0.061), and in form D it is still below Haiku · `low` by the image alone (R27 tutor);
- the conclusion "the course of writing does not help": the measurement does not prove it — the handwriting is synthetic, there is no free notation, and Opus is faultless on these sheets even without the course of writing.

— *Consequence:*
- П-21 is closed (privacy 9); R09, privacy 1 and 4 do not change.
- Epic E3 of RUN.md writes the contract `app` ↔ `api` without fields of the course of writing.
- `tutor` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— privacy 9; RUN.md, table 2, Д33.
