R27 `tutor` also stays — by the author's decision (R27 tutor, amendment 2026-10-28).
- **What was measured** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера свободной записи» and «Выводы E4»; T66 tutor). 40 sheets by code with free notation — a number line, a drawing, a note at the side —, 30 of them test sheets, with 3 repeats. The judges and the criterion are the same as above: form D against form A, p < 0.05.
- **The answer by the criterion is "not shown" for all three judges.** Opus 5.5 · `high` is nearly faultless by the image alone too: correct in 87 answers of 90 in both forms. For Haiku 5.5 · `low` p is 0.094, for Haiku without thinking 0.123. There is no false "correct" in any answer.
- **Without a threshold** the log of parts helps a weak judge to find the first error in a drawing. On the 6 sheets where it is in a drawing, Haiku · `low` is right in 10 answers of 18 by the image alone and in 15 with the log, and Haiku without thinking in 1 and in 13. In text and in a note at the side there is nothing of the kind. On the author's three sheets, live writing with a mouse, the measurement went without a threshold (T77 tutor).
- **When to return** — as before, with the measurement on the live handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16). If the course of writing returns into analysis, then analysis will go with it, and the hint without it (R11 tutor). That is already two calls instead of one call of analysis and hint (architecture 4.1), and it is to be decided together with the calls of reading and analysis (R67).

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. The benefit is visible without a threshold, for a weak model and only on drawings, while Opus is right even without the course of writing.

*Rejected:*
- the log of parts only for a weak judge and only on drawings — a rule for one model and one kind of notation by data without a threshold;
- to return the course of writing into analysis now: the benefit by the criterion is not shown.

*Consequence:* `tutor` closes В50 with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

## The place on the canvas

**R53. A place on the canvas in the observation and in the contract `app` ↔ `api` is fractions 0–1000 of the crop that the device sent: `[ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]`, integers. Into fractions the adapter of `tutor` converts from the units of its provider, into units of the sheet `canvas` does, and `sheet_box` does not leave the device.** Т-32 is closed. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В31 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), by the first option of Т-32.
- **The Anthropic adapter** takes pixels from the model and converts them into fractions itself. All read 2026-10-26:
  - the model names a place in pixels of the image it processed: "The coordinates Claude returns are pixel positions in the image Claude processes: your image after Claude resizes it to fit the model's native resolution". And in the same place: "Always ask for pixel coordinates and normalize in your own code if you need to" ([Coordinates and bounding boxes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision-coordinates));
  - the adapter allows no resizing at the provider. It sends the image with `"oversized_image": "error"` (architecture 3.1 tutor), and "No image that sets "error" reaches the model resized" (ibid.). An image larger than the model's limit it scales down itself and knows its size;
  - it divides by the size of the image it sent, not by the size with padding. The model pads every image to a multiple of 28 px on the right and at the bottom, and "Always normalize or rescale by the resized dimensions, not the padded dimensions" (ibid.). A box that went out onto the padding it first clamps to the image: "Clamp returned coordinates to the resized dimensions before rescaling" (ibid.).

  OpenAI has no box format, and Google's models, whose place is fractions 0–1000, are closed (Т-32; R47).
- **The data of the measurement of `tutor`** (R27 tutor; architecture 3.1 tutor, «Итог замера»). A sheet is the whole image 1000 × 600, without a crop, and the model does not scale it down. In the table of sizes, the row "1000x1000 px (1 megapixel)" has "Not resized" at both resolution levels ([Vision](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision), read 2026-10-26). For 1000 × 600 both the side and the number of visual tokens, 792, are below both limits. On sheets with an error, the box of the first error in pixels hit its line:
  - for Opus 5.5 · `high` — in 114 answers of 114;
  - for Haiku 5.5 · `low` — in 100;
  - for Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking — in 95.

  As a hit the measurement counted the line that has the most visible pixels in the box with a margin of 8 px: this is precision to the line, not finer.
- **The rest is as in the recommendation of Т-32.** Into the same fractions are converted:
  - the tutor's marks in the answer of `api` — a group label, an answer slot or a box;
  - the group boxes, if Т-31 accepts them;
  - the zone of an answer slot, if it has to be shown to reading: `canvas` converts the zone, and the crop stays one.

  A box's validity — integers 0–1000 and min < max — the adapter checks, and an invalid box has no place. How the observation chooses a place — a slot, a label or a box — Т-32 left to the question В12 `tutor`, and that one is recorded as Т-32: now this is decided by epic E3, where the observation is written (R11).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26: the first option of Т-32, as Т-32 and `tutor` in В31 recommended it, and `canvas` decided so for itself as early as 2026-10-21 (R06 canvas). The observation depends neither on the canvas kind nor on the provider. Only the adapter sees the image's resizing, and only it can recompute a place, while the server does not need the sheet's geometry (R09). The measurement showed that Claude's pixels on an image not resized fall into the right line, and converting them into fractions is the adapter's arithmetic, as Anthropic advises.

— *Rejected:*
- units of the sheet: the adapter would need `sheet_box` from the device, and the sheet's geometry would go to the server;
- fractions, with `api` converting into units of the sheet by `sheet_box` from `app`: the same, and `api` would know the canvas's geometry;
- fractions that the model itself gives: "Claude does not work well when you ask for normalized coordinates" (Coordinates and bounding boxes, ibid.).

— *Consequence:*
- Т-32 is closed (repositories 8). The field of the place in the observation and in the contract is written by epic E3 of RUN.md (R11), and the types for `canvas` come out by the path of T35 (R36).
- architecture 3.2 and 3.6 name the place by R53.
- `tutor` and `canvas` get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— repositories 8; architecture 3.2, 3.6; RUN.md, table 2, Д33.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* **in the workbook, what goes to the check is the crop of each filled box, and the place in the observation and in the contract `app` ↔ `api` is the answer slot by place, `{ item, slot }` (R34 and R38 canvas).** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В45 (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 6b87374), its first option. "The crop stays one" above is about the sheet's zones.
- **A box's crop** goes by the crop rule R25 canvas, by the box's strokes, at the digit height of the module manifest (R51), ink only: without the box's frame and the line's text. Which stroke is in which box the box rule decides (RUN.md, epic E3). The workbook's request carries a list of "item, box, crop".

This is the answer to "if T80 of `tutor` shows" of the amendment above.

The rule was written down before the run: a false "correct" that exists only with the caption means that the item's text does not go into reading.

## The tutor's words

**R54. The tutor's words go to the device whole: `api` gives them when the whole text has passed the leak check, and otherwise the fallback text. Nobody gives them out as a stream; a stream is only for the reading call, whose answer a program reads.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В23 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **Why not a stream.** The leak check looks in the model's text for the key and the leak phrases that the author gave, and a text that did not pass it the fallback text replaces (concepts 10). It runs before any text of the tutor goes to the device (architecture 3.5). A hint that is shown in parts cannot be checked whole before it is shown: the beginning, already shown to the learner, cannot be replaced with the fallback text if the leak is further on.
- **What we pay.** A stream would show the first words earlier. On the review board, where the answer goes as a stream, the first token of Opus 5.5 · `high` came after 1.6 s of 2.5 s (architecture 2.6 tutor, series T45). The learner will see the tutor's words when the model has finished writing them whole.
- **Where the stream stays.** The reading call may stream: its answer a program reads — `module-kit` gives the verdict by the observation (architecture 4.1) —, and the learner sees the verdict, not the model's text. Whether to give the verdict by lines while they arrive — the early verdict, В24 `tutor` — R54 does not decide.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 by the recommendation of `tutor` in В23. The leak check is a safeguard, not a proof (concepts 10), but there is no other between the model's text and the learner, and what is shown before it bypasses it.

— *Rejected:*
- a stream after the check of the whole text: there is no gain — the first words come at the same time as the whole text;
- a leak check by sentences: the beginning, already shown to the learner, cannot be recalled if the continuation does not pass.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.5 and 3.6. A real-time channel is still not needed (Т-25). `tutor`, `api` and `app` get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— architecture 3.5, 3.6; RUN.md, Д33.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* how the leak check looks for keys and leak phrases in the tutor's text, the [format text](../format/README.md), section 20 says normatively (R57). A key that already stands in the statement or in the text of its own item is not looked for: there the author's leak phrases guard the answer.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **there is no early verdict by lines in format v0: `module-kit` gives the verdict by the observation whole, when the reading has ended. The early verdict waits for a check kind by steps in a new format version.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В24 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), by the recommendation of `tutor`. This is the answer to "R54 does not decide" above.
- Only a program check by lines can judge a line while the next ones arrive. There is no kind "steps" in format v0 (R56), so the stream stays for reading, but the verdict waits for the end of the observation.
- Return with a check kind by steps, if the stream shows that the lines arrive noticeably before the end of the answer.

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. *Rejected:* a verdict by lines as they arrive — for now there is nothing to judge lines by.

*Consequence:* architecture 4.1 does not change. `tutor` closes В24 with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

## The term "solution"

**R55. "Solution" («решение») is the task's solution or the learner's solution, and where the context does not show whose, it is written in full. "Analysis of the course of solution" stays the name of an AI capability, and the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures are the course of writing, not the course of solution.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В25 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its second option.
- **The task's solution** is its course of solution, the field `solution`: it is shown after the correct answer, and before it does not enter the open view (concepts 15; R05). In a module it is from the author, and for a task from paper AI may derive it, and then it is marked so (concepts 9.4). In code and schemas `solution` is only this.
- **The learner's solution** is how the learner solves the task on the canvas: lines, a drawing, a note at the side. It is part of their work, which goes to the check (concepts 9). Reading reads it, and the analysis of the course of solution looks for the first error in it (architecture 3.6).
- **Where to write it in full** — where both meanings occur side by side: "the model sees the key and the task's solution and looks for the first error in the learner's solution". Where it is clear whose solution is meant, just "solution": "showing the solution" (О-7) is always the task's solution, and "the learner's free solution" (product 2) is already named in full.
- **The course of solution** is the steps of a solution, the task's or the learner's, as they are seen in the notation: "analysis of the course of solution" analyses the steps of the learner's solution in the image.
- **The course of writing** is the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures: what the writing history carries beyond the final image (concepts 15). П-21 and the measurement of `tutor` called it the course of solution, and R52 and onward the course of writing.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 by the recommendation of `tutor` in В25: it needs the fewest changes both in `spec` and in the components, and "analysis of the course of solution" stays the capability's name. A term means one thing (RULES.md, The bar), and each meaning now has its own full name. The names are the executor's proposal after review. «Решение автора» ("the author's solution"), as in the option of `tutor`, in this log already means a decision of the project's author — "*Why:* the author's decision …" stands at almost every entry —, while the solution of a task from paper is not always from the author (concepts 9.4). "Course of writing" is the word of R26 tutor: it separates what the writing history carries from the steps of a solution, which "analysis of the course of solution" analyses.

— *Rejected:*
- "solution" only for the task's solution, and for the learner "work": work is wider — it is also a text, a typed answer and a widget's state (privacy 4) —, and the capability "analysis of the course of solution" would have to be renamed in the documents of all the components;
- «решение автора» ("the author's solution") — it already means a decision of the project's author, and the solution of a task from paper may be from AI;
- leave it as it is: one term with two meanings is against RULES.md, The bar.

— *Consequence:* concepts 6, 9.4 and 15, architecture 3.6 and 4.1 and privacy 5.1 name the solution in full where the other meaning is beside it, and R52, П-21 and the records of the measurement of `tutor` say "course of writing". `tutor` corrects its documents with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— concepts 6, 9.4, 15; architecture 3.6, 4.1; privacy 5.1; RUN.md, Д33.

## Slot check

**R56. The check belongs to each answer slot: the field `check` with the check kind and its parameters, closed whole, together with the kind. The kinds of format v0 are `number`, `fraction`, `choice`, `predicate` and `rubric`. How each reads the value and gives the slot's verdict, and how the item's verdict is made up of the slots' verdicts, the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15 says. The verdict vectors are `format/vectors/verdicts/`, and `spec` computes them itself, but for what Starlark gives a predicate.** The author's answers in planning T29 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **The check is at the slot** — at a slot of the sheet and at a box of a workbook line. The kind and the key stand beside what they check, and the kinds in one line may differ. Which kinds suit which binding, the schema says: `sheet` only a rubric, `choice` a tapped choice, `anywhere`, `zone` and `box` a number, a fraction, a choice by hand and a predicate. An item's "own key" in concepts 6 and 15 reads as the keys of its slots.
- **The kinds of v0** are what the three modules of the slice need: numbers and fractions for the workbooks of school maths, numbers and choice for olympiad maths, rubric and choice for short essays (R41). And the predicate: it will enter v1 only if a module of the slice takes it (the amendment to R44).
  - `number` — an integer, a decimal with a point or a simple fraction; the comparison is by value, in rational numbers, exact. `units` are the words after the number that the check discards.
  - `fraction` — a simple fraction. `form`: `any` — any fraction of the same value, `reduced` — only an irreducible one, and a reducible one of the same value is "not yet".
  - `choice` — by tap, from the options of a slot with the binding `choice`, or by hand, and then the options are in the check itself. So the signs <, > and = in a workbook box are checked: what is read not from the options is "unreadable", not "not yet".
  - `predicate` — a Starlark expression of the read integer `value`, no longer than 1000 characters. `True` is "correct", `False` is "not yet"; an error, a result that is not a `bool`, more than 1,000,000 steps in the count of go.starlark.net, or the clock of `module-kit` — "unchecked".
  - `rubric` — the criteria `criteria`, only on the whole sheet; the result is feedback, not a verdict (R04).
- **The key is a string,** `key: "7"`: a plain `0.1` in YAML is a binary fraction, and an exact comparison with it would give a false "not yet".
- **Value and normalization.** The reader gives a slot's value as it is written, and the check kind normalizes it: NFKC, minus signs and dashes into `-`, the slashes of a fraction and of division into `/`, White_Space spaces one at a time.
  - For numbers, `=` at the start and `.!?` at the end are discarded, the units too, and a superscript or subscript digit is "not in notation".
  - For a choice, also a plain lowercase letter, and nothing is discarded.
  - A notation is up to 16 characters.
- **A slot's verdict:** empty — "unreadable" with the reason `blank`; not in a notation — with the reason `notation`; matched — "correct"; otherwise "not yet". **An item's verdict:** all slots correct — "correct"; at least one "not yet" — "not yet"; otherwise "unreadable", and if there is no such either, "unchecked".
- **Closed whole.** The app gets neither the key, nor the options of a choice by hand, nor the predicate, nor the rubric's criteria, nor the kind. What the learner is to know — which signs the box awaits, by which criteria the essay is judged — the author writes in the task statement (the amendment to R51).
- **Assessability is a rule,** `task.assessability`: the primary skill of an item with a key or a predicate is `verdict`, of an item with a rubric `rubric`, and a skill `none` is only supporting (the amendment to R49).
- **The task's rules** are `task.choice-key`, `task.choice-options`, `task.fraction-key`, `task.predicate-expression` and `task.assessability`. `module-kit` checks them, and their vectors the CI of `spec` checks by the schema and the YAML rules, like the vectors of the other rules of a task (R45).
- **The verdict vectors** are `format/vectors/verdicts/<kind>/<case>.yaml` by the schema `verdict-vector.schema.json`: an item with its checks and its readings — the value of each slot with the verdict of the slot and of the item.
  - `format-check` computes the verdicts as a second implementation, as it builds the open view, and the CI of `module-kit` passes the same vectors.
  - The predicate is an exception: `spec` has no Starlark, and it computes only "blank" and "not in notation" (the amendment to R45).
  - The rest of an observation — whether it is legible, whether it is unambiguous, how many final answers — the vectors do not hold: that is the observation's type, epic E3.
- **The predicate's step limit is in the format:** the same expression on the same value makes the same steps on any machine, and the verdict repeats by the stored value (R03). The clock, its figure and concurrent runs are T03 of `module-kit`.
- **What v0 does not have:** text, edit, quantity, order and set, widget state and "steps" — a check of each line of the course of solution. Each will come as a new kind, with a minor version. This answers В10 `tutor`.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 14 and 15.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T29 — eight, all by the plan's recommendations but the first: the author kept the task one, together with the predicate and its limits (RUN.md, T29, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Normalization follows canvas-api,** `docs/spec.md`, commit 0901af0, read 2026-10-27: «Unicode NFKC; юникодные минусы и тире заменяются на `-`; пробелы по краям убираются», «Знак `=` в начале и знаки `.`, `!`, `?` в конце отбрасываются: «= 7» и «7.» — это 7», «Слово единицы в конце отбрасывается», and the whitelist of notations comes before parsing (spec 5.2 canvas-api); the comparison is `big.Rat`, and «`3/6` и `0.5` равны» (spec 5.3 canvas-api). The differences:
  - a decimal and a common fraction are in one kind, `number`, like `number` of canvas-api, and an integer is in it too;
  - a superscript digit is "not in notation": NFKC makes `7²` the number 72 (Node 24.21, ICU 78.3, Unicode 17.0);
  - for a choice, `=` and a period are not dropped: they can be the answer.
- **In doubt, "unreadable", not "not yet"** (R04), as in R38 canvas-api: «`INCORRECT` получает только разборчивый, однозначный ответ правильной формы». So a read value that is not among the options of a choice is "unreadable" too: `7` in a box for a sign is a doubt in the reading, not the learner's error. But an answer slot read confidently and wrong is no longer a doubt, and the item with it is "not yet".
- **A reducible fraction where an irreducible one is needed is "not yet",** as `tutor` plans: «несокращённая дробь там, где нужна сокращённая, — «пока нет»» (RUN.md `tutor`, T79, commit 49f4c6a).
- **The predicate is an expression,** not a program: a short check is visible in the task itself, and it needs neither a line of the layout nor a rule about files. standalone's solver programs — the files `content/examples/solvers/<id>.star` (SPEC 1.5 and 6 standalone, commit 99d8a65) — are needed by the keys of templates, RUN.md, T33. The step limit is as in standalone, `thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps`, but smaller: an expression of one number does not need 25,000,000 steps.
- **The predicate's vectors are a part:** there is no mature Starlark in JavaScript. `starlark-webasm` 1.0.3 is Apache-2.0, about 5 MB of WASM, published 2022-04-11 (the npm registry, read 2026-10-27), and its go.starlark.net is older than the one `module-kit` will take.
- **Without "steps":** no module of the slice takes them, the measurement did not return a verdict by lines (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R43), and canvas-api removed the exact equivalence of steps from the product (R37 canvas-api).

— *Rejected:*
- the predicate and Starlark as a separate task after T03 `module-kit`, and the verdict vectors as one more: the author kept one task;
- the check on the item, with keys by the place of the answer slots: there would be one kind in a line, and the number of keys would need one more rule;
- a kind "text" with options and normalization for signs and words by hand — its defaults would freeze from v1, and for signs a choice by hand is enough; a separate kind "sign"; a workbook page without signs;
- open criteria of a rubric: then the kind by which the schema branches would be open too;
- assessability without a rule or only for items with a key;
- vectors only by the schema, without a second implementation; `starlark-webasm` in `tools/`;
- the predicate as a file `predicates/<id>.star` in the module layout;
- the key as a YAML number; a decimal comma and digit group separators in v0;
- "steps" in v0.

— *Consequence:*
- the [format text](../format/README.md) — section 15 and edits of sections 2, 3, 6, 9 and 14; `task.schema.json` — the field `check`; the schema of vectors `verdict-vector.schema.json`; examples of tasks with keys — three new valid and 15 invalid; vectors of rules, of the open view and of verdicts; `format-check` — `verdicts.mjs`.
- concepts 4, 6, 9.1–9.3, 11 and 15; architecture 3.5–3.7; repositories 3, 5, 7 and Т-18; the README and CLAUDE.md of `spec`.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* trap values (R57). The checks `number`, `fraction` and `choice` have `trap_values`: a trap value is compared like the key, with the same normalization, and at "not yet" it names the trap. The verdict vectors name it, and `format-check` computes it; the rule `task.trap-values` is among the rules of the answer slot that `spec` checks at a vector's item. The short key in the leak check, which T29 handed to T30, is decided: a key that already stands in the text of its own item is not searched for. Step 1 of the normalization of numbers now also replaces a fraction like `½` that a number adjoins. Otherwise NFKC would make `1½` the notation `11⁄2`, eleven halves, and a mixed number would get "not yet" rather than "unreadable" (R04). The error was found by the review in the planning of T30, in the code of `format-check` on Node 24.21.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* placeholders in the key (R60). In the key and the trap value of `number` and `fraction` of a template, a placeholder stands in the place of the integer, the numerator or the denominator, and outside a template a placeholder in them breaks `task.placeholders`. Solver programs for the keys of templates are no longer T33 but T43: the key of a template in format v0 is computed by an expression. Template expressions are a narrow subset of the same Starlark as the predicate's, but without a step limit of their own: they have no more steps than characters.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the template's solver (R61). A Starlark program in the format is only a template's solver, the field `template.solver`, and its limit is in the format too: 100,000,000 steps in the count of go.starlark.net for all instances of the template together. The check's predicate stays an expression no longer than 1000 characters.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the slot checks lie in the canonical view — the server part —, and the open view does not have them (R62). — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **how a reader gives a fraction written vertically and a mirrored digit: the fraction in a line, "numerator/denominator", and the mirrored digit as the digit itself.** The author's answers to the `tutor` rows «в реестр spec» В46 and В48 (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), their first options, by the recommendations of `tutor`. Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, "The value read".
- **A vertical fraction.** The notation of a fraction is only in a line, `3/4`, and a two-storey fraction in an item line will come to the format later (R51). But in a box of the workbook the learner writes a fraction vertically too. It is the same fraction, and the notation in a line is the only one the kind `fraction` takes. Without the rule one reader would write `3/4`, another "3 over 4", and the verdict would depend on the reader.
  - The measurement T80 of `tutor` (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера тетради»): with such a rule of the prompt, Opus 5.5 · `high` gets 27 readings out of 33 correct for vertical fractions and 29 out of 33 for fractions in a line. Haiku 5.5 · `low` has three times more extra "unreadable" for vertical ones — 16 out of 99 against 5 out of 99.
- **A mirrored digit.** A child who wrote 5 mirrored has solved correctly, and "not yet" for them is a false alarm. So the truth of a mirrored digit is the digit itself. "Unreadable" on it is an acceptable outcome, and the false alarm is in the target of the first slice (product 10). The rule does not concern letters: a mirrored b is a d.
  - The measurement T80 on the workbook's synthetic data, without a caption, at 32 px: mirrored boxes were read correctly in 0 out of 15 by Opus, in 8 out of 45 by Haiku · `low` and in 5 out of 45 by Haiku without thinking. False alarms on them — 8 out of 15, 9 out of 45 and 14 out of 45: the models read a mirrored 5 as 2, and a 2 as 5. On boxes without peculiarities nobody has false alarms.
  - The workbook's eval set measures mirrored digits as a separate row.
- **The module format version** does not change: the rule is about the reader, not the module, and with the same read value the verdict is the same ([format text](../format/README.md), section 2).

*Why:* the recommendations of `tutor`. The rule about letters is the executor's proposal.

*Rejected:*
- a vertical fraction as "unreadable" until the format takes a two-storey fraction, or deciding it together with that: a correct fraction would wait for a format version;
- a mirrored digit as "unreadable", and the learner rewrites it: a correct solution would get a request to rewrite;
- not measuring mirrored digits.

*Consequence:* product 10. `tutor` closes В46 and В48 by its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

## Traps, techniques, solving steps and hints

**R57. The trap and technique catalogs and the solving steps are files at the root of the module: `traps.yaml`, `techniques.yaml` and `solving-steps.yaml`. A trap by a wrong value is in the slot check, and the traps that AI may suppose are named by the task. The task carries the "givens and unknown", the techniques, the solution, the leak phrases, and its item the simpler case. The fallback texts of the ladder are the trap text, the trap advice and the module's rung template from the manifest. How the leak check searches is said normatively by the [format text](../format/README.md), section 20, and its vectors are `format/vectors/leaks/`, and `spec` computes them itself.** The author's answers in the planning of T30 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **The catalogs are files at the root,** dictionaries by local ID, like the skills in the skill graph (R46):
  - the trap catalog `traps.yaml` — the description, the skills and the advice `trap_advice` of each trap;
  - the technique catalog `techniques.yaml` — the name and the description of each technique;
  - the solving steps `solving-steps.yaml` — the steps in order.

  Each of them is optional. A published trap ID names no other trap (the amendment to R46).
- **A trap by a wrong value is in the slot check,** `trap_values`: the value, the trap and, optionally, the trap text — what the learner will read at this error.
  - The value is compared by the check like the key, with the same normalization, and names the trap only when the verdict is "not yet".
  - Such traps exist for `number`, `fraction` and `choice`: a predicate has no key, and a rubric has no verdict.
  - The rule `task.trap-values`: a trap value gets "not yet", for a choice it is an option as written, and no two values of one check are equal by its comparison.
  - The verdict vectors name the matched trap, and `format-check` computes it (the amendment to R56).
- **The traps that AI supposes** by the kind of error in the work are the task's field `traps`; their provenance is "derived by AI" (concepts 9.4). Traps of both kinds come only from the catalog (`task.known-traps`).
- **The trap advice is `trap_advice`,** as the term of concepts 15 and the example of R45: what to suggest to an adult or the learner at this error. Progress shows it, and it is also the fallback text when a trap value has no text of its own. The skills of a trap are the IDs of the module's skills (`traps.known-skills`; R49).
- **The fields of a task** (the amendment to R51):
  - `givens` and `unknown` — the "givens and unknown", open;
  - `techniques` — techniques from the catalog (`task.known-techniques`), closed;
  - `solution` — texts and pictures, as in the task statement, closed. The schema requires it of a task that has an item with a verdict: a format rule is only what the schema does not express;
  - `leak_phrases` — leak phrases, closed;
  - for an item, `simpler_case`, the simpler case, closed.
- **Open** is what the learner sees before the answer and what does not suggest the method: the solving steps with exit conditions, the "givens and unknown" and the technique catalog, like the skills in the skill map. **Closed** are the task's techniques — their name suggests the method of solution, like the names of a task's skills (R51) — and also the trap catalog, the traps and texts of the task, the simpler case, the leak phrases and the solution. `api` gives a task's technique at the step that gives it, or at the learner's request, and records this.
- **A solving step** is a name `title`, `gives` — what the step gives, `givens` or `techniques`, — and an exit condition `exit_condition`: `givens_ticked`, `answer_slots_filled` or `none`. A step with `givens_ticked` gives `givens`, and the widget's state will come with stage 4.
- **Fallback texts** (concepts 10):
  - at rungs 1–2 — the text of the trap value, without it the advice of its trap, and without that the rung template;
  - at the third rung — the item's simpler case, and without it the same as at the second.

  The rung templates belong to the module: two different texts `rung_templates` in the manifest, in the explanation language. A module with an item with a verdict cannot do without them (`manifest.rung-templates`).
- **О-21 as far as the format goes:** before the first submission a request gives the "givens and unknown" and the task's technique — without AI and without reading the work. There is no sketch "how to start" in v0: it will come as a minor version when `canvas` learns to draw it. The rest of О-21 — what a request gives after a wrong answer and "explain differently" — is decided by the detailing of `api`, and О-21 stays open.
- **The leak check** — normatively, the [format text](../format/README.md), section 20:
  - searched for are the keys `number`, `fraction` and `choice` of all items of the task and all its leak phrases;
  - a key that itself is found in the text of the task statement and in the `alt` of its pictures, in the text and line of its own item and in the options of its answer slots `choice` is not searched for: the leak phrases hold it. So the key of a tapped choice is never searched for. So the short key that T29 handed to T30 is decided (the amendment to R56);
  - the normal form is step 1 of the normalization of numbers and the normalization of a choice ([format text](../format/README.md), section 15); the letters of a word are the categories L, M and N;
  - a string is found whole, with a boundary where its edge is a letter of a word; a number by value and by absolute value;
  - numbers in words and notations that the check does not read as a number are caught only by leak phrases;
  - the rule `task.no-leaks` checks the author's texts that the learner sees before solving.
- **Leak vectors** — `format/vectors/leaks/<case>.yaml` by the schema `leak-vector.schema.json`, the fourth schema without a part. `format-check` computes them with a second implementation, `leaks.mjs`, and CI of `module-kit` passes the same vectors (the amendment to R45).
- **Step 1 of normalization** also replaces a fraction like `½` that a number adjoins: otherwise NFKC makes `1½` the notation `11⁄2`, and the learner would get a false "not yet" (the amendment to R56).

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10, 11 and 14–20.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T30 — eight, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T30, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Traps follow standalone:** "The catalog stays closed for the same reason the topic catalog does: `trap_hit` is what makes a wrong answer a diagnosis, and free-form trap names cannot be counted" and "Each trap carries its advice" (SPEC 1.3 standalone, commit 99d8a65, read 2026-10-27). The differences: a task's trap is found by the value, not by the letter of an option, and a trap has skills, as concepts 7 requires.
- **A trap by value and the fallback texts follow canvas-api** (commit 0901af0, read 2026-10-27): the task has `traps: {"6": "…"}`, and «Ответ совпадает с ловушкой по тем же правилам» (spec 8.6 and 5.3 canvas-api); «на ступенях 1–2 — текст ловушки, который автор задачи написал для этого неверного ответа, а если такого нет — шаблон ступени; на ступени 3 — случай попроще от автора задачи» (R24 canvas-api). The difference is that the rung template belongs to the module, not the service: a module has one explanation language (R46), and the platform does not need to translate templates into the language of each module.
- **A key from the text of its own item is not searched for** — this is a departure from R24 canvas-api, where «Ключ запрещён всегда — даже если это слово есть в самом условии». Because of this rule R40 canvas-api removed a task in which the leak check «пришлось бы запрещать «no», «never», «cannot»», and `tutor` keeps open how not to take for a leak «законную цифру ключа — «2 ноги»» (RUN.md `tutor`, T75, commit 8451728). standalone did not count as giving away what is said in the task statement either (SPEC 5.4 standalone).
- **Numbers in words are leak phrases,** not tables of the platform. canvas-api translated "seven" into 7, but such a table is needed for each language, and modules are written in any. In the measurement bank of `tutor` the leak phrases are «сверх самого ключа» (architecture 3.1 tutor, commit 8451728).
- **What is open follows the prototype:** "Understand: tap what we know and what we need to find", "Plan: a technique card" ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). standalone's hint "arrives with the task and is revealed locally, and the fact that it was opened travels with the answer" (SPEC 8.3 standalone). A technique, though, is closed, like a task's skills (R51), and `api` gives it.
- **The solution is by the schema:** a format rule is what the schema does not express ([format text](../format/README.md), section 7; concepts 15), and "has an item with a verdict" the schema expresses by open fields.
- **`gives` of a step:** physics has no step "plan" (concepts 7), so the step itself says what it gives.

— *Rejected:*
- T30 as two or three tasks: the author kept one;
- catalogs as folders, a file per trap, and one file of all catalogs;
- a trap beside the slot check and a trap in the task by the places of the item and the answer slot;
- a key that is always searched for, as in R24 canvas-api, and a length threshold below which a key is not searched for;
- open techniques of a task and closed "givens and unknown";
- the rung template at the platform, and a template at the module or the platform;
- the sketch "how to start" in v0, and also nothing before the first submission;
- rules of the leak check only as data, and leak vectors at `module-kit`;
- the solution as a format rule, not by the schema;
- `advice` instead of `trap_advice`; the exit condition `givens_marked`: «пометка — mark» is already taken (Д36).

- the schemas `traps`, `techniques`, `solving-steps` and `leak-vector`, edits of the schemas of the task, the manifest and the verdict vectors;
- examples of the three catalogs for the three modules of the slice and the module `with-hints`; solutions for the tasks with a verdict and rung templates in the manifests; vectors of rules, of the open view, of verdicts and of leaks;
- `format-check` — `leaks.mjs`;
- concepts 3, 6, 7, 9.1, 10 and 15; architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7; repositories 4, 5, 7; product 13, О-21;

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the leak check reaches lessons too (R58). The rule `lesson.no-leaks` searches for the keys and leak phrases of each task of a lesson in all its texts — in the title, in the explanations, in the task statement and demo of worked examples, and after the task too: the open view of a lesson goes to the device whole (R05). `task.no-leaks` still searches the module's texts outside lessons. No rule searches for a task in the texts of other lessons and in the texts of another task of the same lesson: a worked example SHOULD NOT solve a task of the module, and a lesson SHOULD NOT name two tasks where the texts of one give the answer of the other ([format text](../format/README.md), sections 20 and 21).

So the rung template, the trap advice and a technique hold no numbers that the key of an instance may be. The trap values, simpler cases, solution and leak phrases of a template carry placeholders and are checked on the instances.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **the leak check stays strict. The false leaks that the measurement T76 of `tutor` found are handled by the prompt and the fallback text, not by exceptions in the check.** The author's answer to the `tutor` row «в реестр spec» В44 (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its second option, by the recommendation of `tutor`.
- **What the measurement found** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера подсказок»; R39 tutor). On 34 synthetic sheets with an error, three configurations gave 612 hints, and the leak check ([format text](../format/README.md), section 20) caught 49:
  - 30 repeat the learner's own correct line — "3x = 12", "x − 3 = 5": the leak phrases of the measurement banks are solving steps, and those are what the learner writes. All are Haiku's;
  - 13 carry a number of the key not as the answer, most often in the similar case of rung 3: "□ + 2 = 5" with the key 2. Here belong all 6 caught at Opus 5.5 · `high`;
  - 4 name or confirm the answer — all Haiku's;
  - 2 are a phrase of the bank in the reasoning of rung 3, where the bank expected it.

  The rule "a key that already stands in the text of its own item is not searched for" does not cover the first two kinds. With Opus, 6 hints out of 204, about 3 %, got the fallback text because of a leak: its prompt tells it to name the learner's notation in words and not to copy its numbers (R39 tutor, the 2026-10-28 amendment).

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. The check is a safeguard (concepts 10). If it did not search for the key and phrases that the reading found in the learner's notation, it would depend on the AI's reading.

*Rejected:*
- not searching for the key and phrases that the reading observation found in the learner's notation;
- the similar case of rung 3 only from the module, `simpler_case`, not from AI. Return to this if modules give simpler cases.

*Consequence:* `tutor` closes В44 by its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **О-21 is decided — R82.** The "givens and unknown" and the task's technique a request gives before the first wrong answer, not only before the first submission: a submission that had only "unreadable" or "unchecked" gives no rung (R04). A rung, its words and the fallback text speak of the rung's answer slot — the first answer slot "not yet" in order in the submission that gave the rung: items by place, answer slots by order in the item. This also decides which answer slot the fallback text speaks of when there are several wrong ones in a submission (architecture 3.5). — R82; concepts 10; the [format text](../format/README.md), section 19.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **about a number in the text of the whole module — the rung template `rung_templates`, the trap advice `trap_advice`, the name and description of a technique — `module-kit` warns but does not refuse, and the trap advice of the format example `olympiad-math` holds no numbers.** The author's answer to the `modules` rows «в реестр spec» В25 and В26 (RUN.md `modules`, branch `e3`, commit ac445f4), by the recommendations of `modules`. The warning finds a number before a task or a template instance with such a key comes.
- **The warning** is about each number of the text, as the leak check reads it ([format text](../format/README.md), section 20, "What is read as a number"). It is not a rule, like the one about a picture with transparent points (the second 2026-11-01 amendment to R51): it has neither an ID nor vectors, it does not reject a module, and it does not require a format version (R44). `module-kit` writes it in a task of its own.

## Lessons

**R58. A lesson is a file `lessons/<id>.yaml`: the module's skills it teaches, and segments in the author's order — explanations, worked examples and the module's tasks by ID. The demo is parts of a worked example on the handwriting sheet. The order of lessons is set by the skill graph, and О-19 is decided: there is no separate field of order.**
- **The lesson's skills** are `skills`, the module's skills by local ID (`lesson.known-skills`). They are closed, like a task's skills (R51): the app needs only the lesson's title, and the engine reads the skills. Each task of the lesson trains at least one of them as primary — its item's skill or, without one, the task's skill (`lesson.task-skills`).
- **The lesson's segments** are `segments`, in order and without repeats. A segment is an object with exactly one field:
  - `explanation` — an explanation, paragraphs and pictures, like the parts of a task statement;
  - `worked_example` — a worked example;
  - `task` — a task of the module by its ID (`lesson.known-tasks`). The next segment comes when the task has ended.

  There is no special check segment at the end: the check is the last tasks of the lesson, and the format does not mark them.
- **A worked example** is not a task: no answer slots, no key, and it does not serve as evidence.
  - It has a task statement, a handwriting sheet and `demo` — the demo: parts of the example's solution, which the learner opens one at a time and can hide all at once. A part is a paragraph, a picture beside the sheet or a picture on a sheet area.
  - The area `area` is a rectangle of the sheet in its units, like a zone, and it lies on the sheet (`lesson.areas`). A picture on an area stands on the layer of the demo, at the size of the area (concepts 8).
  - A worked example has no workbook in v0. The learner does not write on the example's sheet: there is no work of the learner there.
  - The example is open: R05 guards the key and the solution of a task, and an example is not a task. So its parts are `demo`, not `solution`: a task's solution is never opened ([format text](../format/README.md), section 6).
- **The order of lessons follows the skill graph** (О-19).
  - Lesson A comes after lesson B when a skill of A needs, through the module's prerequisites, a skill of B that is not among the skills of A. Anchor skills give no order.
  - A graph without cycles does not guarantee an order without a cycle: a lesson [a, c] and a lesson [b], where b requires a and c requires b, each come after the other. Hence the rule `lesson.order`.
  - Where the graph gives no order — two lessons of one skill, skills without a link — the engine's rule chooses.
  - For a sequential module the graph is a chain, and the app infers the mark "sequential" from the graph.
- **Adaptation.** The segments go in the author's order, and the engine does not reorder them.
  - In a lesson whose skills are not all with a verdict, the engine adds nothing and skips nothing: the lesson goes in the author's order, without adaptation (concepts 4, 5). So "the skills of essays with a rubric go in the author's order" of the record of T22 at table 1 of RUN.md: in the order of the graph and of the lesson.
  - Whether the engine adds consolidation to a lesson whose skills are all with a verdict, and whether it ends it early, is decided by the detailing of `engine`.
- **Age** is the lesson's `age_categories`, as for a task, closed. A lesson is given only to a learner whom both the lesson and each of its tasks suit. Otherwise a task only for adults (П-20) would reach a child in a lesson where nothing is skipped. The rule `lesson.age-categories`: the lesson's categories are from the manifest, and at least one category suits both the lesson and each of its tasks: a lesson that no learner will get is an error.
- **Open** are `id`, `title` and the segments with all their fields: the app runs the lesson. **Closed** are the skills and the age categories.
- **The leak check in a lesson** is the rule `lesson.no-leaks`: neither the lesson's title, nor its explanations, nor the task statement and demo of its examples contain the keys and leak phrases of its tasks ([format text](../format/README.md), section 20). All texts are searched, after the task too: the open view of a lesson goes to the device whole, and the key does not go there before solving (R05). So the author decided by a finding of the review, instead of searching only before the task's segment. `format-check` computes the rule itself, like `task.no-leaks` (the amendments to R45 and R57).
- **The lesson's pictures** are files of the module (`lesson.known-pictures`).
- **Common definitions.** The parts of a task statement, the canvas and the rectangle of a sheet moved to `common.schema.json`, so that the lesson does not refer to the task's schema (the amendment to R51).

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 21, and edits of sections 6, 9, 10, 12, 14 and 20.

- **The order through the graph** is the recommendation of О-19 (product 13): "A sequential module's graph is a chain, and the engine goes along it as along any graph", and "the next lesson is still chosen by the engine" (R03).
  - In the prototype the mark *Sequential* cannot move the package: "Next in a sequential module" is only a line (`draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`, commit 4846d00, read 2026-10-27).

## The generator of randomness

**R59. The platform's generator is PCG, as in Go's `math/rand/v2`, and the stream of a place of randomness is derived as in standalone's simulator: FNV-1a 64 of the seed and the place's names, and the seed itself. Over the stream five Go functions are normative. The text is the [format text](../format/README.md), section 22, and the vectors are `format/vectors/random/`, and `spec` computes them itself. Т-18 is closed.**
- **The generator** is PCG with 128 bits of state, exactly the `PCG` of Go's package `math/rand/v2`:
  - the state is two words, the high and the low, taken from the words of the seed as they are;
  - the step is `state · M + C mod 2^128`, with Go's constants;
  - the output is DXSM after the step.

  This is not numpy's PCG64DXSM and not a cryptographically secure generator. The algorithm is set by the format itself, not by a library.
- **A place of randomness** is a seed, an unsigned 64-bit integer, and a non-empty list of names. A name is a non-empty string without "|", and names are compared as written.
  - The stream of a place is a generator with the words: FNV-1a 64 (RFC 9923) of the UTF-8 text "the seed in decimal digits, and then '|' and the name, for each name" and the seed itself.
  - A new place is new names, and it does not shift the numbers of the earlier places. `seeded` of standalone's simulator is a place of the main seed with the names "experiment, unit, assignment".
  - For reference: the places of one seed share the low word of the state, and FNV-1a is not resistant to collisions. For the places of a module and of a run this does not matter.
- **The functions**, as Go's methods, and how many integers each takes: an integer (`Uint64`), a number below a bound (`Uint64N`: a power of two by a mask, otherwise Lemire's method with rejection), a number in a range (`a + Int64N(c − a + 1)`), a fraction of 53 bits (`Float64`) and the Fisher–Yates permutation (`Perm` and `Shuffle`). The format has no normal and no exponential distributions.
- **The platform's seeds:**
  - `api` takes the seed of an attempt from a cryptographically secure source and keeps it with the attempt. Neither it nor the state of its places goes to the device: the state of a place shows its seed;
  - the places of a module are places of the seed of its attempt, and the first name says whose place it is: `template` — a task template's, the other names are decided by T33;
  - a widget has its own seed, and how it gets it is decided by the widget protocol (Т-24);
  - `engine`, if it needs randomness, and `sim` have their own seeds, of the choice and of the run, and their own names.
- **The vectors** are `format/vectors/random/<case>.yaml` by the schema `random-vector.schema.json`: the start of the stream — the words and, if the stream is a place, its seed and names — and the calls of the functions in order, each with its value. `format-check` derives each state and computes each value with a second implementation, `random.mjs`. And `random.mjs` repeats the golden outputs of Go and RFC 9923 in its tests.
- **Versions** are as the amendment to R44 says: the generator has no version of its own.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 22, and edits of sections 1, 2, 3 and 9.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T32 — five, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T32, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Not waiting for T02 `module-kit` and T03 `engine`:** neither is started, nor are the tasks before them (`module-kit`, commit 1a54028; `engine`, commit 08bc48a; read 2026-10-27). Т-18 is a question of the register of `spec`, and T33 and T38 would wait together with T32.
- **PCG from Go** is the generator that standalone's simulator and `tutor` already take. Go promises the streams not by the package's documentation but thus:
  - the blog post "Evolving the Go Standard Library with math/rand/v2" (go.dev/blog/randv2, 2024-05-01): "Go 1 compatibility included the specific random outputs for a given seed", and "The concrete rand.Rand API is now locked in to that value stream";
  - and `regress_test.go`: "Do NOT make changes to the golden outputs" (Go, commit b98d22c1, read 2026-10-27).

  So the format sets the algorithm itself, and the vectors will catch a divergence. A port on BigInt repeated Go's golden outputs exactly.
- **The derivation as in the simulator** — R27 required taking the simulator's scheme into account, and with it `sim` will repeat its streams. The simulator keeps the same promise: "a generator added leaves every child of the others as they were" (docs/learners.md standalone, commit 4dece74). FNV-1a 64 is RFC 9923, February 2026 (read 2026-10-27). There is nowhere to take a synchronous SHA-256 in the browser from: `crypto.subtle.digest` returns a Promise (W3C Web Cryptography Level 2, draft 2025-04-22, read 2026-10-27).
- **Go's functions, without the normal and the exponential distributions:** otherwise two consumers would make a range differently. And `Math.exp` and `Math.log` in JS give implementation-approximated values (ECMA-262, draft 2026-10-23, read 2026-10-27), and Go on arm64 fuses a multiplication with an addition: "On arm64 the last digits may differ, since Go fuses a multiplication and an addition there" (docs/learners.md standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-27).
- **The seed of an attempt does not go to the device:** the state of a place contains the seed itself, and the generator is not cryptographically secure. The seed carries nothing about the learner, so this does not change privacy.

— *Rejected:*
- waiting for the recommendations of T02 `module-kit` and T03 `engine`;
- SplitMix64 — it does not repeat the simulator's numbers — and ChaCha8, complex in JS;
- a derivation where the second word is SplitMix64 of the first;
- only a stream of integers, without functions over it;
- a document and a version of its own for the generator; vectors that only `module-kit` computes;
- Go in the container of `spec` for the sake of the vectors: Go's golden outputs in the tests of `random.mjs` and CI of `module-kit` check the same without it;
- the vector fields `n`, `pcg` and `uint64`: `n` is rejected by the rule `yaml.plain-strings`, and the others are not words.

— *Consequence:*

- the schema `random-vector` and 12 vectors in `format/vectors/random/`;
- `format-check` — `random.mjs`;

## Task templates

**R60. A module's tasks are a pool and templates with parameters, and О-12 is decided. A template is a task with the field `template`: parameters with domains, derived numbers and a constraint, and the expressions are a narrow subset of Starlark. The key of each instance is known already at the module's check: `module-kit` enumerates all combinations, no more than 10,000, and checks each instance by all the rules of a task, and an attempt gets an instance by its seed. The text is the [format text](../format/README.md), section 23, and the vectors are `format/vectors/templates/`, and `spec` computes them itself.** The author's answers in the planning of T33 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **О-12:** a published pool and templates with parameters. Tasks with the help of AI only in the preparation of a module, and the author checks them; there is no generation on the fly.
- **A template** is a task of R51 in `tasks/<id>.yaml` with the field `template`, closed whole:
  - `parameters` — a name and a domain, integers from `from` to `to`;
  - `derived` — derived numbers, each an expression of the parameters;
  - `constraint` — a constraint, a boolean expression of the parameters and derived numbers.

  A name is lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, no longer than 14 characters, and not a keyword or a reserved word of Starlark. A lesson names a template as a task, and the learner model and the engine see one task.
- **Expressions** are a narrow subset of Starlark: integers and names, `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, `%`, comparisons without chains, `and`, `or` and `not`. Types are checked: arithmetic and comparisons are of integers, logic of `bool`. The meaning is Starlark's: integers without a bound, division rounding down, an error at division by zero, and `and` and `or` evaluate the right operand only when the left does not decide. An expression is up to 1000 characters, without a step limit.
- **Instances:** combinations in counter order — names by code units, the first changes slowest of all —, and on each first the derived numbers, then the constraint. The product of the domains is no more than 10,000, the derived numbers are within ±(2^53−1), and there is at least one instance.
- **An attempt's instance** is the number `below(count)` of the place of its seed with the names `template`, the task's ID and `instance` (R59). The same package and the same seed give the same instance (R03).
- **Placeholders** are `{name}` in each string of the task outside `template`; `{{` and `}}` are a curly brace of the text; substitution goes in one pass. In the key and the trap value of `number` and `fraction` a placeholder stands in the place of the integer, the numerator or the denominator: `"{second}"`, `"{part}/{whole}"`; a decimal fraction has no placeholders.
- **The key in advance:** the rules of a task and `lesson.no-leaks` are applied to each instance at the module's check. At an attempt Starlark is not run, and what the package carries about a template is decided by T34.
- **To the device** goes the open view of the instance — without `template`, without the seed and without numbers that are not in its open fields.
- **Five rules:** `task.template-names`, `task.template-expressions`, `task.placeholders`, `task.template-instances` and `task.instances`. `format-check` checks them itself, with the earlier rules of a task on the instances.
- **The vectors** are `format/vectors/templates/<case>.yaml` by the schema `template-vector.schema.json`: the template, the number of its instances and attempts — the seed, the numbers of the instance and the instance itself. `format-check` computes them with a second implementation, `expressions.mjs` and `templates.mjs`, and its tests compare the expressions with the examples of the Starlark specification.
- **The solver** — a Starlark program that computes the key by enumeration when there is no formula — is separated into RUN.md, T43.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 23, and edits of sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 14, 15, 20, 21 and 22.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T33 — four, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T33, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **A pool and templates, without generation on the fly:** a module is data (R02), and a program gives the verdict (R03). A text that a model writes at an attempt passes no rule of the format. In standalone such a task was checked by a solver written by the same model: "the program is written by the same model that wrote the task, so if the model misread its own wording, the program will confirm the misreading" (SPEC 6.1 standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-27). standalone has no parametric templates. Closest to them is GSM-Symbolic, which the simulator's review retells: "Templates name variables, their domains and conditions that keep answers whole" (`research/literature/generation-verification.md` standalone, the same commit).
- **The key in advance:** T03 `module-kit` is not started (commit 1a54028, read 2026-10-27), and its В1 — where to compute a template's key — waits for the cost of running a solver. All 2^64 seeds cannot be enumerated, but a seed only chooses the number of an instance, and there are no more than 10,000 instances. Then each instance passes all the rules of a task, the leak too, before the first attempt, and an attempt has neither the solver's clock nor its refusal. As T32 decided without T02 `module-kit`, so T33 without T03.
- **A subset of Starlark:** the language is the same as the check's predicate (R56), and `module-kit` computes the expressions with the same go.starlark.net. And a narrow subset `spec` computes itself too, so its template vectors are checked not by the schema alone. The Starlark specification (bazelbuild/starlark, commit c0af0ea03d, read 2026-10-27): "The `//` and `%` operations on integers compute floored division and remainder of floored division", and "Comparison operators, `in`, and `not in` are non-associative, so the parser will not accept `0 <= i < n`". `x or y` there "yields the value of `x` if its truth value is `True`", so `and` and `or` in the subset take only `bool`. The parser of go.starlark.net puts unary minus above `*`, `//` and `%`: "Unary MINUS, unary PLUS, and TILDE have higher precedence so are handled in parsePrimary" (`syntax/parse.go`, google/starlark-go, commit 4f4267fb14, read 2026-10-27).
- **The fields `derived` and `constraint`:** "values" would be confused with the value of an answer slot and with `trap_values`, and "condition" in Russian is «условие», which is both the check kind `predicate` and the task statement.
- **A derived number is only of the parameters:** the order of keys carries no meaning ([format text](../format/README.md), section 4), and a chain of derived numbers would have to set an order of evaluation.
- **One call of `below`:** the choice is uniform over the instances, takes one integer — or slightly more at Lemire's rejection —, and `spec` computes it itself. Parameters one at a time with rejection by the constraint take an unknown number of integers, and a limit of tries would make some seeds a refusal that nobody will check.
- **Splitting the task:** about 3000 lines is more than one check (rule 11 of RUN.md). The cut is clean: in T33 everything that `spec` computes itself, in T43 only the solver's Starlark.

— *Rejected:*
- only a pool in v0; AI generation on the fly, with a solver or without;
- the key at each attempt, with parameters one at a time and rejection; waiting for T03 `module-kit`;
- everything, the numbers of the task statement too, by a solver: then `spec` would check the template vectors only by the schema;
- the format's own language of expressions beside Starlark;
- `abs`, `min`, `max`, a conditional expression and derived numbers of derived numbers in v0: no example asks for them, and each will come as a minor version;
- parameters as a list, not a dictionary: names without repeats are given by `yaml.unique-keys` anyway;
- a template as a part of its own, `templates/<id>.yaml`: a lesson names a task, and the learner model sees one;
- one task together with the solver.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **template expressions run in the dialect of all of the format's Starlark — go.starlark.net `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d` (R88).** The meaning and the subset do not change. "It takes no more steps than it has tokens" of the format text is wrong on both of go.starlark.net's counts: on the new one any expression takes 10 steps on entering the function. The conclusion is the same — an expression calls no functions and holds no loops, and it has no step limit; format 0.3 will say so, RUN.md, T69. — R88.

**R61. A template may carry a solver — the field `solver` with a program in Starlark and the names of its results. `solve` gets the numbers of an instance's open fields and returns a dictionary of results, and the results stand only in the key and in the trap value of `number` and `fraction`, in the solution and in leak phrases. The dialect is that of standalone's solvers, the budget is 100,000,000 steps for all the template's instances together. Only `module-kit` runs the solver, and in template vectors its results are data. Text — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 24.** The author's answers in planning T43 (RUN.md), 2026-10-28.
- **The field** `template.solver`, closed, like all of `template`:
  - `program` — the program, no longer than 8192 characters, most conveniently as a block scalar;
  - `results` — the names of the results, at least one and without repeats. A name is like a parameter's, and a parameter, a derived number and a result never share a name (`task.template-names`).
- **The input of `solve`** is a frozen dictionary of the numbers that the template's open fields show: each parameter and each derived number whose placeholder stands in the statement, the data, the unknown, an item's text, a piece of a line or an option of a slot with the binding `choice`. The names are inserted in the order of code units. The numbers of only closed fields — the key, the trap value, the solution — do not go into the dictionary.
- **The output** is a dictionary with exactly the names of `results`, and each value is an `int` in ±(2^53−1). A result is a number of the instance, like a derived one, and its placeholders are replaced by it.
- **Where the results stand** — only in the key and in the trap value of `number` and `fraction`, in the solution and in leak phrases. Everything the learner sees before solving, `spec` builds without the solver, and a placeholder of a result anywhere else breaks `task.placeholders`.
- **The dialect** is go.starlark.net with the `syntax.FileOptions` options of standalone's solvers: `Set`, `While`, `TopLevelControl` and `GlobalReassign` on, `Recursion` off, `load` forbidden. Only Starlark's own names are built in: none of the modules `math`, `json`, `time`, nor the 13 helpers of standalone's sandbox. `print` writes nothing, and the dialect has no randomness and no clock.
- **The run:** the program is executed once, on one thread, and `solve` is called on each instance in the order of instances (R60), on the same thread. The top level and all the calls together take no more than 100,000,000 steps in go.starlark.net's count. The budget is the template's, not the instance's, and it is in the format, like a predicate's step limit (R56); the clock and concurrent runs are `module-kit`'s.
- **The rule** `task.template-solver`: the solver gives its results on each instance — the program parses and executes in the dialect, `solve` is a function of one parameter, and on each instance, within the budget, without an error, it returns exactly its results as integers within the bounds. Only `module-kit` checks it. The rule's vectors are checked by `spec`'s CI as it checks the vectors of `task.predicate-expression`: by the schema, the YAML rules and by their not breaking the rules it checks itself.
- **What `spec` does:** on an instance without results it checks the task's rules on whatever has no results, and skips the key, the trap value and the leak phrase with a result. A template vector with a solver names `inputs` — the names that `solve` gets — and the results at each attempt: `spec` compares `inputs` with the template's open view and checks the task's rules on the instance with these results, and `module-kit`'s CI runs the solver and compares.
- **Provenance:** a key that the solver computes is "checked by a solver", like a key from a template expression (concepts 9.4).

Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 24, and the edits to sections 1, 2, 9, 14, 15, 20 and 23.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-28 in planning T43 — four, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T43, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Only the numbers of open fields:** the solver solves the task that the learner sees. If it got all the numbers, it could return a closed parameter, and "checked by a solver" would check nothing. standalone's solver, too, gets only what the learner sees — the texts of the options: "`options: {"A": "4", "B": "5", "C": "6", "D": "8", "E": "12"} — the task's own option texts`" (SPEC 6.2 standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-28). The order of the names is fixed, because a Starlark dictionary is iterated in insertion order, and the result must not depend on it.
- **Results only in closed fields:** `spec` does not run Starlark (R56), and it must build an instance's open view itself: its vectors of the open view and of templates are then checked by more than the schema (R60).
- **standalone's dialect:** its solvers already run in it — "`Set: true, While: true, TopLevelControl: true, GlobalReassign: true, Recursion: false, LoadBindsGlobally: false`" (`internal/infra/starlark/dialect.go`, lines 29–36 of standalone, the same commit). On recursion, SPEC 6.4 standalone: "A recursive Starlark function recurses on the **Go** stack, and a stack overflow in Go cannot be recovered". standalone rejects `load` at compilation: `if program.NumLoads() > 0` (`internal/infra/starlark/starlark.go`, line 214). No helpers — because each would become a normative contract that `module-kit` implements and holds with test vectors. The format example needs only `range`, `len` and `fail`, and a helper will come in a minor version when a module asks for it.
- **A budget per template:** 100,000,000 is the recommendation of the plan of T33. In standalone it is 25,000,000 steps per run: "`thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps`; the interpreter tests the counter on every instruction", and the heaviest of the 705 solvers takes 2,413,617 steps (SPEC 6.6 standalone). A budget per instance at 10,000 instances would give up to 250 billion steps for one template when a module is checked. One budget for all the instances bounds the cost of checking a module, and a template with a search for each instance searches only what is open, like standalone's solver templates: "A solver template searches only what the question leaves open, and every program runs under the one step budget" (R72 standalone).
- **The program in the task:** the template stays one file, closed as a whole, like a check's predicate, for which R56 rejected the file `predicates/<id>.star`. The limit of 8192 characters is like standalone's "`MaxSource = 8 * 1024`" (`internal/infra/starlark/starlark.go`, line 36), only in characters: the schema measures a string's length in characters.
- **One thread and the order of instances:** a thread's steps accumulate, and the template's budget is simply the thread's limit. Starlark's global variables are frozen after the top level, so the calls do not affect one another.

— *Rejected:*
- `solve` gets all the numbers of the instance; the numbers as capitalized constants without an argument, like standalone's solver templates (R64 standalone);
- 25,000,000 steps for each instance, without a shared budget; the helpers of standalone's sandbox in format v0;
- results also in trap texts, simpler cases and hints; a result only in the key;
- the program as a file `solvers/<id>.star` in the module layout.
